1	# Notes
2	
3	This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
4	Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.
5	
6	By default there are chores-*.md and todo.md. Chores are general notes
7	about tasks and todo.md contains short term tasks and their status.
8	
9	In the future we I expect we may want to create a "notes"
10	database to better manage the information, TBD.
11	
12	Examples chore file:
13	```
14	# Chores-01.md
15	 
16	General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
17	more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
18	how and why of a particular chore.
19	
20	## Create a binary that lists jj info 
21	
22	This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
23	and using `jj-lib`
24	```
25	
26	## Workflow and conventions
27	
28	Bot-facing workflow, versioning, and code conventions live in
29	[`../CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md). Start there for:
30	
31	- **Versioning during development** — single-step vs multi-step,
32	  `-N` pre-release suffixes, done-marker discipline.
33	- **Code Conventions** — doc comments on every file / fn / method,
34	  `// OK: …` justifications on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
35	  stuck detection.
36	- **Commit-Push-Finalize Flow** — two-checkpoint per-step
37	  discipline with hard stop after finalize.
38	
39	## Todo format
40	
41	Todo.md contains two main sections "Todo" and "Done" each item is a
42	short explanations of a tasks and links to more details using 1 or more
43	references.
44	
45	Todo items use lazy numbering — every entry begins with `1. ` and the
46	markdown renderer auto-numbers them. Reorder or insert items without
47	renumbering, and reference an entry by its displayed number ("let's
48	work on #3"). The Done section keeps `-` bullets — items aren't
49	referenced by number once completed.
50	
51	Multiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.
52	In markdown, `[2,3]` is a single ref key (won't resolve) and `[2][3]`
53	is parsed as display text `2` with ref key `3` (so `[2]` won't resolve).
54	
55	Examples:
56	
57	# Todo
58	- Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)
59	- Fix bug Y [1]
60	
61	# Done
62	- Fixed issue Z [2],[3]
63	
64	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
65	[2]: issues.md#issue-z
66	[3]: fixes.md#fix-z
67	
68	## Reference numbering
69	
70	Every note file (`todo.md`, `chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a
71	file-local `# References` section at the bottom. Reference numbers
72	are scoped to that file — `[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in
73	`chores-01.md` are independent slots that may point at completely
74	different URLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.
75	
76	## Retiring Done entries
77	
78	`todo.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently shipped
79	work, not a permanent log. Move entries into `done.md` at two natural
80	beats:
81	
82	- **Closing a ladder** — when the final `X.Y.Z` (no suffix) commit
83	  ships, decide which prior entries are no longer needed for nearby
84	  context and migrate them.
85	- **Opening a new ladder** — at `X.Y.Z-0`, do the same sweep before
86	  bumping the version.
87	
88	Migration mechanics:
89	
90	- Move the bullet itself from `todo.md > ## Done` to
91	  `done.md` (preserving the original ref number).
92	- Copy any references the moved entries cite into
93	  `done.md`'s `# References` section (those refs are file-local,
94	  so coexisting with `todo.md`'s namespace is fine).
95	- Prune any references in `todo.md > # References` no longer cited
96	  by anything in `## In Progress` / `## Todo` / `## Done`. This
97	  frees the numbers for future reuse.
98	
```

224	## init + clone redesign (0.41.1)
225	
226	Empirical validation 2026-04-27 against `vc-x1 0.42.0-3` (see
227	`notes/vc-x1-init.md`) surfaced cosmetic anomalies and a
228	substantive design gap. Init's flag surface (`--repo-local`,
229	`--repo-remote`, `--owner`, `--dir`, `[NAME]`) carries 6+
230	mutually-exclusive preflight checks just to prevent impossible
231	combinations from being typed. Clone already implements a
232	unified-positional alternative (URL / `owner/name` shorthand);
233	this cycle extends that pattern to init, adds POR support to
234	both, and unifies their CLI surfaces.
235	
236	Branched off 0.41.0 (commit `6747a27`). On close-out, the
237	in-flight 0.42.0 work rebases on top.
238	
239	### Command structure
240	
241	```
242	vc-x1 init  <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por] [--private] [--dry-run]
243	vc-x1 clone <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por]             [--dry-run]
244	```
245	
246	Identical surfaces modulo `--private` (init only).
247	
248	`<TARGET>` accepts:
249	
250	- **URL** — `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`
251	  (detected by `://` or SSH `<host>:<path>` shape with `@`).
252	- **`owner/name` shorthand** — single `/`, no path prefix;
253	  resolved to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
254	- **Path-prefixed** — `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`. Path
255	  IS the target; last component is the workspace name. Bare
256	  `.` and bare `NAME` are errors (require explicit prefix).
257	
258	`[NAME]`:
259	
260	- For URL / `owner/name` forms: overrides the derived
261	  destination dir name. `vc-x1 clone owner/foo my-name`
262	  clones into `./my-name/` instead of `./foo/`.
263	- For path-prefix form: error if combined (path already
264	  specifies the full target).
265	- Path-form for clone: error (clone needs a remote URL;
266	  see "Operations" for clone's target rules).
267	
268	`--scope`:
269	
270	- `code,bot` (default): both repos, dual-repo layout.
271	- `por`: single repo, no `.vc-config.toml` written.
272	- `code` / `bot` standalone: error. Reason — these are
273	  config-lookup keywords; init has no config to look up
274	  against, and clone's simplification omits them too. The
275	  manual decomposition (clone code as POR, clone bot as
276	  POR, place at `.claude/`, run `vc-x1 symlink`) covers
277	  the rare cases where a user wants the dual layout
278	  composed by hand.
279	
280	`--private`: only meaningful for init when creating a new
281	GitHub repo. Sets visibility at `gh repo create`. Silently
282	warn-and-ignore if the remote already exists. Errors on
283	clone (clone never creates a remote).
284	
285	`--dry-run`: validate the operation as far as possible
286	without side effects. Print what would be done.
287	
288	### Operations
289	
290	**Init** is *smart* — it detects the target dir's state and
291	chooses the right operation.
292	
293	| Target state | `--scope=code,bot` | `--scope=por` |
294	|---|---|---|
295	| empty / nonexistent | create dual-repo from scratch | create POR |
296	| POR (jj+git, no config) | upgrade to dual | error (already POR) |
297	| POR (git only, no `.jj/`) | bootstrap `jj git init`, then upgrade | error (already POR-shape) |
298	| code POR + `.claude/` peer POR (configs missing) | write configs only | error |
299	| dual-repo (configs present) | error (already there) | error (downgrade) |
300	| single-repo (illegal shape) | error | error |
301	| anything else (random files, etc.) | error with diagnostic | error with diagnostic |
302	
303	**Clone** is *dumb* — it just clones URLs into target dirs.
304	
305	| `--scope=por` | clone the URL into `<target>` |
306	| `--scope=code,bot` | clone code URL into `<target>`, derive bot URL (`<URL>.claude`), clone into `<target>/.claude/`, then create symlink via `vc-x1 symlink` |
307	
308	For both clone modes: target must NOT exist (`vc-x1 clone`
309	errors if anything is there). Use `vc-x1 sync` to update an
310	existing checkout.
311	
312	`.vc-config.toml` files for the dual-repo case are *tracked
313	content in the remotes*, not files clone writes. They ride
314	along with the clone. If a remote doesn't have them
315	committed, `vc-x1 init <path> --scope=code,bot` from inside
316	the cloned dir handles the config-only upgrade case (see
317	init's state table above).
318	
319	`--scope=code,bot` is implemented as in-process composition
320	of the `--scope=por` primitive (called twice: once for code
321	URL, once for derived bot URL) plus a `symlink::create`
322	call. No subprocess overhead.
323	
324	If init or clone fails partway through, manual cleanup is
325	required (no rollback).
326

331	`vc-init test-repos/tf1 --scope=code,bot`

> AGENT

Thoughts on the fork:

## chid stability — you're fine

jj's two-id system is built for this. `commit_id` (the git SHA) changes on rewrite; `change_id` is stable through rebase, squash-into-self, describe — anything that doesn't *fold* commits. ochid trailers point at change_ids. So when 0.42.0-0..-4 later rebases on top of 0.41.1, the chids are preserved and every ochid trailer (in both directions) still resolves. The fork doesn't break the cross-ref scheme.

The risk is `jj squash` / `jj abandon` — those collapse or remove change_ids. If we just rebase and describe, we're safe.

## time isn't a better primitive

Two problems with time-based linking: clock skew between repos (commits are authored in different processes/sessions), and time doesn't solve the rewrite problem any better than chid does — you still need a stable identifier baked into the trailer. If we ever distrust chid, the answer is jj hygiene (don't squash-collapse during rebase), not switching primitives. I'd keep chid.

## fork mechanics

Current state: `55eadc8` (0.42.0-4) is just the 0.41.1 docs capture — Cargo.toml bump + chores-07's 0.41.1 section + `notes/vc-x1-init.md`. The "push --scope" work that 0.42.0-4 was nominally for hasn't started.

Cleanest move:

1. **New bookmark** `0.41.1-init-clone` at `6747a27` (the 0.41.0 close-out).
2. **Rebase 55eadc8 onto 6747a27** — `jj rebase -r 55eadc8 -d 6747a27`. This preserves its chid, so the bot's ochid trailer still resolves; the docs land on the new branch as 0.41.1-0.
3. **Rewrite the description + version** in the rebased commit: `(0.42.0-4)` → `(0.41.1-0)`, Cargo.toml `0.42.0-4` → `0.41.1-0`. Probably also relocate the chores section out of `chores-07.md` (which is the 0.42.0-cycle file) into its own file (`chores-08.md` or similar) so the future 0.42.0 rebase doesn't collide on chores-07.
4. **Move `main` back** to `4d8709a` (0.42.0-3, the previous 0.42.0 commit). Reset the bookmark; force-push.
5. **Push the new bookmark.**
6. **Clear `.vc-x1/push-state.toml`** — any saved state from the prior push is stale after the rewind.

Bot repo: untouched. The bot commit that paired with 55eadc8 keeps its ochid trailer; it just now points at a chid living on a different branch instead of main. That's correct — it reflects the actual history of *this* session, which is linear.

## frictions worth flagging

- **Force-push to main.** Destructive, needs your explicit go-ahead. Anyone with `55eadc8` fetched will need to reset.
- **Chores file split.** `chores-07.md` opened for 0.42.0 — the 0.41.1 section bolted onto it should probably move to its own file on the new branch to avoid rebase conflicts later.
- **Cross-ref check after the move.** Run `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` (or the validate flow) on the rebased commit to confirm the bot side's ochid trailer still resolves to it.
- **Validation that chids actually survive** the specific rebase we're doing — the theory is solid but worth empirically checking the first time we do this. If they don't, that's a real gap and *then* we'd talk about alternatives.

4. **Freeze main** for the duration of init-clone-refactor — no new 0.42.0 commits while the side branch is active. Otherwise we'd be deciding on the rebase strategy under deadline pressure later.
5. **Chores file:** new `notes/chores-08.md` for the 0.41.1 cycle, instead of folding into chores-07. Keeps the 0.42.0 chores file untouched on main, so the eventual rebase has zero overlap on chores.
6. **At close-out:** rebase main onto init-clone-refactor; drop `55eadc8` in the rebase; verify ochid trailers resolve via `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` on the rebased commits.

## Bot-side question to settle now

`.claude` is linear and the current session has already advanced past `6747a27`'s pair. When we push the code-side `init-clone-refactor` branch, what does the bot side do? `vc-x1 push <bookmark>` assumes symmetric bookmark names. Three options:

- **(a) Mirror bookmark** — create `init-clone-refactor` on `.claude` *at current `.claude` main HEAD* (not at the historical 0.41.0-paired position). New session commits advance it forward. `.claude` main stays frozen. At close-out, fast-forward `.claude` main to it. Plays nicely with current push tooling. `.claude` history stays linear.
- **(b) Keep `.claude` on main** — push advances `.claude` main as normal, code side advances `init-clone-refactor`. Requires asymmetric-bookmark push, which doesn't exist yet. Probably out of scope for this fork.
- **(c) Use `--scope` to split** — code-only push for branch work, periodic bot-only push for session capture. Awkward; not what scope was designed for.

I'd go with **(a)**. It's mechanically the simplest, doesn't require touching push, and "fast-forward .claude main to init-clone-refactor at close-out" is just `jj bookmark set main -r init-clone-refactor` — no rewrite. The asymmetric ordering between code and bot history (rebased main commits will point at .claude commits that come *before* their init-clone-refactor pairs) is a cosmetic wrinkle, not a chid-correctness problem.

Naming suggestions, in order of preference:

- **partner** — bookmarks cooperate via `push` but each holds its own repo's state. Conveys "yoked together for a purpose, not duplicates of each other." Pairs naturally with a verb form ("partnered bookmarks") and reads well in code/docs.
- **tandem** — captures "advance together via the same mechanism, but each carries its own load." Like a tandem bicycle — two seats, one drivetrain. Slightly more evocative than partner, slightly less common in software vocabulary.
- **paired** — neutral and clear; weaker than partner because "pair" can imply matching halves.

I'd avoid:

- **mirror** — yes, exactly the problem you flagged.
- **disjoint** / **asymmetric** — these describe a property of the relationship, not the technique. Good for prose ("the bookmarks are disjoint here"), poor as a label.
- **yoked** — accurate metaphor but obscure; readers will stumble.

My pick is **partner**, with **tandem** as runner-up. Both leave room to talk about "partner-bookmark mode" or "tandem push" when documenting later.

## Force-push question

Yes, even a description-only change is a force push. `jj describe` rewrites the commit — same `change_id` (good, preserves ochid validity), new `commit_id`. The bookmark moves to the new `commit_id`. From git's view that's a non-fast-forward bookmark move, which is force-push territory. Same is true of `jj squash`, `jj rebase`, any rewrite. Only operations that don't change the commit_id are FF-safe (and there basically aren't any for an existing commit — the commit_id is a hash of its content).

Side note on `-pm`: per CLAUDE.md the suffix is numeric specifically for semver ordering (`0.42.0-1 < 0.42.0-2 < … < 0.42.0`). `-pm` is non-numeric, which semver compares lexically — `0.42.0-2 < 0.42.0-pm < 0.42.0`, sorts *after* every numeric ladder rung. Not broken, but it breaks the convention. If you want an "out of sequence" marker, a high numeric (like `0.42.0-99`) preserves the rule; or just keep `-4` in Cargo.toml and signal the out-of-bandness in the description.

## Should we do it?

I'd lean toward **leaving 55eadc8 alone**. Reasoning:

- The "uncleanliness" is temporary: at close-out we rebase main onto init-clone-refactor and drop 55eadc8 in the rebase (its content has been re-landed). So the cosmetic mess self-resolves.
- Force-pushing 55eadc8 *now* is the first time we'd be exercising chid-preservation-across-rewrite on this project for real. That's a thing we'd want to test deliberately, not as a side effect of cleanup.
- The `fmt::Display for Scope` addition that snuck in — if it's tiny and inert on main (no callers), leaving it costs nothing; if it'd conflict with the eventual 0.42.0 work, we can revert it as a tiny standalone commit later.
- Two operations (rewrite 55eadc8 + plan capture for 0.42.0-5) vs one (just the plan capture) — the simpler path puts us at the fork faster.

The case *for* the rewrite is real if `fmt::Display for Scope` is going to interfere with later 0.42.0 work, or if you want a clean main while init-clone-refactor is in flight (psychological tidiness has value too).

Your call. If you want the rewrite, I'd suggest `0.42.0-99` over `-pm` to keep the semver convention intact.

> AGENT

Big topic. A few framings I think actually hold up:

## Bot repo as a forest of linear chains

The "linear" property generalizes — each session is one append-only chain, and the bot repo is a forest of those chains, never merged. No bot-side merge commits at all. Code-side has a DAG (merges, branches); bot-side is a forest. The mapping is the multi-ochid trailer set on each code commit, fanning out to the contributing chain tips.

This is a cleaner model than "bot side mirrors code side topology" because:
- Each conversation is what it is — merging two conversations into one commit would be falsifying the historical record. A jsonl line is a wire-format record of "the user said X at time T," and merging that with another user's "I said Y at time T'" produces an event that never happened.
- "Never rewrite bot commits" becomes an enforceable rule rather than a guideline. ochid-into-bot is automatically stable.
- Storage and sync stay simple — appending only, no merge conflict resolution on bot side ever.

## Multi-line ochid trailer

Standard git trailer convention already allows multiple values for the same key. Just emit `ochid:` once per pointer:

```
ochid: /.claude/abc123
ochid: /.claude/def456
ochid: /.claude/ghi789
```

Parsers (`vc-x1 chid`, viewers) collect all instances. Single-pointer commits stay backward compatible — they're just the N=1 case. No version bump needed; existing parsers either already accept repeated trailers or are easy to extend.

## When multi-ochid actually shows up

- **Code-side merge with no extra bot work** — N ochids = the merge parents' contributing tip chids (one per parent). Possibly with de-duplication if parents share ancestry.
- **Code-side merge with conflict-resolution session** — N parents' ochids + the resolution session's tip ochid. So if user A and user B merge into M and user C resolves the conflict, M has 3 ochids: A's tip, B's tip, C's session tip.
- **Single-user single-session** — still 1 ochid. Same as today.
- **Code rebase** — ochids unchanged (chids are stable). Same as today. Multi-user rebases work the same as single-user — preserved chids preserved trailers.

## Per-user vs shared bot repo

Open question worth deciding before code lands:

- **Shared bot repo** (today's model extended): one `.claude/` repo holds all sessions across all users. Push from any user appends a chain. Pros: viewer sees everything in one place; cross-references resolve locally. Cons: every user pulls every other user's session data on sync — could be heavy. Permissions are coarse.
- **Per-user bot repos**: each user has their own `.claude-<user>/` repo, ochid trailers carry a user qualifier (`ochid: /.claude-alice/abc123`). Pros: lightweight sync, natural permissions. Cons: viewer needs to know all the bot-repo URLs to show full context; offline viewing breaks if you don't have the relevant user's repo.

I'd lean **shared** as the default with a per-project escape hatch — most teams want the cross-references to "just work." The qualifier in ochid (the path component after the leading `/`) can already encode either model: `/.claude/<chid>` for shared, `/.claude-alice/<chid>` for per-user. The trailer format itself is forward-compatible.

## Things I'd want to think about more before committing

- **Conflict resolution sessions: how do they get authored?** When user C resolves a merge conflict, does their bot session start a fresh chain rooted "from nowhere," or branch off one of the contributing chains? The chain-rooting question affects how the viewer renders it.
- **De-duplication on octopus merges.** If parents share ancestry, you'll get redundant ochids. Trim to unique tips? Keep all? Probably trim, but worth deciding.
- **Bot-side bookmark scheme.** Per-session bookmark? Per-user-per-feature? Naming convention matters because bookmarks are how `jj git push` decides what to send.
- **Viewer concerns.** "Show me the sessions that contributed to this commit" is straightforward (read the trailers, walk back in each chain to the relevant range). "Show me the code commits this session contributed to" is the inverse and needs an index, since chids don't carry forward references. Probably build the index from a one-time scan of code-side trailers.
- **Migration story for existing repos** with single-ochid trailers — they're already valid in the multi-ochid scheme (N=1 case), so probably no migration needed. Worth confirming on the parser side.

Big picture: I think the multi-ochid + linear-forest bot repo + immutable bot commits model is coherent and scales the existing scheme cleanly. The hard parts are mostly UX (viewer, bot bookmark scheme) rather than data-model issues. Worth capturing as a chores section sometime — but probably not in the 0.42.0-5 plan capture, since that's about the immediate fork, not the multi-user roadmap.

96	
97	Expected: ideally an incremental upgrade — add `.claude/`,
98	rewrite parent's `.vc-config.toml` to include `other-repo`,
99	ochid-link the existing initial commit to a new bot-side
100	initial commit, create the symlink. Actual:
101	
102	- Same plan-time error as Test 4 — the
103	  `--scope=bot is meaningless` check fires before any
104	  inspection of the existing workspace.
105	- Filesystem unchanged.
106	- The error message suggests `--scope=code,bot` as the
107	  alternative, but that path is also blocked (see Test 7).
108	
109	## Test 7: `--scope=code,bot` on top of existing code-only workspace
110	
111	`vc-x1 init repoA --repo-local=../tmp-vc-x1 --scope=code,bot`
112	(after Test 5 left a code-only workspace in place)
113	
114	Expected fatal — confirmed, but at a different check than
115	Test 6:
116	
117	- Exit 1.
118	- Error fires at preflight (after `Preflight checks...`):
119	  `'/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/../tmp-vc-x1/repoA'
120	  already exists`.
121	- Filesystem unchanged.
122	
123	## Findings: missing incremental-upgrade path
124	
125	`init` today supports two and only two terminal modes from a
126	clean dir:
127	
128	| Mode | Invocation | Outcome |
129	|---|---|---|
130	| Single-repo | `--scope=code` | code repo + `.vc-config.toml` (no `other-repo`) |
131	| Dual-repo | `--scope=code,bot` (or default) | both repos + cross-ref configs + ochid trailers + symlink |
132	
133	There is **no path** to grow a single-repo workspace into a
134	dual-repo workspace via `init`. Both candidate invocations
135	fail:
136	
137	- `init --scope=bot` on existing code-only → fatal at
138	  plan-time (`--scope=bot is meaningless at init time`),
139	  before any inspection of the existing workspace.
140	- `init --scope=code,bot` on existing code-only → fatal at
141	  preflight (`'<path>/repoA' already exists`).
142	
143	The bot's design sketch for the upgrade path:
144	
145	- Detect the upgrade case in plan-time: `--scope=bot` AND the
146	  target dir contains a `.vc-config.toml` with `path = "/"`
147	  AND no `other-repo`.
148	- Switch to upgrade mode: skip code-side init steps; create
149	  `.claude/`, write `.claude/.vc-config.toml`, rewrite
150	  parent's `.vc-config.toml` to add `other-repo = ".claude"`,
151	  bare-init the bot remote, write a bot-side initial commit
152	  with an `ochid:` trailer pointing at the existing code
153	  initial commit, optionally rewrite the existing code commit
154	  to add the reverse `ochid:` trailer (or accept asymmetry
155	  for the upgrade case), create the symlink.
156	- `init --scope=code,bot` on existing code-only could either
157	  also enter upgrade mode (reusing the existing code repo) or
158	  stay fatal — the user-facing semantics matter (does
159	  `code,bot` mean "ensure both" or "create both fresh"?). The
160	  bot's lean: keep `code,bot` strict-create (today's
161	  semantics) and route the upgrade through the explicit
162	  `--scope=bot`-on-existing form.
163	
164	This is a feature gap, not a bug — to be filed as a todo
165	candidate after the 0.41.1 sync work is settled.
166	
167	## Test 8: `--scope=<path>` (path-form)
168	
169	`vc-x1 init repoA --scope=../tmp-vc-x1-path`
170	(no `--repo-local`, no `--repo-remote`)
171	
172	Expected fatal — confirmed:
173	
174	- Exit 1.
175	- Error: `--scope=../tmp-vc-x1-path: path-form scope is
176	  meaningless at init time — use --repo-local <PATH> for a
177	  local fixture or --repo-remote <URL> for an existing
178	  remote`.
179	- Filesystem unchanged (no `repoA/` or `tmp-vc-x1-path/`
180	  created).
181	- Same `bm-track` cosmetic anomaly fires.
182	
183	Status: per the chores-07 design (`### --scope enum refactor
184	(0.42.0)`'s applicability matrix), init was deliberately
185	specified as `Single(_)` accepted = no, on the rationale
186	"init creates workspaces, not POR repos." Re-opened
187	2026-04-27 — see "Findings: path-form support" below.
188	
189	## Findings: path-form support is wanted
190	
191	The user wants `init --scope=<path>` to work. The current
192	flag set splits two concerns that the path form could fold
193	together:
194	
195	| Today | Path-form shorthand |
196	|---|---|
197	| `--scope=code` (mode) + `--repo-local=<dir>` (location) | `--scope=<dir>` |
198	
199	Two reasonable semantics for `init NAME --scope=<path>`:
200	
201	- **(a) Local-fixture single-repo shorthand.** Equivalent
202	  to `init NAME --repo-local=<path> --scope=code`. Creates
203	  a single-repo workspace at `<path>/NAME` with a local bare
204	  remote, no GitHub. Mirrors the `Single(_)` semantic from
205	  sync — "ignore the dual-repo defaults, operate on this one
206	  spot." This is the bot's recommended reading.
207	- **(b) Bare-init at exactly `<path>`.** The path IS the
208	  workspace location, no `NAME` segment appended. Conflicts
209	  with the existing `NAME` positional arg (would have to
210	  become optional / mutually exclusive). More invasive.
211	
212	Reading (a) is the cleanest: it preserves the existing
213	`NAME` positional, drops to single-repo by default
214	(consistent with `Single(_)` everywhere else), and the
215	generated workspace looks identical to what
216	`--scope=code --repo-local=<path>` produces today.
217	
218	The user's stated priority (2026-04-27): implement
219	path-form support **before** the 0.41.1 sync fix, since the
220	sync fix's validation harness benefits from the shorthand.
221

{
  "file_path": "/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/notes/forks-multi-user.md",
  "content": "# Forking and multi-user coordination\n\nCaptures design discussion about two related but separable\nconcerns:\n\n1. **Forking** a dual-repo workspace — working on an older\n   code-side base while keeping the bot side append-only.\n2. **Multi-user collaboration** on the same dual-repo —\n   multiple humans, multiple bot sessions, code-side merges.\n\nBoth surface the same underlying tension: the code repo has\nthe classic git/jj DAG (branches, merges, rebases), while the\nbot repo is fundamentally an append-only journal of\nconversations that should never be rewritten.\n\nThis file is forward-looking: most of what it describes is\nthe bot thinks, not implemented. Treat as a design reference,\nnot a status doc.\n\n## Forking with the bot side staying linear\n\n### The asymmetric situation\n\nWhen work needs to happen on an older code-side base — e.g.,\n0.41.1 work branched off 0.41.0 while 0.42.0 is in flight on\nmain — the code repo can fork without difficulty. That's a\nnormal git/jj branch.\n\nThe bot repo can't fork the same way: each session is a linear\nconversation, and rewriting an existing session line would\nfalsify the historical record. The conversation that happened\nis the conversation that happened; it doesn't get re-played\nfrom a different branch base.\n\n### chid stability across rebase\n\njj's two-id model is built for this scenario. Each commit has\nboth:\n\n- `commit_id` — git SHA, changes on rewrite.\n- `change_id` — stable across `describe` / `rebase` /\n  `squash-into-self`.\n\n`ochid:` trailers carry change_ids. So when a code-side branch\nlater rebases on top of another branch, change_ids are\npreserved and ochid trailers in both directions still resolve.\n\nThe bot thinks the only operations that break this are\n`jj squash` (folding two commits into one — collapses two\nchange_ids into one) and `jj abandon` (removing a commit —\nloses the change_id entirely). Pure rebase is safe.\n\n### Why not time-based linkers\n\nTime isn't a stronger primitive than change_id:\n\n- Clock skew between processes / repos breaks ordering.\n- Time still doesn't survive rewrites any better than\n  change_id does — you'd still need a stable identifier baked\n  into the trailer that matches some property of the\n  counterpart commit.\n- change_id is jj's intended stability primitive — that's\n  literally the job it exists to do.\n\nIf the change_id scheme ever shows weakness, the bot thinks\nthe answer is jj-side hygiene (don't `squash`-collapse during\nrebase) rather than switching primitives.\n\n### Partner bookmarks\n\nThe chosen technique for forking the code side while keeping\nthe bot side linear: **partner bookmarks**.\n\nWhen a code-side branch needs to advance independently, create\na bookmark of the same name on the bot side starting at the\n*current* bot HEAD — not at the historical bot commit paired\nwith the code-side branch base. The two bookmarks share a name\nand advance together via `vc-x1 push`, but each carries its\nown repo's state.\n\nOther names considered and rejected:\n\n- **mirror** — implies symmetric content. The bookmarks are\n  not mirrors; they hold different content with no\n  point-by-point correspondence.\n- **tandem** — captures cooperation, but slightly less common\n  in software vocabulary.\n- **paired** — bland; \"pair\" can imply matching halves.\n- **disjoint** / **asymmetric** — describe a property of the\n  relationship, not a label for the technique.\n- **yoked** — accurate metaphor but obscure.\n\n**partner** won because it conveys cooperation without\nimplying duplication. Always subject to change as we live\nwith the term.\n\nThe asymmetric ordering between code and bot history (rebased\nmain commits on the code side will eventually point at bot\ncommits that come *before* their partner-branch pairs in bot\nhistory) is a cosmetic wrinkle, not a correctness problem —\nchange_ids resolve regardless of position.\n\n### Recovery anchor\n\nThe original main HEAD — the commit being \"branched away\nfrom\" — should stay put, not be rewritten or rewound. It's\nthe recovery anchor for the operation. If the partner-branch\nwork goes wrong, main is still where it was, and recovery is\n`jj abandon` on the new branch's commits.\n\nIn the 0.41.1 init+clone refactor, this means main stays at\nits current 0.42.0-4 docs-capture commit (`55eadc8`) for the\nduration of the side-branch work. That commit becomes\nredundant after the eventual rebase — its content has been\nre-landed on `init-clone-refactor` — and gets dropped during\nthe rebase rather than being rewound now.\n\n## Multi-user collaboration\n\nThe bot thinks the same model — linear forest on the bot\nside, multi-trailer reconciliation on the code side —\ngeneralizes naturally to multi-user.\n\n### Bot repo as a forest of linear chains\n\nEach session is one append-only chain. The bot repo is a\nforest of those chains; never merged. No bot-side merge\ncommits at all. Code-side has a DAG (merges, branches);\nbot-side is a forest. The mapping is the multi-ochid trailer\nset on each code commit, fanning out to the contributing\nchain tips.\n\nThe bot thinks this is cleaner than \"bot side mirrors code\nside topology\" because:\n\n- Each conversation is a wire-format record of what was\n  actually said. Merging two conversations into one commit\n  would falsify that record.\n- \"Never rewrite bot commits\" becomes an enforceable rule —\n  change_ids on the bot side are automatically stable.\n- Storage and sync stay simple — appending only, no merge\n  conflict resolution on the bot side ever.\n\n### Multi-line ochid trailer\n\nStandard git trailer convention allows multiple values for\nthe same key. Just emit `ochid:` once per pointer:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/abc123\nochid: /.claude/def456\nochid: /.claude/ghi789\n```\n\nSingle-pointer commits stay backward compatible — they're\njust the N=1 case. No version bump needed; existing parsers\neither already accept repeated trailers or are easy to\nextend.\n\n### When multi-ochid actually applies\n\n- **Code-side merge with no extra bot work** — N ochids =\n  the merge parents' contributing tip change_ids (one per\n  parent). Possibly with de-duplication if parents share\n  ancestry.\n- **Code-side merge with conflict-resolution session** —\n  N parents' ochids + the resolution session's tip ochid.\n  If user A and user B merge into M and user C resolves the\n  conflict, M has 3 ochids: A's tip, B's tip, C's session\n  tip.\n- **Single-user single-session** — still 1 ochid. Same as\n  today.\n- **Code rebase** — ochids unchanged (change_ids are\n  stable). Same as today. Multi-user rebases work the same\n  as single-user.\n\n### Per-user vs shared bot repo\n\nOpen question worth deciding before code lands.\n\n- **Shared bot repo** (today's model extended): one\n  `.claude/` repo holds all sessions across all users. Push\n  from any user appends a chain. Pros: viewer sees\n  everything in one place; cross-references resolve locally.\n  Cons: every user pulls every other user's session data on\n  sync — could be heavy. Permissions are coarse.\n- **Per-user bot repos**: each user has their own\n  `.claude-<user>/` repo, ochid trailers carry a user\n  qualifier (`ochid: /.claude-alice/abc123`). Pros:\n  lightweight sync, natural permissions. Cons: viewer needs\n  to know all the bot-repo URLs to show full context;\n  offline viewing breaks if you don't have the relevant\n  user's repo.\n\nThe bot thinks **shared** is the default with a per-project\nescape hatch — most teams want the cross-references to\n\"just work.\" The qualifier in ochid (the path component\nafter the leading `/`) already encodes either model:\n`/.claude/<chid>` for shared, `/.claude-alice/<chid>` for\nper-user. The trailer format itself is forward-compatible.\n\n### Bot-side commit immutability\n\nCodify \"never rewrite bot commits\" as a hard rule. The\nreason: change_ids on the bot side need to be permanently\nstable for ochid trailers from the code side to resolve\nforever. Even `jj describe` (description-only) changes the\ncommit_id, which doesn't break change_ids but does signal\nthat bot commits are mutable in a way they shouldn't be.\n\nTrade: any commit-level metadata fix has to be done by\nappending a new commit, not amending the existing one.\nAwkward but correct.\n\n## Future-direction notes\n\nTwo alternatives to the partner-bookmark technique that may\nbe worth considering once we live with the current scheme:\n\n### Always keep the bot repo on main\n\nInstead of creating a partner bookmark on the bot side for\neach code-side branch, the bot side could be locked to a\nsingle bookmark — `main` — for the entire lifetime of the\nproject. Every push would advance bot main, regardless of\nwhat bookmark the code side is on.\n\nThe bot thinks this aligns with \"bot history is one linear\njournal\" more strongly than partner bookmarks do. Partner\nbookmarks introduce *parallel* bot bookmarks even though the\nbot history under them is still linear; an always-main\ndiscipline removes that parallelism entirely.\n\nTrade: requires push / finalize / sync to support asymmetric\nbookmark names per side (see next note).\n\n### Multi-bookmark-name support in push / finalize / sync\n\nToday, `vc-x1 push <bookmark>` advances the same bookmark\nname on both code and bot sides. The \"always-on-main\"\ndiscipline above (and other asymmetric workflows) requires\npush / finalize / sync to take separate bookmark arguments\nper side, e.g.:\n\n```\nvc-x1 push --code-bookmark init-clone-refactor --bot-bookmark main\nvc-x1 push -B init-clone-refactor              # bot defaults to main\nvc-x1 push init-clone-refactor                  # both, today's behavior\n```\n\nThe bot thinks the right shape lands once `--scope` is\nfully wired across the dual-repo commands — `--scope`\nalready handles \"which side does this command apply to,\"\nand adding per-side bookmark arguments is a natural\nextension.\n\n## Open questions worth thinking about\n\n- **Conflict resolution sessions: how do they get\n  authored?** When user C resolves a merge conflict, does\n  their bot session start a fresh chain rooted \"from\n  nowhere,\" or branch off one of the contributing chains?\n  The chain-rooting question affects how the viewer renders\n  it.\n- **De-duplication on octopus merges.** If parents share\n  ancestry, you'll get redundant ochids. Trim to unique\n  tips? Keep all? The bot thinks trim, but worth deciding.\n- **Bot-side bookmark scheme.** Per-session bookmark?\n  Per-user-per-feature? Naming convention matters because\n  bookmarks are how `jj git push` decides what to send.\n- **Viewer concerns.** \"Show me the sessions that\n  contributed to this commit\" is straightforward (read the\n  trailers, walk back in each chain to the relevant range).\n  \"Show me the code commits this session contributed to\" is\n  the inverse and needs an index, since change_ids don't\n  carry forward references. Probably build the index from a\n  one-time scan of code-side trailers.\n- **Migration story for existing repos** with single-ochid\n  trailers — they're already valid in the multi-ochid\n  scheme (N=1 case), so probably no migration needed. Worth\n  confirming on the parser side.\n"
}
```

{
  "file_path": "/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/notes/chores-08.md",
  "content": "# Chores-08.md\n\nGeneral chores notes for the 0.41.1 init+clone redesign cycle.\n\nThis file opens at 08 (skipping 07) because chores-07.md is the\n0.42.0-cycle file living on `main`. The 0.41.1 cycle branched\noff `6747a27` (the 0.41.0 close-out commit), where chores-07.md\ndoesn't exist. Starting at 08 here avoids any rebase collision\non chores-07 when `main` later rebases on top of\n`init-clone-refactor`.\n\nFor the broader forking model and partner-bookmark technique\nthat drove this branch's existence, see\n[`forks-multi-user.md`](forks-multi-user.md).\n\n## init + clone redesign (0.41.1)\n\nEmpirical validation 2026-04-27 against `vc-x1 0.42.0-3` (see\n[`vc-x1-init.md`](vc-x1-init.md)) surfaced cosmetic anomalies\nand a substantive design gap. Init's flag surface\n(`--repo-local`, `--repo-remote`, `--owner`, `--dir`,\n`[NAME]`) carries 6+ mutually-exclusive preflight checks just\nto prevent impossible combinations from being typed. Clone\nalready implements a unified-positional alternative (URL /\n`owner/name` shorthand); this cycle extends that pattern to\ninit, adds POR support to both, and unifies their CLI\nsurfaces.\n\nBranched off `6747a27` (0.41.0 close-out). On close-out, the\nin-flight 0.42.0 work on `main` rebases on top.\n\n### Command structure\n\n```\nvc-x1 init  <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por] [--private] [--dry-run]\nvc-x1 clone <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por]             [--dry-run]\n```\n\nIdentical surfaces modulo `--private` (init only).\n\n`<TARGET>` accepts:\n\n- **URL** — `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`,\n  `https://...(.git)?` (detected by `://` or SSH\n  `<host>:<path>` shape with `@`).\n- **`owner/name` shorthand** — single `/`, no path prefix;\n  resolved to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.\n- **Path-prefixed** — `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`.\n  Path IS the target; last component is the workspace name.\n  Bare `.` and bare `NAME` are errors (require explicit\n  prefix).\n\n`[NAME]`:\n\n- For URL / `owner/name` forms: overrides the derived\n  destination dir name. `vc-x1 clone owner/foo my-name`\n  clones into `./my-name/` instead of `./foo/`.\n- For path-prefix form: error if combined (path already\n  specifies the full target).\n- Path-form for clone: error (clone needs a remote URL; see\n  \"Operations\" for clone's target rules).\n\n`--scope`:\n\n- `code,bot` (default): both repos, dual-repo layout.\n- `por`: single repo, no `.vc-config.toml` written.\n- `code` / `bot` standalone: error. Reason — these are\n  config-lookup keywords; init has no config to look up\n  against, and clone's simplification omits them too. The\n  manual decomposition (clone code as POR, clone bot as\n  POR, place at `.claude/`, run `vc-x1 symlink`) covers the\n  rare cases where a user wants the dual layout composed\n  by hand.\n\n`--private`: only meaningful for init when creating a new\nGitHub repo. Sets visibility at `gh repo create`. Silently\nwarn-and-ignore if the remote already exists. Errors on\nclone (clone never creates a remote).\n\n`--dry-run`: validate the operation as far as possible\nwithout side effects. Print what would be done.\n\n### Operations\n\n**Init** is *smart* — it detects the target dir's state and\nchooses the right operation.\n\n| Target state | `--scope=code,bot` | `--scope=por` |\n|---|---|---|\n| empty / nonexistent | create dual-repo from scratch | create POR |\n| POR (jj+git, no config) | upgrade to dual | error (already POR) |\n| POR (git only, no `.jj/`) | bootstrap `jj git init`, then upgrade | error (already POR-shape) |\n| code POR + `.claude/` peer POR (configs missing) | write configs only | error |\n| dual-repo (configs present) | error (already there) | error (downgrade) |\n| single-repo (illegal shape) | error | error |\n| anything else (random files, etc.) | error with diagnostic | error with diagnostic |\n\n**Clone** is *dumb* — it just clones URLs into target dirs.\n\n| `--scope=por` | clone the URL into `<target>` |\n| `--scope=code,bot` | clone code URL into `<target>`, derive bot URL (`<URL>.claude`), clone into `<target>/.claude/`, then create symlink via `vc-x1 symlink` |\n\nFor both clone modes: target must NOT exist (`vc-x1 clone`\nerrors if anything is there). Use `vc-x1 sync` to update an\nexisting checkout.\n\n`.vc-config.toml` files for the dual-repo case are *tracked\ncontent in the remotes*, not files clone writes. They ride\nalong with the clone. If a remote doesn't have them\ncommitted, `vc-x1 init <path> --scope=code,bot` from inside\nthe cloned dir handles the config-only upgrade case (see\ninit's state table above).\n\n`--scope=code,bot` is implemented as in-process composition\nof the `--scope=por` primitive (called twice: once for code\nURL, once for derived bot URL) plus a `symlink::create`\ncall. No subprocess overhead.\n\nIf init or clone fails partway through, manual cleanup is\nrequired (no rollback).\n\n### Example layouts (local repos)\n\ncwd = `~/prgs`\n\n`vc-init test-repos/tf1 --scope=code,bot`\n`vc-init test-repos/tf1`\n\nTODO: add actual output of ls or tree cmds (fill at\nclose-out).\n\n`vc-init ../test-repos/tf1 --scope=code,bot`\n`vc-init ../test-repos/tf1`\n\nTODO: add actual output of ls or tree cmds (fill at\nclose-out).\n\n### Preflight\n\n- Verify `jj` is installed (`jj --version`); friendly error\n  with install link if missing.\n- For init URL / `owner/name` forms: probe with\n  `git ls-remote <url>`. Exists → clone. Doesn't → create\n  via `gh repo create` (errors if host isn't GitHub or\n  `gh` missing).\n- For clone URL / `owner/name` forms: probe with\n  `git ls-remote <url>`. Exists → clone. Doesn't → error\n  (clone is dumb, no auto-create).\n\n### Edits\n\n- `Cargo.toml`: bump to `0.41.1`.\n- New `src/repo_url.rs` (or fold into `src/common.rs`):\n  lift `derive_name` and `resolve_url` from `clone.rs`. Add\n  `parse_target(s) -> Target` enum\n  `{Url(String), OwnerName(String, String), Path(PathBuf)}`.\n  Single source of truth for positional parsing across init\n  and clone.\n- `src/clone.rs`:\n  - `CloneArgs`: `<TARGET>` + optional `[NAME]` positionals;\n    add `--scope code,bot|por` (default `code,bot`); drop\n    `--dir`. Old `--repo` positional rename: `repo` →\n    `target`.\n  - Refactor body into `clone_one(url, target_dir)` (the\n    primitive, also used by `--scope=por`) and\n    `clone_dual(code_url, target_dir)` (orchestrator —\n    derives bot URL, calls `clone_one` twice, calls\n    `symlink::create`).\n  - Pre-clone check: error if `target_dir` exists.\n- `src/init.rs`:\n  - `InitArgs`: drop `owner`, `repo_local`, `repo_remote`,\n    `dir`; replace bare-name `name` positional with\n    `<TARGET>` + optional `[NAME]`.\n  - Remove the 6 mutually-exclusive flag checks.\n  - New `detect_state(path) -> InitTargetState`\n    `{Empty, PorJjGit, PorGitOnly, PorWithPeerPor,\n    SingleRepoWorkspace, DualRepoWorkspace, Other(reason)}`.\n  - Refactor body into `init_one(target_dir, opts)` (the\n    `--scope=por` primitive, also used as a step inside\n    `--scope=code,bot`) and `init_dual(target_dir, opts)`\n    (orchestrator — calls `init_one` twice, writes both\n    `.vc-config.toml` files, ochid-links,\n    `symlink::create`).\n  - POR upgrade paths:\n    - PorJjGit + `--scope=code,bot` → skip code-side init,\n      run bot-side `init_one` into `.claude/`, write\n      configs, ochid-link existing code commit + new bot\n      commit, symlink.\n    - PorGitOnly + `--scope=code,bot` → `jj git init`\n      first, then PorJjGit path.\n    - PorWithPeerPor + `--scope=code,bot` → write only the\n      two `.vc-config.toml` files + symlink (both repos\n      already exist).\n- `src/test_helpers.rs`: `Fixture::new_opts` reshapes to\n  use the new `target` positional shape (and `[NAME]` if\n  needed).\n- `notes/todo.md`: cycle ladder in `## In Progress`.\n- `notes/chores-08.md`: per-step post-impl subsections\n  (this file).\n- `notes/vc-x1-init.md`: close out cosmetic anomalies (fold\n  into final close-out).\n\n### Cycle structure — multi-step\n\n- `-0` — plan + version bump + `notes/forks-multi-user.md`\n  capture + `notes/chores-08.md` (this section) +\n  `notes/vc-x1-init.md` brought forward + partner\n  bookmarks set up.\n- `-1` — lift `derive_name` / `resolve_url` /\n  `parse_target` to shared module; clone migrates\n  internally (no behavior change yet).\n- `-2` — clone reshape: `<TARGET>` + `[NAME]`\n  positionals, add `--scope code,bot|por`, refactor into\n  `clone_one` / `clone_dual`. Add target-exists pre-check.\n- `-3` — init reshape: drop old flags, add `<TARGET>` +\n  `[NAME]`, add `--scope=por`, refactor into `init_one` /\n  `init_dual`. Existing create-from-empty operations work\n  via the new shape.\n- `-4` — init POR detection + upgrade paths\n  (PorJjGit, PorGitOnly auto-bootstrap, PorWithPeerPor\n  config-only).\n- `-5` — `test_helpers::Fixture` migration; audit\n  downstream callers across the test suite.\n- final — cycle close-out: fill in Example Layout outputs,\n  address `notes/vc-x1-init.md` cosmetic anomalies, drop\n  the `-N` suffix.\n\n### Decisions made during design\n\n- **Version + cycle line.** This work + the sync `--check`\n  fix land on the 0.41.x line. ## Thoughts on commit-first-then-review

I'd adopt it for substantive work units — this incident is exactly what it defends against, and jj's `jj squash` (default: WC into `@-`) makes "fold review edits into the existing commit" trivial. Skipping the `.N` suffix is right; jj squash already gives you one clean commit per logical step without the suffix machinery. KIS wins.

A few nuances worth thinking about:

- **Pre-commit checklist runs at commit time, not before.** So `cargo fmt && cargo clippy && cargo test` happen *before* the commit goes through, not as a separate review step. If code touches happen in review-edit cycles, the checklist re-runs on each squash where code changed.
- **Provisional commit message.** The message is drafted at commit time (before review), revised via `jj describe` if review reshapes scope. Small extra step, mostly painless.
- **Summary still matters.** The "stop and ask for review" message should still summarize what's in the commit so you can decide quickly whether to dig in. Without the summary, "review this commit" puts all the work on you.
- **Scope-change escape hatch.** If review surfaces that the work needs substantial rework (not just tweaks), the right move is `jj abandon` + re-author, not squash. Worth codifying as the exception to the squash default.

Codifying in CLAUDE.md can wait until we've used the pattern for a cycle or two and ironed out the wrinkles — but I'd start using it now if you want. Ready when you are.

I'd go with **"review save"**. Reasons:

- "save" matches what every editor says when it writes to disk, so the metaphor is immediate.
- Reads cleanly as both verb and noun: "I'll do a review save of those files" / "looking at the review save now."
- Doesn't overload jj's existing `change` vocabulary — `change_id` / chids are already a thing here, and "review change" risks ambiguity in conversation ("did you review the change?" vs "did you do a review change?").

Runner-up is **"review draft"** if you'd prefer the provisional connotation over the durability one. I'd skip "review change" because of the overload.

{

  "content": "# Draft reviews\n\nA lightweight workflow convention to make in-progress work\ndurable and reviewable without committing prematurely. Adopted\n2026-04-28 after an accidental ESC interrupted a queued file\nwrite and surfaced the question.\n\n## What \"draft saved for review\" means\n\nAfter authoring or editing a unit of work, the bot writes all\nrelevant files to disk and pauses with the following prompt:\n\n> Draft saved for review: approve (y/n), edit, or suggest\n> changes.\n\n\"Draft saved\" = files are on disk in their proposed state.\nNothing has been jj-committed, jj-squashed, or pushed.\n\nThe user can then:\n\n- **Approve (y)** — bot proceeds (typically: pre-commit\n  checklist, then propose commit message for the second\n  approval gate).\n- **Approve (n) or silence** — bot waits.\n- **Edit** — user opens the files in their editor and makes\n  changes directly. Bot resumes only when told.\n- **Suggest changes** — user describes desired changes; bot\n  re-edits the draft and pauses again with the same prompt.\n\n## Why\n\n- **ESC-resilience.** Each `Write` lands atomically on disk.\n  An interruption between writes loses only the in-flight\n  one, not previously-saved files.\n- **Full-fidelity review.** Markdown renders properly, code\n  type-checks, tests can run — anything you'd do on the real\n  files works on the draft.\n- **Trivial revert.** `jj restore` undoes any draft change\n  that wasn't liked. No commit/abandon dance needed during\n  review.\n- **No premature jj state.** Nothing to squash, no commit_id\n  churn, no force-push concerns. The review is purely a\n  filesystem-level activity until the user approves.\n\n## Mechanics\n\n- **No preflight during review iteration.** `cargo fmt`,\n  `cargo clippy`, `cargo test`, etc. are *not* run between\n  draft saves. fmt would mutate files in ways that interact\n  badly with mid-review edits, and the noise distracts from\n  the review itself. Preflight runs once, at final approval,\n  before the actual jj commit.\n- **Multiple draft saves are normal.** Each round of\n  suggested changes ends in a fresh \"Draft saved for review\"\n  prompt. The user's \"approve (y)\" is the explicit transition\n  out of draft mode.\n- **Summary still required.** The pause-for-review message\n  should include a short summary of what's in the draft\n  (file list with one-line gists, plus any noteworthy\n  decisions) so the user can decide quickly whether to\n  inspect closely or approve.\n- **Scope-change escape hatch.** If a review surfaces that\n  the work needs substantial rework (not just edits), the\n  right move is to discard the draft (`jj restore`) and\n  re-author rather than iteratively patching. Squash is for\n  small adjustments.\n\n## Relationship to the existing two-gate flow\n\nCLAUDE.md's `Commit-Push-Finalize Flow` already specifies two\nexplicit approval gates: review (after work) and message\n(before push). Draft reviews refine the *first* gate — they\nmake explicit that the \"review\" stage is iterative and lives\non disk, not in jj. The second gate (commit message) is\nunaffected and still happens at `vc-x1 push` time.\n\nCodification in CLAUDE.md is deferred until the convention\nhas been used for a cycle or two and any wrinkles are\nironed out.\n"

A tighter cadence going forward: one draft review per file (or per small cluster — e.g., a `Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock` pair counts as one). For this `-0`, that would have been ~5 prompts: forks-multi-user, chores-08, draft-reviews, vc-x1-init, todo+Cargo. You could have stopped me on any of them.

10	pub struct CloneArgs {
11	    /// GitHub repo (owner/name) or git URL
12	    #[arg(value_name = "REPO")]
13	    pub repo: String,
14	
15	    /// Local directory name [default: derived from REPO]
16	    #[arg(value_name = "NAME")]
17	    pub name: Option<String>,

28	/// Derive project name from a repo argument.
29	///
30	/// Handles: `owner/name`, `git@github.com:owner/name.git`,
31	/// `https://github.com/owner/name.git`, `https://github.com/owner/name`
32	fn derive_name(repo: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
33	    // Strip trailing .git
34	    let repo = repo.strip_suffix(".git").unwrap_or(repo); // OK: repo arg may not end in .git
35	
36	    // Take everything after the last `/` or `:`
37	    let name = repo
38	        .rsplit_once('/')
39	        .or_else(|| repo.rsplit_once(':'))
40	        .map(|(_, name)| name)
41	        .unwrap_or(repo); // OK: no separator → whole string is the name
42	
43	    if name.is_empty() {
44	        return Err(format!("cannot derive project name from '{repo}'").into());
45	    }
46	    Ok(name.to_string())
47	}
48	
49	/// Resolve a repo argument to a git clone URL.
50	///
51	/// `owner/name` (no scheme, no `:` before `/`) becomes `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
52	/// Anything else is passed through as-is.
53	fn resolve_url(repo: &str) -> String {
54	    // Already a URL (has scheme or SSH-style colon)
55	    if repo.contains("://") || repo.contains('@') {
56	        return repo.to_string();
57	    }
58	    // owner/name shorthand — must have exactly one `/` and no other URL indicators
59	    if repo.matches('/').count() == 1 && !repo.contains(':') {
60	        return format!("git@github.com:{repo}.git");
61	    }
62	    repo.to_string()
63	}
64	
65	/// Derive the session repo URL from the code repo URL.
66	///
67	/// Appends `.claude` before `.git` (or at the end):
68	/// - `git@github.com:owner/name.git` → `git@github.com:owner/name.claude.git`
69	/// - `https://github.com/owner/name.git` → `https://github.com/owner/name.claude.git`
70	/// - `https://github.com/owner/name` → `https://github.com/owner/name.claude`
71	fn derive_session_url(url: &str) -> String {
72	    if let Some(base) = url.strip_suffix(".git") {
73	        format!("{base}.claude.git")
74	    } else {
75	        format!("{url}.claude")
76	    }
77	}
78	
79	pub fn clone_repo(args: &CloneArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
80	    log::debug!("clone: enter");
81	    let parent_dir = match &args.dir {
82	        Some(d) => d.clone(),
83	        None => std::env::current_dir()?,
84	    };
85	
86	    let name = match &args.name {
87	        Some(n) => n.clone(),
88	        None => derive_name(&args.repo)?,
89	    };
90	    let project_dir = parent_dir.join(&name);
91	    let session_dir = project_dir.join(".claude");
92	    let url = resolve_url(&args.repo);
93	
94	    let session_url = derive_session_url(&url);
95	
96	    if args.dry_run {
97	        info!("Dry run — would execute:");
98	        info!("  1. git clone {url} {name}");
99	        info!("  2. git clone {session_url} {name}/.claude");
100	        info!("  3. jj git init --colocate in {name}/");
101	        info!("  4. jj git init --colocate in {name}/.claude/");
102	        info!("  5. Create Claude Code symlink");
103	        return Ok(());
104	    }
105	
106	    // Preflight
107	    if project_dir.exists() {
108	        return Err(format!("'{}' already exists", project_dir.display()).into());
109	    }
110	
111	    run("jj", &["--version"], Path::new(".")).map_err(|_| "jj is not installed")?;
112	
113	    // Step 1: Clone code repo
114	    let project_str = project_dir
115	        .to_str()
116	        .ok_or("project path is not valid UTF-8")?;
117	    info!("Step 1: Cloning {url}...");
118	    run("git", &["clone", &url, project_str], &parent_dir)?;
119	
120	    // Step 2: Clone session repo
121	    let session_str = session_dir
122	        .to_str()
123	        .ok_or("session path is not valid UTF-8")?;
124	    info!("Step 2: Cloning {session_url}...");
125	    match run("git", &["clone", &session_url, session_str], &parent_dir) {
126	        Ok(_) => {}
127	        Err(e) => {
128	            info!("Step 2: No session repo found ({e}) — skipping");
129	        }
130	    }
131	
132	    // Step 3: jj git init --colocate in code repo. Note: colocate after a
133	    // plain `git clone` does NOT auto-establish bookmark tracking — jj
134	    // emits a hint to run `jj bookmark track …`. We do that explicitly,
135	    // then assert via verify_tracking.
136	    info!("Step 3: Initializing jj in code repo...");
137	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &project_dir)?;
138	    run(
139	        "jj",
140	        &["bookmark", "track", "main", "--remote=origin"],
141	        &project_dir,
142	    )?;
143	    crate::common::verify_tracking(&project_dir, "main")?;
144	
145	    // Step 4: jj git init --colocate in session repo (if cloned)
146	    if session_dir.exists() {
147	        info!("Step 4: Initializing jj in session repo...");
148	        run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &session_dir)?;
149	        run(
150	            "jj",
151	            &["bookmark", "track", "main", "--remote=origin"],
152	            &session_dir,
153	        )?;
154	        crate::common::verify_tracking(&session_dir, "main")?;
155	    } else {
156	        info!("Step 4: No session repo — skipping jj init");
157	    }
158	
159	    // Step 5: Create Claude Code symlink
160	    info!("Step 5: Creating Claude Code symlink...");
161	    let symlink_dir = {
162	        let home =
163	            std::env::var("HOME").map_err(|_| "HOME environment variable not set".to_string())?;
164	        PathBuf::from(home).join(".claude").join("projects")
165	    };
166	
167	    let sl = symlink::SymLink::new(&project_dir, Path::new(".claude"), &symlink_dir)?;
168	    sl.create(false)?;
169	
170	    info!("");
171	    info!("Done! Project cloned to {}", project_dir.display());
172	    info!("  Code repo:    {project_str}");
173	    info!("  Session repo: {}", session_dir.display());
174	    info!(
175	        "  Symlink:      {} -> {}",
176	        sl.symlink_path.display(),
177	        sl.abs_target.display()
178	    );
179	
180	    log::debug!("clone: exit");
181	    Ok(())
182	}

Plan for `0.41.1-1`:

**Module:** new `src/repo_url.rs`. `common.rs` is at 1061 lines and is the catch-all; URL/target parsing is coherent enough to deserve its own module.

**Contents:**
- `Target` enum + `parse_target()` — the new positional parser (no consumer yet; staged for -2/-3).
- `derive_name`, `resolve_url`, `derive_session_url` — lifted from `clone.rs`. Tests move with them.

**Deviation from chores-08 plan:** `init.rs` also has `derive_session_url` and `derive_name_from_url` — verbatim duplicates of clone's. I'd consolidate both call sites in this step rather than leaving init's copies until `-3` (init reshape is about CLI surface, not these helpers). Net effect: cleaner -1 commit; -3 stays focused.

**Cadence:** ~5 draft-review prompts — one per file (repo_url.rs new, main.rs mod decl, clone.rs migration, init.rs migration, then preflight/commit).

Sound good? Or do you want me to keep -1 narrow (clone-only, init's dup stays for -3)?

  "content": "//! Parsing and derivation helpers for repository URLs and targets.\n//!\n//! Single source of truth for the positional shapes that `init` and\n//! `clone` accept (URL, owner/name shorthand, path) and for the\n//! URL-derivation helpers shared between them.\n//!\n//! Lifted from `clone.rs` / `init.rs` in 0.41.1-1; consumers\n//! migrate to `parse_target` in 0.41.1-2 (clone) and 0.41.1-3\n//! (init).\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\n/// A parsed positional `<TARGET>` argument to `init` or `clone`.\n///\n/// - `Url` — full git URL (`scheme://...` or SSH `user@host:path`).\n/// - `OwnerName(owner, name)` — `owner/name` shorthand;\n///   resolves to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.\n/// - `Path` — local path with explicit prefix\n///   (`./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, or bare `~`). Path text is preserved\n///   literally; tilde expansion is the consumer's responsibility.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Target {\n    Url(String),\n    OwnerName(String, String),\n    Path(PathBuf),\n}\n\n/// Parse a positional `<TARGET>` argument into one of the three\n/// shapes.\n///\n/// Detection order (path forms first, then URL, then shorthand):\n///\n/// - Path forms: bare `~`, or starts with `./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`.\n/// - URL: contains `://`, or SSH-style `user@host:path` (an `@`\n///   followed somewhere by `:`).\n/// - `owner/name` shorthand: exactly one `/`, both sides non-empty,\n///   no path or URL indicators.\n///\n/// Errors on bare `.`, bare names without a prefix, and empty input.\npub fn parse_target(s: &str) -> Result<Target, String> {\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(\"empty target\".into());\n    }\n\n    if s == \"~\"\n        || s.starts_with(\"./\")\n        || s.starts_with(\"../\")\n        || s.starts_with('/')\n        || s.starts_with(\"~/\")\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::Path(PathBuf::from(s)));\n    }\n\n    if s.contains(\"://\") {\n        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));\n    }\n    if let Some(at) = s.find('@')\n        && s[at + 1..].contains(':')\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));\n    }\n\n    if s.matches('/').count() == 1\n        && let Some((owner, name)) = s.split_once('/')\n        && !owner.is_empty()\n        && !name.is_empty()\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::OwnerName(owner.to_string(), name.to_string()));\n    }\n\n    if s == \".\" {\n        return Err(\n            \"bare '.' is not a valid target — use './' to refer to cwd explicitly\".into(),\n        );\n    }\n\n    Err(format!(\n        \"'{s}' is not a recognized target — expected URL, owner/name shorthand, or path prefix (./X, ../X, /X, ~/X, ~)\"\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Derive the project name from a repo URL or `owner/name` shorthand.\n///\n/// - Strips trailing `.git`.\n/// - > AGENT

`src/repo_url.rs` written (~290 lines, 21 tests). Let-chains are project-style, so consistent.

Summary:
- `Target` enum: `Url(String)`, `OwnerName(String, String)`, `Path(PathBuf)`. Path text preserved literally; tilde expansion is the consumer's job.
- `parse_target`: path forms first (avoids URL-detection false positives on `@`/`:` in paths), then URL (`://` or `@...:` SSH), then `owner/name`. Errors on bare `.`, bare names, and empty input.
- `derive_name`: consolidated from clone's `derive_name` + init's `derive_name_from_url` (used init's cleaner single-rsplit form, kept clone's more general error wording).
- `resolve_url`: unchanged from clone.
- `derive_session_url`: unchanged (clone and init had identical impls).
- 21 tests (5 derive_name + 3 resolve_url + 5 derive_session_url + 8 parse_target covering URL/shorthand/path forms + 3 errors).

  "old_string": "/// Parse a positional `<TARGET>` argument into one of the three\n/// shapes.\n///\n/// Detection order (path forms first, then URL, then shorthand):\n///\n/// - Path forms: bare `~`, or starts with `./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`.\n/// - URL: contains `://`, or SSH-style `user@host:path` (an `@`\n///   followed somewhere by `:`).\n/// - `owner/name` shorthand: exactly one `/`, both sides non-empty,\n///   no path or URL indicators.\n///\n/// Errors on bare `.`, bare names without a prefix, and empty input.\npub fn parse_target(s: &str) -> Result<Target, String> {\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(\"empty target\".into());\n    }\n\n    if s == \"~\"\n        || s.starts_with(\"./\")\n        || s.starts_with(\"../\")\n        || s.starts_with('/')\n        || s.starts_with(\"~/\")\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::Path(PathBuf::from(s)));\n    }\n\n    if s.contains(\"://\") {\n        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));\n    }\n    if let Some(at) = s.find('@')\n        && s[at + 1..].contains(':')\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));\n    }\n\n    if s.matches('/').count() == 1\n        && let Some((owner, name)) = s.split_once('/')\n        && !owner.is_empty()\n        && !name.is_empty()\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::OwnerName(owner.to_string(), name.to_string()));\n    }\n\n    if s == \".\" {\n        return Err(\n            \"bare '.' is not a valid target — use './' to refer to cwd explicitly\".into(),\n        );\n    }\n\n    Err(format!(\n        \"'{s}' is not a recognized target — expected URL, owner/name shorthand, or path prefix (./X, ../X, /X, ~/X, ~)\"\n    ))\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Parse a positional `<TARGET>` argument into one of the three\n/// shapes.\n///\n/// Detection order (path forms first, then URL, then shorthand):\n///\n/// - Path forms: bare `.`, `..`, or `~`; or starts with `./`,\n///   `../`, `/`, or `~/`. `.` and `..` are POSIX cwd/parent and\n///   are unambiguous; the consumer resolves them to a real\n///   workspace name via `canonicalize` + `file_name`.\n/// - URL: contains `://`, or SSH-style `user@host:path` (an `@`\n///   followed somewhere by `:`).\n/// - `owner/name` shorthand: exactly one `/`, both sides non-empty,\n///   no path or URL indicators.\n///\n/// Errors on bare alphanumeric names (genuinely ambiguous —\n/// \"missing `./`?\" / \"missing `/name` suffix?\") and empty input.\npub fn parse_target(s: &str) -> Result<Target, String> {\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(\"empty target\".into());\n    }\n\n    if s == \".\"\n        || s == \"..\"\n        || s == \"~\"\n        || s.starts_with(\"./\")\n        || s.starts_with(\"../\")\n        || s.starts_with('/')\n        || s.starts_with(\"~/\")\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::Path(PathBuf::from(s)));\n    }\n\n    if s.contains(\"://\") {\n        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));\n    }\n    if let Some(at) = s.find('@')\n        && s[at + 1..].contains(':')\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));\n    }\n\n    if s.matches('/').count() == 1\n        && let Some((owner, name)) = s.split_once('/')\n        && !owner.is_empty()\n        && !name.is_empty()\n    {\n        return Ok(Target::OwnerName(owner.to_string(), name.to_string()));\n    }\n\n    Err(format!(\n        \"'{s}' is not a recognized target — expected URL, owner/name shorthand, or path prefix (./X, ../X, /X, ~/X, ~)\"\n    ))\n}"

continue, but by the time we're complete with changes for init and clone they and all of the subcommands should have the same semantics for the same situation, speaking of the "per chores-08, Pat errors .." flag. Maybe thats a bug in chores-08?

> AGENT

You're right — I think it's a bug in chores-08, or at least an overrestriction.

Reasoning: `git clone` natively accepts a local path as the source URL (`git clone /tmp/foo.git mydir` works). For vc-x1, `vc-x1 clone /tmp/foo.git` would naturally mean "clone the local bare repo at this path" — useful for local fixtures, CI scratch dirs, integration tests against bare repos. There's no good reason to reject it.

The init/clone unification then becomes:
- **Same TARGET parse rules everywhere** (URL, owner/name, Path all accepted by `parse_target`).
- **Semantics per command** — naturally differ because the commands' purposes differ:
  - init: TARGET = destination (where to create)
  - clone: TARGET = source (what to copy)
- For clone with Path: pass it as the URL to `git clone`. `derive_name` already handles paths (`/tmp/foo.git` → `foo`).
- For `--scope=code,bot` with Path: try to clone `derive_session_url(path)` (e.g. `/tmp/foo.claude.git`); existing graceful skip if missing — same shape as today's URL-form behavior.

Cross-subcommand consistency this preserves:
- Same parser, same enum.
- Same flag vocabulary (`--scope`, `--dry-run`, etc.).
- Same error messages on shared failure modes ("target dir already exists", "missing prefix", etc.).

Cross-subcommand difference this preserves:
- Per-command semantic role of TARGET (destination vs source vs whatever later subcommands need).

That's the right kind of consistency, I think — uniform input handling, command-specific output behavior. Forcing init and clone to do the *same thing* with a Path would be wrong; forcing them to *accept the same Path syntax* is right.

**Updated -2 plan:**
- Drop the "Path errors for clone" branch.
- Path → use as URL directly (`git clone <path> <target_dir>`).
- Update chores-08 in this commit (same drift-fix-now principle as before).

Sound right? If so I'll proceed.

42	
43	- **URL** — `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`,
44	  `https://...(.git)?` (detected by `://` or SSH
45	  `<host>:<path>` shape with `@`).
46	- **`owner/name` shorthand** — single `/`, no path prefix;
47	  resolved to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
48	- **Path-prefixed** — `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`,
49	  bare `.`, or bare `..`. Path IS the target; last component
50	  is the workspace name (consumer canonicalizes `.` / `..`
51	  to a real basename via `canonicalize` + `file_name`).
52	  Bare alphanumeric `NAME` is an error (genuinely ambiguous
53	  — "missing `./`?" / "missing `/name` suffix?").
54	
55	`[NAME]`:
56	
57	- For URL / `owner/name` forms: overrides the derived
58	  destination dir name. `vc-x1 clone owner/foo my-name`
59	  clones into `./my-name/` instead of `./foo/`.
60	- For path-prefix form: error if combined (path already
61	  specifies the full target).
62	- Path-form for clone: error (clone needs a remote URL; see
63	  "Operations" for clone's target rules).
64	
65	`--scope`:
66	
67	- `code,bot` (default): both repos, dual-repo layout.
68	- `por`: single repo, no `.vc-config.toml` written.
69	- `code` / `bot` standalone: error. Reason — these are
70	  config-lookup keywords; init has no config to look up
71	  against, and clone's simplification omits them too. The
72	  manual decomposition (clone code as POR, clone bot as
73	  POR, place at `.claude/`, run `vc-x1 symlink`) covers the
74	  rare cases where a user wants the dual layout composed
75	  by hand.
76	
77	`--private`: only meaningful for init when creating a new
78	GitHub repo. Sets visibility at `gh repo create`. Silently
79	warn-and-ignore if the remote already exists. Errors on
80	clone (clone never creates a remote).
81	
82	`--dry-run`: validate the operation as far as possible
83	without side effects. Print what would be done.
84	
85	### Operations
86	
87	**Init** is *smart* — it detects the target dir's state and
88	chooses the right operation.
89	
90	| Target state | `--scope=code,bot` | `--scope=por` |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| empty / nonexistent | create dual-repo from scratch | create POR |
93	| POR (jj+git, no config) | upgrade to dual | error (already POR) |
94	| POR (git only, no `.jj/`) | bootstrap `jj git init`, then upgrade | error (already POR-shape) |
95	| code POR + `.claude/` peer POR (configs missing) | write configs only | error |
96	| dual-repo (configs present) | error (already there) | error (downgrade) |
97	| single-repo (illegal shape) | error | error |
98	| anything else (random files, etc.) | error with diagnostic | error with diagnostic |
99	
100	**Clone** is *dumb* — it just clones URLs into target dirs.
101	
102	| `--scope=por` | clone the URL into `<target>` |
103	| `--scope=code,bot` | clone code URL into `<target>`, derive bot URL (`<URL>.claude`), clone into `<target>/.claude/`, then create symlink via `vc-x1 symlink` |
104	
105	For both clone modes: target must NOT exist (`vc-x1 clone`
106	errors if anything is there). Use `vc-x1 sync` to update an
107	existing checkout.
108	
109	`.vc-config.toml` files for the dual-repo case are *tracked
110	content in the remotes*, not files clone writes. They ride
111	along with the clone. If a remote doesn't have them
112	committed, `vc-x1 init <path> --scope=code,bot` from inside
113	the cloned dir handles the config-only upgrade case (see
114	init's state table above).
115	
116	`--scope=code,bot` is implemented as in-process composition
117	of the `--scope=por` primitive (called twice: once for code
118	URL, once for derived bot URL) plus a `symlink::create`
119	call. No subprocess overhead.
120	
121	If init or clone fails partway through, manual cleanup is
122	required (no rollback).
123	
124	### Example layouts (local repos)
125	
126	cwd = `~/prgs`
127	
128	`vc-init test-repos/tf1 --scope=code,bot`
129	`vc-init test-repos/tf1`

3	use clap::Args;

10	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
11	pub struct CloneArgs {
12	    /// GitHub repo (owner/name) or git URL
13	    #[arg(value_name = "REPO")]
14	    pub repo: String,
15	
16	    /// Local directory name [default: derived from REPO]
17	    #[arg(value_name = "NAME")]
18	    pub name: Option<String>,
19	
20	    /// Parent directory to clone into [default: cwd]
21	    #[arg(long)]
22	    pub dir: Option<PathBuf>,
23	
24	    /// Dry run — show what would be done without executing
25	    #[arg(long)]
26	    pub dry_run: bool,
27	}
28	
29	pub fn clone_repo(args: &CloneArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
30	    log::debug!("clone: enter");
31	    let parent_dir = match &args.dir {
32	        Some(d) => d.clone(),
33	        None => std::env::current_dir()?,
34	    };
35	
36	    let name = match &args.name {
37	        Some(n) => n.clone(),
38	        None => derive_name(&args.repo)?,
39	    };
40	    let project_dir = parent_dir.join(&name);
41	    let session_dir = project_dir.join(".claude");
42	    let url = resolve_url(&args.repo);
43	
44	    let session_url = derive_session_url(&url);
45	
46	    if args.dry_run {
47	        info!("Dry run — would execute:");
48	        info!("  1. git clone {url} {name}");
49	        info!("  2. git clone {session_url} {name}/.claude");
50	        info!("  3. jj git init --colocate in {name}/");
51	        info!("  4. jj git init --colocate in {name}/.claude/");
52	        info!("  5. Create Claude Code symlink");
53	        return Ok(());
54	    }
55	
56	    // Preflight
57	    if project_dir.exists() {
58	        return Err(format!("'{}' already exists", project_dir.display()).into());
59	    }
60	
61	    run("jj", &["--version"], Path::new(".")).map_err(|_| "jj is not installed")?;
62	
63	    // Step 1: Clone code repo
64	    let project_str = project_dir
65	        .to_str()
66	        .ok_or("project path is not valid UTF-8")?;
67	    info!("Step 1: Cloning {url}...");
68	    run("git", &["clone", &url, project_str], &parent_dir)?;
69	
70	    // Step 2: Clone session repo
71	    let session_str = session_dir
72	        .to_str()
73	        .ok_or("session path is not valid UTF-8")?;
74	    info!("Step 2: Cloning {session_url}...");
75	    match run("git", &["clone", &session_url, session_str], &parent_dir) {
76	        Ok(_) => {}
77	        Err(e) => {
78	            info!("Step 2: No session repo found ({e}) — skipping");
79	        }
80	    }
81	
82	    // Step 3: jj git init --colocate in code repo. Note: colocate after a
83	    // plain `git clone` does NOT auto-establish bookmark tracking — jj
84	    // emits a hint to run `jj bookmark track …`. We do that explicitly,
85	    // then assert via verify_tracking.
86	    info!("Step 3: Initializing jj in code repo...");
87	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &project_dir)?;
88	    run(
89	        "jj",
90	        &["bookmark", "track", "main", "--remote=origin"],
91	        &project_dir,
92	    )?;
93	    crate::common::verify_tracking(&project_dir, "main")?;
94	
95	    // Step 4: jj git init --colocate in session repo (if cloned)
96	    if session_dir.exists() {
97	        info!("Step 4: Initializing jj in session repo...");
98	        run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &session_dir)?;
99	        run(
100	            "jj",
101	            &["bookmark", "track", "main", "--remote=origin"],
102	            &session_dir,
103	        )?;
104	        crate::common::verify_tracking(&session_dir, "main")?;
105	    } else {
106	        info!("Step 4: No session repo — skipping jj init");
107	    }
108	
109	    // Step 5: Create Claude Code symlink
110	    info!("Step 5: Creating Claude Code symlink...");
111	    let symlink_dir = {
112	        let home =
113	            std::env::var("HOME").map_err(|_| "HOME environment variable not set".to_string())?;
114	        PathBuf::from(home).join(".claude").join("projects")
115	    };
116	
117	    let sl = symlink::SymLink::new(&project_dir, Path::new(".claude"), &symlink_dir)?;
118	    sl.create(false)?;
119	
120	    info!("");
121	    info!("Done! Project cloned to {}", project_dir.display());
122	    info!("  Code repo:    {project_str}");
123	    info!("  Session repo: {}", session_dir.display());
124	    info!(
125	        "  Symlink:      {} -> {}",
126	        sl.symlink_path.display(),
127	        sl.abs_target.display()
128	    );
129	
130	    log::debug!("clone: exit");
131	    Ok(())
132	}
