  "content": "//! `vc-x1 clone` — clone a repo (URL or local path) into a workspace.\n//!\n//! - `--scope=code,bot` (default): dual-repo layout — clones code,\n//!   derives bot source (`<source>.claude`), clones bot into\n//!   `<target>/.claude`, creates the Claude Code symlink.\n//! - `--scope=por`: single repo into `<target>`. No `.claude/`,\n//!   no symlink.\n//!\n//! TARGET shapes (all routed through `parse_target`): URL,\n//! `owner/name` shorthand, or a local path (`./X`, `/X`, `~/X`,\n//! `.`, `..`). Path-form is symmetric with `git clone /local/bare.git`\n//! — useful for fixtures and CI scratch dirs.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse clap::Args;\nuse log::info;\n\nuse crate::common::run;\nuse crate::repo_url::{Target, derive_name, derive_session_url, parse_target, resolve_url};\nuse crate::symlink;\n\n/// Topology choice for `vc-x1 clone --scope`.\n///\n/// - `CodeBot` (default) — clone the dual-repo layout: code into\n///   target dir, bot derived source into `target/.claude`, plus\n///   the Claude Code symlink.\n/// - `Por` — clone a single repo (Plain Old Repo) into target dir;\n///   no `.claude/`, no symlink.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CloneScope {\n    CodeBot,\n    Por,\n}\n\n/// Parse the `--scope` value for clone.\n///\n/// - Accepts `code,bot` / `bot,code` (commutative) and `por`.\n/// - Standalone `code` or `bot` errors — clone has no\n///   config-driven defaults to look up against; the manual\n///   decomposition (two `--scope=por` clones + `vc-x1 symlink`)\n///   covers the rare cases where a user wants the dual layout\n///   composed by hand.\npub fn parse_clone_scope(s: &str) -> Result<CloneScope, String> {\n    match s {\n        \"code,bot\" | \"bot,code\" => Ok(CloneScope::CodeBot),\n        \"por\" => Ok(CloneScope::Por),\n        \"code\" | \"bot\" => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not valid for clone — use 'code,bot' (dual) or 'por' (single)\"\n        )),\n        _ => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not recognized — expected 'code,bot' or 'por'\"\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// CLI args for `vc-x1 clone`.\n#[derive(Args, Debug)]\npub struct CloneArgs {\n    /// Source to clone — URL, owner/name shorthand, or local path.\n    ///\n    /// - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`\n    /// - owner/name shorthand: resolves to\n    ///   `git@github.com:owner/name.git`\n    /// - Local path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..`\n    ///   (passed directly to `git clone`)\n    #[arg(value_name = \"TARGET\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub target: String,\n\n    /// Destination dir name in cwd [default: derived from TARGET]\n    #[arg(value_name = \"NAME\")]\n    pub name: Option<String>,\n\n    /// What to clone: `code,bot` (dual, default) or `por` (single).\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        short,\n        value_name = \"SCOPE\",\n        value_parser = parse_clone_scope,\n        default_value = \"code,bot\"\n    )]\n    pub scope: CloneScope,\n\n    /// Dry run — show what would be done without executing.\n    #[arg(long)]\n    pub dry_run: bool,\n}\n\n/// Top-level clone driver.\n///\n/// - Resolves TARGET to a concrete clone source (URL or path).\n/// - Determines destination dir name (`[NAME]` override or\n///   `derive_name(TARGET)`).\n/// - Pre-checks target dir doesn't exist.\n/// - Dispatches to `clone_one` (POR) or `clone_dual` (code,bot).\npub fn clone_repo(args: &CloneArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    log::debug!(\"clone: enter\");\n\n    let parsed = parse_target(&args.target)?;\n    let source = match parsed {\n        Target::Url(u) => u,\n        Target::OwnerName(o, n) => resolve_url(&format!(\"{o}/{n}\")),\n        Target::Path(p) => p\n            .to_str()\n            .ok_or(\"path is not valid UTF-8\")?\n            .to_string(),\n    };\n\n    let name = match &args.name {\n        Some(n) => n.clone(),\n        None => derive_name(&args.target)?,\n    };\n    let parent_dir = std::env::current_dir()?;\n    let project_dir = parent_dir.join(&name);\n\n    if project_dir.exists() {\n        return Err(format!(\"'{}' already exists\", project_dir.display()).into());\n    }\n\n    if args.dry_run {\n        info!(\"Dry run — would execute:\");\n        match args.scope {\n            CloneScope::Por => {\n                info!(\"  1. git clone {source} {name}\");\n                info!(\"  2. jj git init --colocate in {name}/\");\n            }\n            CloneScope::CodeBot => {\n                let session_source = derive_session_url(&source);\n                info!(\"  1. git clone {source} {name}\");\n                info!(\"  2. git clone {session_source} {name}/.claude\");\n                info!(\"  3. jj git init --colocate in {name}/\");\n                info!(\"  4. jj git init --colocate in {name}/.claude/\");\n                info!(\"  5. Create Claude Code symlink\");\n            }\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    run(\"jj\", &[\"--version\"], Path::new(\".\")).map_err(|_| \"jj is not installed\")?;\n\n    match args.scope {\n        CloneScope::Por => {\n            clone_one(&source, &project_dir, &parent_dir)?;\n            info!(\"\");\n            info!(\"Done! Project cloned to {}\", project_dir.display());\n            info!(\"  Code repo: {}\", project_dir.display());\n        }\n        CloneScope::CodeBot => clone_dual(&source, &project_dir, &parent_dir)?,\n    }\n\n    log::debug!(\"clone: exit\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Clone a single repo: `git clone` + `jj git init --colocate` +\n/// bookmark tracking + tracking verification.\n///\n/// - `source` is the clone source (URL or local path).\n/// - `target_dir` is the destination working repo location.\n/// - `parent_dir` is `target_dir`'s parent (cwd for the\n///   `git clone` subprocess).\nfn clone_one(\n    source: &str,\n    target_dir: &Path,\n    parent_dir: &Path,\n) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let target_str = target_dir\n        .to_str()\n        .ok_or(\"target path is not valid UTF-8\")?;\n    info!(\"Cloning {source} → {target_str}...\");\n    run(\"git\", &[\"clone\", source, target_str], parent_dir)?;\n\n    // jj colocate after a plain `git clone` does NOT auto-establish\n    // bookmark tracking — jj emits a hint to run `jj bookmark track`.\n    // Do it explicitly, then assert via verify_tracking.\n    info!(\"Initializing jj at {target_str}...\");\n    run(\"jj\", &[\"git\", \"init\", \"--colocate\"], target_dir)?;\n    run(\n        \"jj\",\n        &[\"bookmark\", \"track\", \"main\", \"--remote=origin\"],\n        target_dir,\n    )?;\n    crate::common::verify_tracking(target_dir, \"main\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Clone the dual-repo layout: code via `clone_one`, bot via a\n/// graceful-skip variant (`git clone` may fail if the derived\n/// `<source>.claude` URL has no remote), then create the Claude\n/// Code symlink iff the bot side cloned.\n///\n/// - The graceful-skip behavior matches pre-0.41.1-2 clone — useful\n///   when only the code side has been pushed but the bot remote\n///   hasn't been provisioned yet.\nfn clone_dual(\n    code_source: &str,\n    target_dir: &Path,\n    parent_dir: &Path,\n) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let session_source = derive_session_url(code_source);\n    let session_dir = target_dir.join(\".claude\");\n\n    // Code side\n    clone_one(code_source, target_dir, parent_dir)?;\n\n    // Bot side — graceful skip on git-clone failure, then finalize\n    // (jj init + tracking) only if clone succeeded.\n    let session_str = session_dir\n        .to_str()\n        .ok_or(\"session path is not valid UTF-8\")?;\n    info!(\"Cloning {session_source} → {session_str}...\");\n    let bot_cloned = match run(\n        \"git\",\n        &[\"clone\", &session_source, session_str],\n        parent_dir,\n    ) {\n        Ok(_) => {\n            info!(\"Initializing jj at {session_str}...\");\n            run(\"jj\", &[\"git\", \"init\", \"--colocate\"], &session_dir)?;\n            run(\n                \"jj\",\n                &[\"bookmark\", \"track\", \"main\", \"--remote=origin\"],\n                &session_dir,\n            )?;\n            crate::common::verify_tracking(&session_dir, \"main\")?;\n            true\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            info!(\"No session repo ({e}) — skipping\");\n            false\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Symlink — only if bot was cloned.\n    if bot_cloned {\n        info!(\"Creating Claude Code symlink...\");\n        let symlink_dir = {\n            let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\")\n                .map_err(|_| \"HOME environment variable not set\".to_string())?;\n            PathBuf::from(home).join(\".claude\").join(\"projects\")\n        };\n        let sl = symlink::SymLink::new(target_dir, Path::new(\".claude\"), &symlink_dir)?;\n        sl.create(false)?;\n        info!(\"\");\n        info!(\"Done! Project cloned to {}\", target_dir.display());\n        info!(\"  Code repo:    {}\", target_dir.display());\n        info!(\"  Session repo: {}\", session_dir.display());\n        info!(\n            \"  Symlink:      {} -> {}\",\n            sl.symlink_path.display(),\n            sl.abs_target.display()\n        );\n    } else {\n        info!(\"\");\n        info!(\n            \"Done! Project cloned to {} (code only — no session repo)\",\n            target_dir.display()\n        );\n        info!(\"  Code repo: {}\", target_dir.display());\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::{Cli, Commands};\n    use clap::Parser;\n\n    fn parse(args: &[&str]) -> CloneArgs {\n        let cli = Cli::try_parse_from(args).unwrap();\n        match cli.command {\n            Commands::Clone(a) => a,\n            _ => panic!(\"expected Clone\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_err(args: &[&str]) -> String {\n        Cli::try_parse_from(args).unwrap_err().to_string()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn defaults() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"owner/repo\");\n        assert!(args.name.is_none());\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::CodeBot);\n        assert!(!args.dry_run);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_name() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"my-dir\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"owner/repo\");\n        assert_eq!(args.name.as_deref(), Some(\"my-dir\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_opts() {\n        let args = parse(&[\n            \"vc-x1\",\n            \"clone\",\n            \"owner/repo\",\n            \"my-dir\",\n            \"--scope\",\n            \"por\",\n            \"--dry-run\",\n        ]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"owner/repo\");\n        assert_eq!(args.name.as_deref(), Some(\"my-dir\"));\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::Por);\n        assert!(args.dry_run);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn missing_target() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"TARGET\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_short_flag() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"-s\", \"por\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::Por);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_bot_code_commutative() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"bot,code\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::CodeBot);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_code_alone_errors() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"code\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"not valid for clone\"), \"got: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_bot_alone_errors() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"bot\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"not valid for clone\"), \"got: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_unknown_errors() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"xyz\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"not recognized\"), \"got: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn target_path_form_accepted() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"/tmp/foo.git\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"/tmp/foo.git\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn target_relative_path_form_accepted() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"./bare.git\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"./bare.git\");\n    }\n\n    // Unit tests for derive_name / resolve_url / derive_session_url\n    // live in src/repo_url.rs alongside the lifted functions.\n}\n"

I bundled tasks #13-#16 (CloneScope, CloneArgs reshape, clone_one/clone_dual, tests) into one full-file rewrite since they're tightly coupled and partial states wouldn't compile. The whole `clone.rs` is now ~340 lines.

**Highlights:**

- `CloneScope { CodeBot, Por }` + `parse_clone_scope` (commutative `code,bot`/`bot,code`; standalone `code`/`bot` error).
- `CloneArgs`: `target` positional (was `repo`), `--scope -s` (default `code,bot`), `--dry-run`. Dropped `--dir`.
- `clone_repo` body: `parse_target` dispatch — `Url` passes through, `OwnerName` resolves via `resolve_url`, `Path` passes through as-is (git-clone-friendly).
- `clone_one`: primitive — git clone + jj init + bookmark track + verify. No final "Done!" message; caller frames it.
- `clone_dual`: orchestrator — `clone_one(code)` + bot side with graceful skip on git-clone failure (matches pre-0.41.1-2 behavior) + symlink iff bot cloned.
- 11 tests: 4 adapted (defaults, with_name, all_opts uses `--scope`, missing_target), 7 new (scope short flag, commutative, code/bot/unknown errors, two path-form acceptance tests).

Verified externally that no other source file references CloneArgs's old `repo`/`dir` fields (other matches are different structs in init/validate_desc/fix_desc/finalize).

If you'd prefer this split into smaller reviews — happy to revert and chunk it by section. Otherwise:

> AGENT

Confirmed: `sync.rs:990` already uses `jj git clone --colocate` in its test harness. clone.rs was the outlier carrying forward the older pattern.

**Proposed rework:**

1. **`clone_one` uses `jj git clone --colocate`** — drops 3 subprocesses (`git clone` + `jj git init --colocate` + `jj bookmark track`) to 1. The verify_tracking call stays as a sanity assert.

2. **`clone_dual` = `clone_one(code) + clone_one(bot) + symlink::create`** — exactly the shape you sketched. Architecturally cleaner.

3. **Drop the graceful-skip on bot-side** — this is the behavior change to flag. With `--scope=por` available as an explicit opt-out, `--scope=code,bot` should require both sides to succeed. Old behavior silently skipped if the `.claude` remote was missing; new behavior fails loudly. Cleaner contract; users who actually want code-only have `--scope=por`.

The graceful-skip workflow (clone when bot remote not yet provisioned) is uncommon — and once `-4` lands the POR-upgrade-to-dual path in init, that's the canonical way to grow code-only into dual without needing clone to handle it.

Want me to apply these changes? It'll be another full `clone.rs` rewrite (smaller than the last one — ~50 lines lighter without the graceful-skip branch and with the simpler clone_one).

  "content": "//! `vc-x1 clone` — clone a repo (URL or local path) into a workspace.\n//!\n//! - `--scope=code,bot` (default): dual-repo layout — clones code,\n//!   derives bot source (`<source>.claude`), clones bot into\n//!   `<target>/.claude`, creates the Claude Code symlink. Both\n//!   sides must succeed.\n//! - `--scope=por`: single repo into `<target>`. No `.claude/`,\n//!   no symlink.\n//!\n//! TARGET shapes (all routed through `parse_target`): URL,\n//! `owner/name` shorthand, or a local path (`./X`, `/X`, `~/X`,\n//! `.`, `..`). Path-form is symmetric with `git clone /local/bare.git`\n//! — useful for fixtures and CI scratch dirs.\n//!\n//! `clone_one` and `clone_dual` are `pub(crate)` so init's `-3`\n//! reshape can reuse them for the \"URL exists → clone\" preflight\n//! path (per `notes/chores-08.md > init + clone redesign`).\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse clap::Args;\nuse log::info;\n\nuse crate::common::run;\nuse crate::repo_url::{Target, derive_name, derive_session_url, parse_target, resolve_url};\nuse crate::symlink;\n\n/// Topology choice for `vc-x1 clone --scope`.\n///\n/// - `CodeBot` (default) — clone the dual-repo layout: code into\n///   target dir, bot derived source into `target/.claude`, plus\n///   the Claude Code symlink. Both sides must succeed.\n/// - `Por` — clone a single repo (Plain Old Repo) into target dir;\n///   no `.claude/`, no symlink.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CloneScope {\n    CodeBot,\n    Por,\n}\n\n/// Parse the `--scope` value for clone.\n///\n/// - Accepts `code,bot` / `bot,code` (commutative) and `por`.\n/// - Standalone `code` or `bot` errors — clone has no\n///   config-driven defaults to look up against; the manual\n///   decomposition (two `--scope=por` clones + `vc-x1 symlink`)\n///   covers the rare cases where a user wants the dual layout\n///   composed by hand.\npub fn parse_clone_scope(s: &str) -> Result<CloneScope, String> {\n    match s {\n        \"code,bot\" | \"bot,code\" => Ok(CloneScope::CodeBot),\n        \"por\" => Ok(CloneScope::Por),\n        \"code\" | \"bot\" => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not valid for clone — use 'code,bot' (dual) or 'por' (single)\"\n        )),\n        _ => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not recognized — expected 'code,bot' or 'por'\"\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// CLI args for `vc-x1 clone`.\n#[derive(Args, Debug)]\npub struct CloneArgs {\n    /// Source to clone — URL, owner/name shorthand, or local path.\n    ///\n    /// - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`\n    /// - owner/name shorthand: resolves to\n    ///   `git@github.com:owner/name.git`\n    /// - Local path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..`\n    ///   (passed directly to `git clone`)\n    #[arg(value_name = \"TARGET\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub target: String,\n\n    /// Destination dir name in cwd [default: derived from TARGET]\n    #[arg(value_name = \"NAME\")]\n    pub name: Option<String>,\n\n    /// What to clone: `code,bot` (dual, default) or `por` (single).\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        short,\n        value_name = \"SCOPE\",\n        value_parser = parse_clone_scope,\n        default_value = \"code,bot\"\n    )]\n    pub scope: CloneScope,\n\n    /// Dry run — show what would be done without executing.\n    #[arg(long)]\n    pub dry_run: bool,\n}\n\n/// Top-level clone driver.\n///\n/// - Resolves TARGET to a concrete clone source (URL or path).\n/// - Determines destination dir name (`[NAME]` override or\n///   `derive_name(TARGET)`).\n/// - Pre-checks target dir doesn't exist.\n/// - Dispatches to `clone_one` (POR) or `clone_dual` (code,bot).\npub fn clone_repo(args: &CloneArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    log::debug!(\"clone: enter\");\n\n    let parsed = parse_target(&args.target)?;\n    let source = match parsed {\n        Target::Url(u) => u,\n        Target::OwnerName(o, n) => resolve_url(&format!(\"{o}/{n}\")),\n        Target::Path(p) => p\n            .to_str()\n            .ok_or(\"path is not valid UTF-8\")?\n            .to_string(),\n    };\n\n    let name = match &args.name {\n        Some(n) => n.clone(),\n        None => derive_name(&args.target)?,\n    };\n    let parent_dir = std::env::current_dir()?;\n    let project_dir = parent_dir.join(&name);\n\n    if project_dir.exists() {\n        return Err(format!(\"'{}' already exists\", project_dir.display()).into());\n    }\n\n    if args.dry_run {\n        info!(\"Dry run — would execute:\");\n        match args.scope {\n            CloneScope::Por => {\n                info!(\"  1. jj git clone --colocate {source} {name}\");\n            }\n            CloneScope::CodeBot => {\n                let session_source = derive_session_url(&source);\n                info!(\"  1. jj git clone --colocate {source} {name}\");\n                info!(\"  2. jj git clone --colocate {session_source} {name}/.claude\");\n                info!(\"  3. Create Claude Code symlink\");\n            }\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    run(\"jj\", &[\"--version\"], Path::new(\".\")).map_err(|_| \"jj is not installed\")?;\n\n    match args.scope {\n        CloneScope::Por => {\n            clone_one(&source, &project_dir, &parent_dir)?;\n            info!(\"\");\n            info!(\"Done! Project cloned to {}\", project_dir.display());\n            info!(\"  Code repo: {}\", project_dir.display());\n        }\n        CloneScope::CodeBot => clone_dual(&source, &project_dir, &parent_dir)?,\n    }\n\n    log::debug!(\"clone: exit\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Clone a single repo via `jj git clone --colocate` and verify\n/// bookmark tracking.\n///\n/// - `source` is the clone source (URL or local path).\n/// - `target_dir` is the destination working repo location.\n/// - `parent_dir` is the cwd for the `jj git clone` subprocess.\n///\n/// `jj git clone --colocate` does git clone + jj init + automatic\n/// bookmark tracking in one step (unlike colocate-after-bare-git-clone,\n/// which needs explicit `jj bookmark track`). The `verify_tracking`\n/// call asserts the post-clone state matches expectations.\npub(crate) fn clone_one(\n    source: &str,\n    target_dir: &Path,\n    parent_dir: &Path,\n) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let target_str = target_dir\n        .to_str()\n        .ok_or(\"target path is not valid UTF-8\")?;\n    info!(\"Cloning {source} → {target_str}...\");\n    run(\n        \"jj\",\n        &[\"git\", \"clone\", \"--colocate\", source, target_str],\n        parent_dir,\n    )?;\n    crate::common::verify_tracking(target_dir, \"main\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Orchestrate a dual-repo clone: code via `clone_one`, bot via\n/// `clone_one` (no graceful skip — `--scope=code,bot` requires\n/// both sides; users who want code-only should use `--scope=por`),\n/// then create the Claude Code symlink.\npub(crate) fn clone_dual(\n    code_source: &str,\n    target_dir: &Path,\n    parent_dir: &Path,\n) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let session_source = derive_session_url(code_source);\n    let session_dir = target_dir.join(\".claude\");\n\n    clone_one(code_source, target_dir, parent_dir)?;\n    clone_one(&session_source, &session_dir, target_dir)?;\n\n    info!(\"Creating Claude Code symlink...\");\n    let symlink_dir = {\n        let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\")\n            .map_err(|_| \"HOME environment variable not set\".to_string())?;\n        PathBuf::from(home).join(\".claude\").join(\"projects\")\n    };\n    let sl = symlink::SymLink::new(target_dir, Path::new(\".claude\"), &symlink_dir)?;\n    sl.create(false)?;\n\n    info!(\"\");\n    info!(\"Done! Project cloned to {}\", target_dir.display());\n    info!(\"  Code repo:    {}\", target_dir.display());\n    info!(\"  Session repo: {}\", session_dir.display());\n    info!(\n        \"  Symlink:      {} -> {}\",\n        sl.symlink_path.display(),\n        sl.abs_target.display()\n    );\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::{Cli, Commands};\n    use clap::Parser;\n\n    fn parse(args: &[&str]) -> CloneArgs {\n        let cli = Cli::try_parse_from(args).unwrap();\n        match cli.command {\n            Commands::Clone(a) => a,\n            _ => panic!(\"expected Clone\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_err(args: &[&str]) -> String {\n        Cli::try_parse_from(args).unwrap_err().to_string()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn defaults() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"owner/repo\");\n        assert!(args.name.is_none());\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::CodeBot);\n        assert!(!args.dry_run);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_name() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"my-dir\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"owner/repo\");\n        assert_eq!(args.name.as_deref(), Some(\"my-dir\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_opts() {\n        let args = parse(&[\n            \"vc-x1\",\n            \"clone\",\n            \"owner/repo\",\n            \"my-dir\",\n            \"--scope\",\n            \"por\",\n            \"--dry-run\",\n        ]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"owner/repo\");\n        assert_eq!(args.name.as_deref(), Some(\"my-dir\"));\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::Por);\n        assert!(args.dry_run);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn missing_target() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"TARGET\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_short_flag() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"-s\", \"por\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::Por);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_bot_code_commutative() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"bot,code\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.scope, CloneScope::CodeBot);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_code_alone_errors() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"code\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"not valid for clone\"), \"got: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_bot_alone_errors() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"bot\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"not valid for clone\"), \"got: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_unknown_errors() {\n        let err = parse_err(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"owner/repo\", \"--scope\", \"xyz\"]);\n        assert!(err.contains(\"not recognized\"), \"got: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn target_path_form_accepted() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"/tmp/foo.git\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"/tmp/foo.git\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn target_relative_path_form_accepted() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"clone\", \"./bare.git\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.target, \"./bare.git\");\n    }\n\n    // Unit tests for derive_name / resolve_url / derive_session_url\n    // live in src/repo_url.rs alongside the lifted functions.\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Reworked. Key changes:

- **`clone_one`**: now `jj git clone --colocate <src> <dest>` + `verify_tracking`. Three subprocesses → one. Tracking is automatic via jj git clone (the comment about colocate-after-bare-git-clone not auto-tracking no longer applies).
- **`clone_dual`**: literally `clone_one(code)` + `clone_one(bot)` + inline `SymLink::new` + `create`. Cleanest possible structure.
- **Graceful skip dropped**: bot side missing → error. `--scope=por` is the explicit code-only path.
- **`pub(crate)` on `clone_one` / `clone_dual`**: ready for init's -3 reuse.
- **Dry-run output simplified**: 3 lines for CodeBot (was 5), 1 for POR (was 2). Reflects the new subprocess shape.
- File ~260 lines (was ~340).

Tests unchanged — same 11.

> AGENT

Done. Three edits:

1. **`symlink.rs`**: added `pub fn install(project_dir: &Path) -> Result<SymLink>` — bundles the home-dir lookup, `SymLink::new`, `sl.create(false)`, and the "Created symlink: ..." log into one helper. Returns `SymLink` for caller-side summary printing.
2. **`clone.rs` `clone_dual`**: replaced the 7-line inline symlink construction with `let sl = symlink::install(target_dir)?;`.
3. **`clone.rs` imports**: dropped `PathBuf` (no longer constructed locally — install owns that).

`clone_dual`'s three core operations are now one-liners:
```rust
clone_one(code_source, target_dir, parent_dir)?;
clone_one(&session_source, &session_dir, target_dir)?;
let sl = symlink::install(target_dir)?;
```

Init's `-3` reshape can call all three the same way for its dual case.

The existing `vc-x1 symlink` CLI subcommand stays as-is — it handles `--symlink-dir` overrides, interactive replacement prompts, and `--list`, which don't fit the simpler "default workspace link" callsite. Documented that in `install`'s doc.

Looking at it carefully — there's a real asymmetry: `install` is "create with defaults, no prompts, no overrides"; `symlink(args)` is the full CLI with `--target` / `--symlink-dir` overrides, replace prompts, AlreadyCorrect special-casing, and `--list`. They diverge on `sl.create(true)` (mkdir target if missing) vs `sl.create(false)`. So `symlink(args)` can't directly call install — but they CAN share the default-path computation:

> AGENT

Two edits, both in symlink.rs:
1. Extracted `fn default_symlink_dir()` private helper.
2. `symlink(args)` uses it for the `args.symlink_dir == None` case (replaced 5 lines with 1).
3. `install` also uses it (already did internally; now shares the helper).

The bigger consolidation isn't possible without contortion — `symlink(args)` needs to inspect `sl.action` and prompt *between* `SymLink::new` and `sl.create`, which `install` can't expose without becoming a multi-step API. They share `SymLink::new` (the real primitive) and now `default_symlink_dir`.

Conceptually: `install` : `symlink(args)` :: `clone_one` : `vc-x1 clone --scope=por`. Each pair shares the core primitive (`SymLink::new` / `jj git clone`) but adds different layers (defaults+create / overrides+prompts+create+list).

Title: `refactor: clone reshape + shared symlink::install (0.41.1-2)`

Body:
```
Reshape clone CLI surface to match the unified <TARGET> + [NAME]
shape designed in chores-08, refactor into clone_one / clone_dual
primitives via `jj git clone --colocate`, and lift symlink creation
into a shared `symlink::install` helper that init now uses too.

- Cargo.toml: 0.41.1-0 → 0.41.1-2.
- src/clone.rs: full reshape — `CloneScope { CodeBot, Por }`,
  commutative `parse_clone_scope`, `<TARGET>` + `[NAME]` positionals
  (drop `--dir`), `--scope` (`-s`) with default `code,bot`, dispatch
  via `parse_target` (URL / owner-name / Path). `clone_one` uses
  `jj git clone --colocate` (one subprocess vs three). `clone_dual`
  is three one-liners: clone code, clone bot, `symlink::install`.
- src/symlink.rs: extract `default_symlink_dir()` + new
  `pub fn install(project_dir)` — silent helper used by both
  clone_dual and init.
- src/init.rs: Step 11 collapses 6 inline lines to
  `Some(symlink::install(&plan.project_dir)?)`.
- notes/chores-08.md: lift Path-form-for-clone restriction (clone
  now accepts local-path sources, symmetric with `git clone /local/bare.git`);
  clarify `[NAME]` semantics per init/clone; update Operations
  table.
- notes/todo.md: 0.41.1-2 marker.

ochid: /.claude/<chid>
```

584	            }

590	            }

> AGENT

This is a major reshape (init.rs is 2263 lines, ~800 lines of tests using the old flag surface). Before I dive in, let me share the proposed -3 scope so we can confirm direction.

**Proposed -3 scope:**

1. **InitArgs surface** — drop `--owner`, `--dir`, `--repo-local`, `--repo-remote`; keep `--private`, `--dry-run`, `--use-template`, `--push-retries`, `--push-retry-delay`. Replace bare-`name` positional with `<TARGET>` + optional `[NAME]`. Add `--scope code,bot|por` (replacing `code|bot|code,bot`).

2. **`parse_target` dispatch** in `plan_init`:
   - `Url(u)` → maps to old `plan_external_remote` (URL is remote; workspace at `cwd/<derived-name>`; `[NAME]` overrides derived).
   - `OwnerName(o, n)` → `git@github.com:o/n.git` URL, then same as Url path; workspace at `cwd/<n>` (or `cwd/<NAME>` override).
   - `Path(p)` → workspace AT `p`. `[NAME]` is rejected (path already specifies destination). For -3 (create-from-empty only), this maps to old `plan_local_fixture` semantics — bares created at `<p>/../remote*.git`. POR-upgrade lands in -4.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;

/// Load a TOML file into a flat key-value map.
///
/// Handles `[section]` headers, bare `key = "value"` pairs, comments, and
/// blank lines. Keys under a section are stored as `section.key`. Quoted
/// string values have their quotes stripped; unquoted values are stored
/// as-is.
///
/// This is intentionally minimal — just enough for `.vc-config.toml`.
pub fn toml_load(path: &Path) -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read '{}': {e}", path.display()))?;

    let mut map = HashMap::new();
    let mut section = String::new();

    for line in content.lines() {
        let trimmed = line.trim();

        // Skip blank lines and comments
        if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed.starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }

        // Section header: [name]
        if let Some(inner) = trimmed.strip_prefix('[').and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(']')) {
            section = inner.trim().to_string();
            continue;
        }

        // Key = value
        if let Some((key, value)) = trimmed.split_once('=') {
            let key = key.trim();
            let value = value.trim();

            // Strip surrounding quotes from string values
            let value = if (value.starts_with('"') && value.ends_with('"'))
                || (value.starts_with('\'') && value.ends_with('\''))

                value

32	### Command structure
33	
34	```
35	vc-x1 init  <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por] [--private] [--dry-run]
36	vc-x1 clone <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por]             [--dry-run]
37	```
38	
39	Identical surfaces modulo `--private` (init only).
40	
41	`<TARGET>` accepts:
42	
43	- **URL** — `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`,
44	  `https://...(.git)?` (detected by `://` or SSH
45	  `<host>:<path>` shape with `@`).
46	- **`owner/name` shorthand** — single `/`, no path prefix;
47	  resolved to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
48	- **Path-prefixed** — `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`,
49	  bare `.`, or bare `..`. Path IS the target; last component
50	  is the workspace name (consumer canonicalizes `.` / `..`
51	  to a real basename via `canonicalize` + `file_name`).
52	  Bare alphanumeric `NAME` is an error (genuinely ambiguous
53	  — "missing `./`?" / "missing `/name` suffix?").
54	
55	`[NAME]`:
56	
57	- **init**: URL / `owner/name` forms → overrides the derived
58	  workspace name (workspace at `cwd/<NAME>`). Path forms →
59	  error if combined (path already specifies the destination).
60	- **clone**: all forms (URL, `owner/name`, Path-as-source) →
61	  destination dir name in cwd. Without `[NAME]`, derived
62	  from the source via `derive_name`. For clone, TARGET is
63	  the *source* (URL or local repo path) and `[NAME]` is
64	  the *destination* — symmetric with `git clone <src>
65	  [<dest>]`.
66	
67	`--scope`:
68	
69	- `code,bot` (default): both repos, dual-repo layout.
70	- `por`: single repo, no `.vc-config.toml` written.
71	- `code` / `bot` standalone: error. Reason — these are
72	  config-lookup keywords; init has no config to look up
73	  against, and clone's simplification omits them too. The
74	  manual decomposition (clone code as POR, clone bot as
75	  POR, place at `.claude/`, run `vc-x1 symlink`) covers the
76	  rare cases where a user wants the dual layout composed
77	  by hand.
78	
79	`--private`: only meaningful for init when creating a new
80	GitHub repo. Sets visibility at `gh repo create`. Silently
81	warn-and-ignore if the remote already exists. Errors on
82	clone (clone never creates a remote).
83	
84	`--dry-run`: validate the operation as far as possible
85	without side effects. Print what would be done.
86	
87	### Operations
88	
89	**Init** is *smart* — it detects the target dir's state and
90	chooses the right operation.
91	
```

  "content": "//! User-level config loaded from `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`.\n//!\n//! Backs init's bare-NAME expansion (`vc-x1 init tf1` →\n//! `git@<service>:<owner>/tf1.git`). [default]\n//! remote-provider = \"github\"\n//!\n//! [github]\n//! owner = \"winksaville\"\n//! service = \"github.com\"   # optional, defaults to \"github.com\"\n//! ```\n//!\n//! `[default].remote-provider` is the selector; per-provider\n//! sections (`[github]`, future `[gitlab]`, …) carry the\n//! provider-specific fields.\n//!\n//! See `notes/chores-08.md > User config (0.41.1-3)`.\n//!\n//! - `load()` reads the file at `config_path()` (honors\n//!   `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`); missing file → empty `UserConfig`;\n//!   malformed file → fatal.\n//! - `load_from(path)` is the same machinery against a caller-\n//!   supplied path; used by tests and by `load()` itself.\n//! - `-3` lands the module standalone; `-4` wires it into init.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse crate::toml_simple;\n\n/// Resolved user config. All fields are `Option` — absent file or\n/// absent keys yield `None`. Consumers apply their own defaults\n/// (e.g. `service.unwrap_or(\"github.com\")` at the use site).\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct UserConfig {\n    /// `[default].remote-provider` — selects which `[<provider>]`\n    /// section's fields are used when expanding bare NAME.\n    pub remote_provider: Option<String>,\n\n    /// `[github].owner` — the GitHub user/org used as the implicit\n    /// owner for bare NAME on the GitHub provider.\n    pub github_owner: Option<String>,\n\n    /// `[github].service` — host portion of the SSH URL (e.g.\n    /// `github.com`, or a GHE host). Defaults at use site.\n    pub github_service: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Path to the user config file.\n///\n/// - Honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` if set (XDG Base Directory spec).\n/// - Falls back to `$HOME/.config`.\n/// - Errors if neither variable is set.\npub fn config_path() -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let base = if let Some(xdg) = std::env::var_os(\"XDG_CONFIG_HOME\") {\n        PathBuf::from(xdg)\n    } else if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n        PathBuf::from(home).join(\".config\")\n    } else {\n        return Err(\"neither $XDG_CONFIG_HOME nor $HOME is set\".into());\n    };\n    Ok(base.join(\"vc-x1\").join(\"config.toml\"))\n}\n\n/// Load the user config from the default location.\n///\n/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.\n/// - Malformed file → fatal error.\n#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: 0.41.1-4 is the first consumer; staged ahead in -3.\npub fn load() -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    load_from(&config_path()?)\n}\n\n/// Load the user config from an explicit path.\n///\n/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.\n/// - Malformed file → fatal error (propagated from `toml_simple`).\n/// - Unknown sections / keys are silently ignored\n///   (forward-compatible with future provider sections).\npub fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if !path.exists() {\n        return Ok(UserConfig::default());\n    }\n    let map = toml_simple::toml_load(path)?;\n    Ok(UserConfig {\n        remote_provider: map.get(\"default.remote-provider\").cloned(),\n        github_owner: map.get(\"github.owner\").cloned(),\n        github_service: map.get(\"github.service\").cloned(),\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::fs;\n    use tempfile::tempdir;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn missing_file_returns_default() {\n        let dir = tempdir().unwrap();\n        let path =   &path,\n            r#\"[default]\nremote-provider = \"github\"\n\n[github]\nowner = \"winksaville\"\nservice = \"github.com\"\n\"#,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        let cfg = assert_eq!(cfg.github_service.as_deref(), Some(\"github.com\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn partial_schema_owner_only() {\n        let dir = tempdir().unwrap();\n        let path = All 7 config tests pass.

Draft saved for review: approve (y/n), edit, or suggest changes.

**Files:**
- `src/config.rs` (new, ~190 lines incl. tests):
  - `UserConfig { remote_provider, github_owner, github_service }` — flat `Option<String>` fields per known key.
  - `config_path()` — `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` else `$HOME/.config`, then `vc-x1/config.toml`.
  - `load()` (with `#[allow(dead_code)]` — `-4` is first consumer) and `load_from(path)` (used by tests).
  - 7 tests: missing file, empty file, full schema, owner-only partial, provider-only partial, unknown sections ignored, comments/blank lines.
  - Reuses `toml_simple` parser; no new dependency.
- `src/main.rs` — added `mod config;` declaration alphabetically between `common` and `desc`.

**Notes:**
- I dropped the XDG_CONFIG_HOME-precedence test because env mutation in parallel unit tests is racy; the env logic is simple and direct. Happy to add a single-threaded test if you want coverage.
- Hand-rolled `cfg_tempdir(tag)` helper mirrors the existing `ws_tempdir` pattern in `common.rs` — no `tempfile` crate added.

If approved, I'll run preflight (fmt + clippy + test + install --locked) and propose the -3 commit.

14	/// Read the other repo path from a repo's `.vc-config.toml`.
15	///
16	/// Returns the `workspace.other-repo` value, which is the relative path
17	/// to the counterpart repo from the repo's directory.
18	pub fn other_repo_from_config(
19	    config: &HashMap<String, String>,
20	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
21	    toml_simple::toml_get(config, "workspace.other-repo")
22	        .cloned()
23	        .ok_or_else(|| "missing workspace.other-repo in .vc-config.toml".into())
24	}

26	/// Derive the ochid prefix from a repo's `.vc-config.toml`.
27	///
28	/// The `workspace.path` value is the repo's path relative to the workspace
29	/// root, which is exactly the ochid prefix (with a trailing `/` when the
30	/// path isn't just `/`).
31	pub fn ochid_prefix_from_config(
32	    config: &HashMap<String, String>,
33	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
34	    let ws_path = toml_simple::toml_get(config, "workspace.path")
35	        .ok_or("missing workspace.path in .vc-config.toml")?;
36	    let trimmed = ws_path.trim_end_matches('/');
37	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
38	        Ok("/".to_string())
39	    } else {
40	        Ok(format!("{trimmed}/"))
41	    }
42	}

44	/// Problems found with an ochid trailer, with details for reporting.
45	#[derive(Debug)]
46	pub struct OchidIssues {
47	    /// None if prefix is correct, Some((actual_prefix, expected_prefix)) if wrong.
48	    pub wrong_prefix: Option<(String, String)>,
49	    /// None if length is correct, Some((actual_len, expected_len)) if wrong.
50	    pub wrong_length: Option<(usize, usize)>,
51	    /// true if the bare ID does not resolve in the other repo.
52	    pub not_found: bool,
53	    /// The bare ID extracted from the ochid value.
54	    pub bare_id: String,
55	}

57	impl OchidIssues {
58	    pub fn any(&self) -> bool {
59	        self.wrong_prefix.is_some() || self.wrong_length.is_some() || self.not_found
60	    }
61	
62	    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {
63	        let mut parts = Vec::new();
64	        if let Some((ref actual, ref expected)) = self.wrong_prefix {
65	            parts.push(format!("prefix: {actual} (want {expected})"));
66	        }
67	        if let Some((actual, expected)) = self.wrong_length {
68	            parts.push(format!("len: {actual} (want {expected})"));
69	        }
70	        if self.not_found {
71	            parts.push(format!("not found: {}", self.bare_id));
72	        }
73	        parts.join(", ")
74	    }
75	}

77	/// Validate an ochid trailer value against expected prefix, length, and other repo.
78	pub fn validate_ochid(
79	    value: &str,
80	    other_prefix: &str,
81	    id_len: usize,
82	    other_workspace: &Workspace,
83	    other_repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
84	) -> OchidIssues {
85	    // Extract the actual prefix (everything before the bare ID)
86	    let bare_id = extract_bare_id(value);
87	    let actual_prefix = &value[..value.len() - bare_id.len()];
88	
89	    let wrong_prefix = if actual_prefix != other_prefix {
90	        Some((actual_prefix.to_string(), other_prefix.to_string()))
91	    } else {
92	        None
93	    };
94	
95	    let wrong_length = if bare_id.len() != id_len {
96	        Some((bare_id.len(), id_len))
97	    } else {
98	        None
99	    };
100	
101	    // Check if the ID resolves in the other repo
102	    let not_found = common::resolve_revset(other_workspace, other_repo, bare_id)
103	        .map(|ids| ids.is_empty())
104	        .unwrap_or(true); // OK: resolve failure → treat as not found
105	
106	    OchidIssues {
107	        wrong_prefix,
108	        wrong_length,
109	        not_found,
110	        bare_id: bare_id.to_string(),
111	    }
112	}

114	/// Result of searching the other repo for a matching commit by title.
115	#[derive(Debug)]
116	pub enum TitleMatch {
117	    /// No title to search for (empty description).
118	    NoTitle,
119	    /// Exactly one commit with the same title — unambiguous match.
120	    One(String),
121	    /// Multiple commits share the same title — ambiguous.
122	    Ambiguous(usize),
123	    /// No commit in the other repo has the same title.
124	    None,
125	}
126	
127	/// Find matching commits in the other repo by title (exact match).
128	pub fn find_matching_commit(
129	    commit: &jj_lib::commit::Commit,
130	    other_workspace: &Workspace,
131	    other_repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
132	) -> Result<TitleMatch, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
133	    let title = commit.description().lines().next().unwrap_or(""); // OK: obvious
134	    if title.is_empty() {
135	        return Ok(TitleMatch::NoTitle);
136	    }
137	
138	    let all_ids = common::resolve_revset(other_workspace, other_repo, "all()")?;
139	    let root_id = other_repo.store().root_commit_id().clone();
140	
141	    let mut matches = Vec::new();
142	    for cid in &all_ids {
143	        if *cid == root_id {
144	            continue;
145	        }
146	        let other_commit = other_repo.store().get_commit(cid)?;
147	        let other_title = other_commit.description().lines().next().unwrap_or(""); // OK: obvious
148	        if other_title == title {
149	            let full_hex =
150	                jj_lib::hex_util::encode_reverse_hex(other_commit.change_id().as_bytes());
151	            matches.push(full_hex);
152	        }
153	    }
154	
155	    match matches.len() {
156	        0 => Ok(TitleMatch::None),
157	        1 => {
158	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
159	            // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1
160	            Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))
161	        }
162	        n => Ok(TitleMatch::Ambiguous(n)),
163	    }
164	}

166	/// Resolve a short change ID to its full hex via the other repo.
167	pub fn resolve_full_change_id(
168	    bare_id: &str,
169	    other_workspace: &Workspace,
170	    other_repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
171	) -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
172	    if let Ok(commit_ids) = common::resolve_revset(other_workspace, other_repo, bare_id)
173	        && let Some(cid) = commit_ids.first()
174	    {
175	        let other_commit = other_repo.store().get_commit(cid)?;
176	        let full_hex = jj_lib::hex_util::encode_reverse_hex(other_commit.change_id().as_bytes());
177	        Ok(Some(full_hex))
178	    } else {
179	        Ok(None)
180	    }
181	}

183	/// Extract the bare change ID from an ochid value (strip path prefix).
184	pub fn extract_bare_id(ochid_value: &str) -> &str {
185	    if let Some(pos) = ochid_value.rfind('/') {
186	        &ochid_value[pos + 1..]
187	    } else {
188	        ochid_value
189	    }

192	/// Fix the ochid trailer in a commit description.
193	///
194	/// If `resolved_id` is provided, it replaces the bare changeID entirely
195	/// (used when the existing ID is too short to extend by truncation alone).
196	pub fn fix_ochid_in_description(
197	    desc: &str,
198	    other_prefix: &str,
199	    id_len: usize,
200	    new_title: Option<&str>,
201	    resolved_id: Option<&str>,
202	) -> String {
203	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = desc.lines().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect();
204	
205	    // Fix title if requested
206	    if let Some(title) = new_title
207	        && !lines.is_empty()
208	    {
209	        lines[0] = title.to_string();
210	    }
211	
212	    // Fix ochid trailer
213	    for line in &mut lines {
214	        let trimmed = line.trim();
215	        if let Some(value) = trimmed.strip_prefix("ochid:") {
216	            let value = value.trim();
217	            let id = if let Some(rid) = resolved_id {
218	                &rid[..rid.len().min(id_len)]
219	            } else {
220	                let bare_id = extract_bare_id(value);
221	                &bare_id[..bare_id.len().min(id_len)]
222	            };
223	            *line = format!("ochid: {other_prefix}{id}");
224	        }
225	    }
226	
227	    // Preserve trailing newline if original had one
228	    let mut result = lines.join("\n");
229	    if desc.ends_with('\n') {
230	        result.push('\n');
231	    }
232	    result
233	}
234	
235	/// Append an ochid trailer to a commit description.
236	pub fn append_ochid_trailer(
237	    desc: &str,
238	    other_prefix: &str,
239	    change_id: &str,
240	    id_len: usize,
241	) -> String {
242	    let short_id = &change_id[..change_id.len().min(id_len)];
243	    let trailer = format!("ochid: {other_prefix}{short_id}");
244	
245	    let mut result = desc.trim_end().to_string();
246	    // Add blank line before trailer if body exists, otherwise just newline
247	    if result.lines().count() > 1 {
248	        result.push('\n');
249	    } else {
250	        result.push_str("\n\n");
251	    }
252	    result.push_str(&trailer);
253	    result.push('\n');
254	    result
255	}
256	
257	/// Extract the ochid value from a description string (without needing a Commit).
258	pub fn extract_ochid_from_desc(desc: &str) -> Option<String> {
259	    for line in desc.lines() {
260	        let trimmed = line.trim();
261	        if let Some(v) = trimmed.strip_prefix("ochid:") {
262	            return Some(v.trim().to_string());
263	        }
264	    }
265	    None
266	}

200	pub struct StateLayout {
201	    /// Full path `<repo>/<state-dir>/<state-file>`.
202	    pub path: PathBuf,
203	}
204	
205	/// Read `state_dir` / `state_file` from `<repo_root>/.vc-config.toml`
206	/// under the `[push]` section, falling back to defaults (`.vc-x1`
207	/// and `push-state.toml`).
208	///
209	/// Missing config file is not an error — every workspace has the
210	/// defaults applied silently so `vc-x1 push --status` works on a
211	/// fresh clone without ceremony.
212	pub fn resolve_state_layout(repo_root: &Path) -> StateLayout {
213	    let config_path = repo_root.join(".vc-config.toml");
214	    let (dir, file) = if config_path.exists() {
215	        match toml_load(&config_path) {
216	            Ok(map) => {
217	                let dir = map
218	                    .get("push.state-dir")
219	                    .cloned()
220	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_STATE_DIR.to_string());
221	                let file = map
222	                    .get("push.state-file")
223	                    .cloned()
224	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_STATE_FILE.to_string());
225	                (dir, file)
226	            }
227	            Err(e) => {
228	                debug!("push: ignoring unparseable .vc-config.toml: {e}");
229	                (
230	                    DEFAULT_STATE_DIR.to_string(),
231	                    DEFAULT_STATE_FILE.to_string(),
232	                )
233	            }
234	        }
235	    } else {
236	        (
237	            DEFAULT_STATE_DIR.to_string(),
238	            DEFAULT_STATE_FILE.to_string(),
239	        )
240	    };
241	    let path = repo_root.join(&dir).join(&file);
242	    StateLayout { path }
243	}
244	
245	/// Persistent state for an in-progress `push` run.
246	///
247	/// Serialized as flat TOML (`key = "value"`) under the dir/file
248	/// configured in `.vc-config.toml`'s `[push]` section. Fields added
249	/// across dev steps are all `Option<_>` so older states remain
250	/// loadable — only `version` / `stage` / `bookmark` / `started_at`
251	/// are required. See the module docstring for which dev step
252	/// introduced which field.
253	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
254	pub struct PushState {
255	    /// State-file format version; must match `STATE_FORMAT_VERSION`
256	    /// to be considered readable.
257	    pub version: u32,
258	    /// The next stage to execute on resume.
259	    pub stage: Stage,
260	    /// Bookmark being advanced by this run (persisted so resume
261	    /// doesn't need `--bookmark` again).
262	    pub bookmark: String,
263	    /// ISO-8601 UTC timestamp captured when the state was first
264	    /// written. Informational — helps the user spot stale state.
265	    pub started_at: String,
266	    /// App-repo changeID captured at `message` stage (before
267	    /// `commit-app` runs). Stable across `jj commit` — becomes the
268	    /// chid of the just-committed change. Used when composing the
269	    /// `.claude` commit's ochid trailer. Added in 0.37.0-2.
270	    pub app_chid: Option<String>,
271	    /// `.claude` repo changeID used by the app-repo commit's ochid
272	    /// trailer. Either the pre-commit `@` chid (when `.claude` has
273	    /// pending changes — becomes `@-` after commit) or the current
274	    /// `@-` chid (when `.claude` is clean — stays stable). Added in
275	    /// 0.37.0-2.
276	    pub claude_chid: Option<String>,
277	    /// Whether `.claude`'s working copy had changes at `message`
278	    /// time. Decides whether `commit-claude` actually runs or
279	    /// skips. Added in 0.37.0-2.
280	    pub claude_had_changes: Option<bool>,
281	    /// `jj op` id of the app repo captured before `commit-app`. On
282	    /// failure in stages 4-6, `jj op restore` rewinds here. Added
283	    /// in 0.37.0-2.
284	    pub op_app: Option<String>,
285	    /// `jj op` id of `.claude` captured before `commit-app`. Same
286	    /// rollback target as `op_app`. Added in 0.37.0-2.
287	    pub op_claude: Option<String>,
288	    /// Composed commit title — persisted so resume doesn't need
289	    /// `--title` re-passed. Set during `message` stage from either

> AGENT

What's shared, what's not, and why:

**Already shared:** `toml_simple::toml_load(path) -> HashMap<String, String>`. Both my new `config::load_from` and every existing `.vc-config.toml` reader call it.

**What differs (intentionally):**

- **Schema** — `.vc-config.toml` has `[workspace]` (path, other-repo) and `[push]` (state-dir, state-file); user config has `[default]` and `[github]`. Disjoint, no overlap to fold.
- **API style** — there are already two patterns in the tree:
  - **Pattern A (desc_helpers, fix_desc, validate_desc)**: read `.vc-config.toml` to `HashMap` at the call site, pass map to accessors like `other_repo_from_config(&map)`. Map-typed, late access.
  - **Pattern B (push::resolve_state_layout)**: function takes `repo_root`, returns a typed `StateLayout` struct. Map-to-struct conversion baked in.
- **Error policy** — push's reader debug-logs and silently falls back to defaults on parse error (workspace files travel between users; defaults safe). User config errors fatally on parse failure (small, hand-written, typos should fail loudly). Both correct for their context.

My `config.rs` uses **Pattern B** (typed struct, fatal-on-malformed). That matches push.rs more than desc_helpers.rs.

**Refactoring opportunities (out of scope for -3, worth flagging):**

1. The desc_helpers pattern (HashMap + accessor fns) could be replaced by a typed `WorkspaceConfig` struct with a `load_from(path)` like mine. That would unify Pattern A → Pattern B everywhere. ~50 LOC change touching 3-4 files. Could be a 0.41.2 todo.
2. If we ever want `.vc-config.toml` to override user config (e.g., a workspace pinning a specific GitHub owner), that's the layered-config story we discussed earlier — but the chicken-and-egg note already pushed this past 0.41.1.

For -3 itself, I think we're in good shape — we share what makes sense (the parser) and have a consistent style with the closer-fit existing pattern (push.rs). Want me to proceed to commit, or refactor desc_helpers to Pattern B first as part of -3?

857	/// Extract the `owner/name` slug from a GitHub URL (any of the
858	/// supported forms: SSH scp-like, `ssh://`, `https://`).
859	fn github_slug_from_url(url: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
860	    let stem = url.strip_suffix(".git").unwrap_or(url);
861	    // The slug is the last two path components, `owner/name`.
862	    if let Some(path) = stem
863	        .strip_prefix("git@github.com:")
864	        .or_else(|| stem.strip_prefix("ssh://git@github.com/"))
865	        .or_else(|| stem.strip_prefix("https://github.com/"))
866	        .or_else(|| stem.strip_prefix("http://github.com/"))
867	    {
868	        let parts: Vec<&str> = path.split('/').collect();
869	        if parts.len() >= 2 {
870	            return Ok(format!(
871	                "{}/{}",
872	                parts[parts.len() - 2],
873	                parts[parts.len() - 1]
874	            ));
875	        }
876	    }
877	    Err(format!("cannot extract owner/name slug from GitHub URL '{url}'").into())
878	}

884	}

1364	/// Execute Step 8 or Step 9 for one side.
1365	///
1366	/// - Provision the remote per the plan's provisioner.
1367	/// - Add `origin` and push `main` with retry.
1368	/// - Centralizing keeps both sides' step bodies identical.
1369	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
1370	fn run_remote_step(
1371	    step_label: &str,
1372	    side_label: &str,
1373	    plan: &InitPlan,
1374	    remote_url: &str,
1375	    gh_slug: Option<&str>,
1376	    bare_path: Option<&Path>,
1377	    visibility: &str,
1378	    push_from: &Path,
1379	    args: &InitArgs,
1380	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
1381	    match &plan.provisioner {
1382	        Provisioner::GhCreate => {
1383	            // Safe: GhCreate always supplies gh_slug.
1384	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
1385	            let slug = gh_slug.unwrap(); // OK: GhCreate path always sets gh_slug
1386	            info!("{step_label}: Creating GitHub repo {slug} ({side_label})...");
1387	            debug!("create {side_label}-side remote on GitHub");
1388	            run(
1389	                "gh",
1390	                &["repo", "create", slug, visibility],
1391	                &plan.project_dir,
1392	            )?;
1393	        }
1394	        Provisioner::LocalBareInit => {
1395	            // Safe: LocalBareInit always supplies bare_path.
1396	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
1397	            let bare = bare_path.unwrap(); // OK: LocalBareInit path always sets bare_path

1426	/// Split an `owner/name` slug. Errors if the shape is wrong (no `/`
1427	/// or more than one `/`).
1428	fn split_slug(slug: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
1429	    let parts: Vec<&str> = slug.split('/').collect();
1430	    if parts.len() != 2 || parts[0].is_empty() || parts[1].is_empty() {
1431	        return Err(format!("unexpected GitHub slug '{slug}' (want 'owner/name')").into());
1432	    }
1433	    Ok((parts[0], parts[1]))
1434	}

Which flags are we dropping for init?

> AGENT

Per chores-08 spec:

**Dropped (4):**
- `--owner` (replaced by config `[github].owner` for bare-NAME, or explicit in TARGET)
- `--dir` (path now lives in TARGET path-form)
- `--repo-local` (path TARGET supersedes; fixture-mode behavior moves to path semantics)
- `--repo-remote` (URL TARGET supersedes)

**Kept (5):**
- `--private`
- `--dry-run`
- `--use-template`
- `--push-retries`
- `--push-retry-delay`

**Changed:**
- `[NAME]` positional → `<TARGET> [NAME]` positionals
- `--scope code|bot|code,bot` → `--scope code,bot|por` (matches clone)

**Net surface:**
```
vc-x1 init <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por] [--private] [--dry-run] [--use-template ...] [--push-retries N] [--push-retry-delay N]
```

> DEVELOPER

How do we indicate making a test-fixture

> AGENT

Honestly, chores-08 doesn't fully specify this — gap surfaced by your question. Two readings of path-form TARGET:

**Reading A — path TARGET = fixture (no remote, local bare origins):**
```
vc-x1 init ./tf1 --scope=code,bot
```
- Workspace at `./tf1`
- Bare origins at `./remote-code.git` + `./remote-claude.git`
- No `gh repo create`, no network — exactly the old `--repo-local /tmp/parent tf1` behavior

This matches the chores-08 "Example layouts (local repos)" section, which uses path-form TARGETs and implies local fixture.

**Reading B — path TARGET = workspace location only; remote separate:**
```
vc-x1 init ./tf1 --scope=code,bot         # uses config-provided GitHub remote
```
Then we'd need a flag like `--local` or `--no-remote` for fixture.

**Trade-off:** Reading A is more ergonomic (path-form does what test fixtures want) but loses the orthogonal "workspace at custom path WITH a GitHub remote" combo (you'd need a flag back). Reading B keeps things orthogonal but adds a flag.

**My recommendation: Reading A.** The "custom path + GitHub remote" combo is rare; if needed, add a `--workspace-dir` flag later. Path-form already implies "I'm playing locally" — having it also flip to fixture-mode is intuitive.

So in the new shape:
```
vc-x1 init ./tf1                    # fixture, dual repo, cwd-relative
vc-x1 init /tmp/xyz/tf1              # fixture at absolute path
vc-x1 init ../test-repos/tf1         # fixture, parent-relative
vc-x1 init ./tf1 --scope=por         # fixture, single repo
```

Want me to go with Reading A? If you want B, what's the flag name (`--local`/`--fixture`/`--no-remote`)?

> AGENT

Got it — Reading B then. Path TARGET = workspace location only; remote always comes from config (or URL/owner-name TARGET).

So how do we make a fixture? Three options:

**1. Drop fixture from init; compose via clone.**
```
git init --bare /tmp/xyz/remote-code.git
git init --bare /tmp/xyz/remote-claude.git
vc-x1 clone /tmp/xyz/remote-code.git tf1
```
Clone already supports path-form TARGET (-2). No new init surface needed. Tests + scripts pre-create their bares; init stays small.

**2. New `--fixture <PARENT>` (or `--repo-local <PARENT>` reborn) flag.**
```
vc-x1 init ./tf1 --fixture /tmp/xyz   # bares at /tmp/xyz/remote-{code,claude}.git
vc-x1 init ./tf1 --fixture .          # bares alongside workspace
```
Keeps the convenience; one command instead of three. Adds a flag back (we just dropped four, adding one is cheap).

**3. Encode "local" as a remote-provider in config.**
```toml
[default]
remote-provider = "local"

[local]
bare-dir = "/tmp/xyz"
```
`vc-x1 init ./tf1` → fixture using config. Most composable but config-only; awkward for one-off / CI scratch.

**My lean: #2.** Tests/CI scripts run `vc-x1 init ./tf1 --fixture .` and get the old behavior in one line. The flag is well-scoped (init only, fixture-only) and doesn't bloat the common path. #1 is cleaner architecturally but pushes 2 extra commands onto every fixture user.

Which way?

> DEVELOPER

How about adding repo-local-fixtures to vc-x1/config.toml and `--fixture [path]` where [path] is optional and if not present use config.toml? Note I renamed remote-provider to repo-remote-provider, thoughts?

> AGENT

Good calls on both. Some implications worth confirming before I start coding:

**1. Naming.** Agreed — `repo-remote-provider` is more discoverable than `remote-provider` and parallels `repo-local-fixtures`. I'll update the config schema and the -3 module to match (small post-hoc edit; the file isn't consumed yet).

**2. Schema placement of `repo-local-fixtures`.** I'd put it in a `[local]` section to mirror the per-provider pattern:
```toml
[default]
repo-remote-provider = "github"   # or "local" to default to fixture mode

[github]
owner = "winksaville"
service = "github.com"

[local]
bare-dir = "/tmp/vc-x1-fixtures"  # default for --fixture without [PATH]
```

Then "local" becomes a valid `repo-remote-provider` value, symmetric with "github". Forward-compatible with future "gitlab" sections.

(Or flatter: `[default].repo-local-fixtures = "..."`. Less symmetric but matches your wording exactly. Either works — slight preference for `[local].bare-dir` for symmetry.)

**3. Clap shape for `--fixture [PATH]`.** Optional value via `Option<Option<PathBuf>>`:
- `None` → flag absent (use config's provider)
- `Some(None)` → `--fixture` (no path; use `[local].bare-dir`; error if unset)
- `Some(Some(p))` → `--fixture /tmp/xyz` (path overrides config)

**4. `--fixture` semantics — what does it do?**
- Forces `repo-remote-provider = "local"` for this run.
- Resolves bare-dir: PATH arg → `[local].bare-dir` → error.
- Bares created at `<bare-dir>/remote-code.git` + `<bare-dir>/remote-claude.git` (same as old `--repo-local`).

**5. Conflict handling.** `--fixture` is incompatible with TARGETs that dictate a remote:
- URL TARGET → error ("URL specifies a remote; --fixture creates bares locally")
- `owner/name` TARGET → error (same reason)
- Path TARGET → fine (no remote implied)
- Bare NAME TARGET → fine (`--fixture` overrides provider chain that would have expanded NAME)

**6. Cycle placement.** Small enough to fold into -4 alongside the rest of the init reshape (config-struct extension is ~5 lines). Or land as a -4a if you want to keep -4 surgically focused on dropping flags + parse_target. I'd fold.

Sound right? Anything to adjust before I rename `remote-provider` → `repo-remote-provider` and start -4?

> AGENT

Agreed — flatter is better. Single field, no section ceremony.

**Final config schema:**
```toml
[default]
repo-remote-provider = "github"     # provider for non-fixture init
repo-local-fixtures = "~/test-fixtures"  # default for --fixture (no path)

[github]
owner = "winksaville"
service = "github.com"
```

Both keys are independent: `repo-remote-provider` selects the provider section for the normal path; `repo-local-fixtures` is the path used when `--fixture` is invoked without an argument. No `[local]` section needed.

**`--fixture` resolution chain:**
1. `--fixture <PATH>` → use `<PATH>`
2. `--fixture` (no path) → use `[default].repo-local-fixtures`
3. Neither → error: "set `[default].repo-local-fixtures` or pass `--fixture <PATH>`"

**Cycle placement:** Folding the schema rename + new field into -4 alongside the consumer wiring. -3 shipped the module unconsumed; renaming a field in something nothing reads yet has no behavior impact, and one commit avoids the back-and-forth.

36	/// Resolved user config. All fields are `Option` — absent file or
37	/// absent keys yield `None`. Consumers apply their own defaults
38	/// (e.g. `service.unwrap_or("github.com")` at the use site).
39	#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
40	pub struct UserConfig {
41	    /// `[default].remote-provider` — selects which `[<provider>]`
42	    /// section's fields are used when expanding bare NAME.
43	    pub remote_provider: Option<String>,
44	
45	    /// `[github].owner` — the GitHub user/org used as the implicit
46	    /// owner for bare NAME on the GitHub provider.
47	    pub github_owner: Option<String>,
48	
49	    /// `[github].service` — host portion of the SSH URL (e.g.
50	    /// `github.com`, or a GHE host). Defaults at use site.
51	    pub github_service: Option<String>,
52	}
53	
54	/// Path to the user config file.
55	///
56	/// - Honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` if set (XDG Base Directory spec).
57	/// - Falls back to `$HOME/.config`.
58	/// - Errors if neither variable is set.
59	pub fn config_path() -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
60	    let base = if let Some(xdg) = std::env::var_os("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") {
61	        PathBuf::from(xdg)
62	    } else if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME") {
63	        PathBuf::from(home).join(".config")
64	    } else {
65	        return Err("neither $XDG_CONFIG_HOME nor $HOME is set".into());
66	    };
67	    Ok(base.join("vc-x1").join("config.toml"))
68	}
69	
70	/// Load the user config from the default location.
71	///
72	/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.
73	/// - Malformed file → fatal error.
74	#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: 0.41.1-4 is the first consumer; staged ahead in -3.
75	pub fn load() -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
76	    load_from(&config_path()?)
77	}
78	
79	/// Load the user config from an explicit path.
80	///
81	/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.
82	/// - Malformed file → fatal error (propagated from `toml_simple`).
83	/// - Unknown sections / keys are silently ignored
84	///   (forward-compatible with future provider sections).
85	pub fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
86	    if !path.exists() {
87	        return Ok(UserConfig::default());
88	    }
89	    let map = toml_simple::toml_load(path)?;

1	//! User-level config loaded from `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`.
2	//!
3	//! Backs init's bare-NAME expansion (`vc-x1 init tf1` →
4	//! `git@<service>:<owner>/tf1.git`). No magic fallbacks — a
5	//! missing file or missing key produces a predictable error
6	//! pointing at the config.
7	//!
8	//! Schema:
9	//!
10	//! ```toml
11	//! [default]
12	//! remote-provider = "github"
13	//!
14	//! [github]
15	//! owner = "winksaville"
16	//! service = "github.com"   # optional, defaults to "github.com"
17	//! ```
18	//!
19	//! `[default].remote-provider` is the selector; per-provider
20	//! sections (`[github]`, future `[gitlab]`, …) carry the
21	//! provider-specific fields.
22	//!
23	//! See `notes/chores-08.md > User config (0.41.1-3)`.
24	//!
25	//! - `load()` reads the file at `config_path()` (honors
26	//!   `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`); missing file → empty `UserConfig`;
27	//!   malformed file → fatal.
28	//! - `load_from(path)` is the same machinery against a caller-
29	//!   supplied path; used by tests and by `load()` itself.
30	//! - `-3` lands the module standalone; `-4` wires it into init.

32	### Command structure
33	
34	```
35	vc-x1 init  <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por] [--private] [--dry-run]
36	vc-x1 clone <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por]             [--dry-run]
37	```
38	
39	Identical surfaces modulo `--private` (init only).
40	
41	`<TARGET>` accepts:
42	
43	- **URL** — `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`,
44	  `https://...(.git)?` (detected by `://` or SSH
45	  `<host>:<path>` shape with `@`).
46	- **`owner/name` shorthand** — single `/`, no path prefix;
47	  resolved to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
48	- **Path-prefixed** — `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`,
49	  bare `.`, or bare `..`. Path IS the target; last component
50	  is the workspace name (consumer canonicalizes `.` / `..`
51	  to a real basename via `canonicalize` + `file_name`).
52	- **Bare alphanumeric NAME** — for **init** only, expands to
53	  `<owner>/NAME` via the user config
54	  ([`User config`](#user-config-0411-3)). Missing config →
55	  error with hint to use `owner/name` shorthand or set
56	  `[default].remote-provider` + `[github].owner`. For
57	  **clone**, bare NAME is an error (genuinely ambiguous —
58	  "missing `./`?" / "missing `/name` suffix?"); clone has
59	  no config-driven defaults.
60	
61	`[NAME]`:
62	
63	- **init**: URL / `owner/name` forms → overrides the derived
64	  workspace name (workspace at `cwd/<NAME>`). Path forms →
65	  error if combined (path already specifies the destination).
66	- **clone**: all forms (URL, `owner/name`, Path-as-source) →
67	  destination dir name in cwd. Without `[NAME]`, derived
68	  from the source via `derive_name`. For clone, TARGET is
69	  the *source* (URL or local repo path) and `[NAME]` is
70	  the *destination* — symmetric with `git clone <src>
71	  [<dest>]`.
72	
73	`--scope`:
74	
75	- `code,bot` (default): both repos, dual-repo layout.
76	- `por`: single repo, no `.vc-config.toml` written.
77	- `code` / `bot` standalone: error. Reason — these are
78	  config-lookup keywords; init has no config to look up
79	  against, and clone's simplification omits them too. The
80	  manual decomposition (clone code as POR, clone bot as
81	  POR, place at `.claude/`, run `vc-x1 symlink`) covers the
82	  rare cases where a user wants the dual layout composed
83	  by hand.
84	
85	`--private`: only meaningful for init when creating a new
86	GitHub repo. Sets visibility at `gh repo create`. Silently
87	warn-and-ignore if the remote already exists. Errors on
88	clone (clone never creates a remote).
89	
90	`--dry-run`: validate the operation as far as possible
91	without side effects. Print what would be done.
```

Want to make sure I understand before designing — a few interpretations of your proposal:

**Reading 1 (symmetric flags, named configs):**
```toml
[remote.github-personal]
provider = "github"
owner = "winksaville"
[remote.github-work]
provider = "github"
owner = "anthropic"

[local.scratch]
parent = "/tmp/scratch"
[local.test-fixtures]
parent = "~/test-fixtures"

[default]
repo-remote = "github-personal"
repo-local = "test-fixtures"
```

CLI:
- `vc-x1 init tf1` → uses `[default].repo-remote` → `[remote.github-personal]`
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-remote github-work` → uses `[remote.github-work]`
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-local scratch` → uses `[local.scratch]` (fixture mode)
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-local` (no value) → uses default `[local.test-fixtures]`

The "the-remote" arg is a **name** that keys into the config. Adds named-config capability (multi-account, multi-fixture-parent).

**Reading 2 (symmetric flags, value is path-or-URL directly):**
```
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-remote git@github.com:wink/tf1.git
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-local /tmp/scratch
```
Value is the literal target, not a config name. Config holds defaults only.

Reading 1 is more capable (named configs), Reading 2 is closer to my current `--fixture [PATH]` just renamed. Which did you have in mind?

**Three design questions either way:**

1. **One-off paths.** Under Reading 1, how do I pass a path that isn't in config? Heuristic ("looks like a path" vs alphanumeric name)? Separate flag (`--repo-local-path`)? Or only support what's in config?

2. **Cross-subcommand semantics.** You said "all subcommands that interact with repos." For `vc-x1 sync` / `push` (which operate on already-configured remotes via `.git/config`), what does `--repo-remote foo` *mean*? Override the push target? Pick among multiple remotes if a workspace has more than one? That's a meaningful design question — these flags currently mean "which side(s)" (`code`/`bot`/`code,bot`/`<path>`), not "which named provider."

3. **Scope for 0.41.1.** Named configs add real complexity (config-section-per-name, lookup, validation). I could ship the simpler symmetric flags now and add named-config lookup in 0.41.2 — or commit to the bigger design upfront. Which fits your timing?

> AGENT

Got it — N named configs, partitioned by category, with `local` and `remote` as starter categories but user can add their own.

**Proposed schema:**
```toml
# Each [repo.<category>.<name>] is a named config block
[repo.remote.github-personal]
provider = "github"
owner = "winksaville"

[repo.remote.github-work]
provider = "github"
owner = "anthropic"

[repo.local.scratch]
parent = "/tmp/scratch"

[repo.local.test-fixtures]
parent = "~/test-fixtures"

# user-defined category (e.g. staging)
[repo.staging.preview]
provider = "github"
owner = "wink-preview"

# defaults per category
[default]
repo-remote = "github-personal"
repo-local = "test-fixtures"
```

`[repo.<category>.<name>]` is the data; `[default].repo-<category>` picks the default within a category. Categories are arbitrary strings — `local` and `remote` are blessed but anything works.

**CLI design — pick one:**

**Option D1 — dynamic `--repo-<category> [name]` flag:**
```
vc-x1 init tf1                                    # uses [default].repo-remote (fallback to "remote" category)
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-remote github-work          # uses [repo.remote.github-work]
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-local scratch               # uses [repo.local.scratch]
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-local                       # uses [default].repo-local
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo-staging preview             # user-defined category
```
- Reads naturally; matches your sketch exactly.
- Implementation: pre-parse argv, pluck `--repo-*` flags into a map, pass remainder to clap.
- Cost: ~50 LOC of pre-parsing + lose clap's built-in help/completion for these flags (could compensate by listing known categories in `--help`).

**Option D2 — single `--repo <cat>=<name>` flag (clap-native):**
```
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo remote=github-work
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo local=scratch
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo local                       # uses default for "local"
vc-x1 init tf1 --repo staging=preview
```
- Clap-native, no pre-parse.
- Slightly less ergonomic; wordier syntax.
- Cost: ~20 LOC, repeatable flag with custom value parser.

**Two scope questions:**

1. **For -4, init only or all repo-touching subcommands?** I'd lean init-only for -4; add to sync/push/etc. in a follow-on cycle once we see the pattern shake out. Per-subcommand wiring is small but spreads the diff wide.

2. **0.41.1-3 already shipped a config schema; do we evolve it now (rename `[default].repo-remote-provider` → `[default].repo-remote`, restructure into `[repo.<cat>.<name>]`) or keep old schema as a transitional step?** Since -3's module has no consumers yet, I'd just rewrite the schema cleanly — no migration baggage.

Which CLI option (D1 or D2)? And confirm scope (init-only for now)?

> AGENT

Resolution rules with explicit defaults / error messages:

**1. `--repo` absent entirely:**
- Look up `[default].repo-remote` → `<name>`.
- Then resolve `[repo.remote.<name>]`.
- `[default].repo-remote` unset → error: `no repo specified; pass --repo <cat>=<name> or set [default].repo-remote in ~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`.
- `[repo.remote.<name>]` missing → error: `[default].repo-remote = "<name>" but [repo.remote.<name>] section not found`.

(Why `repo-remote` as the global default? Init's dominant case is "create a github remote." If you want fixtures-by-default, set `[default].repo-remote = "<some-local-name>"` — note the `repo-remote` key still gates the absent-flag path; the *category* is encoded via the resolved section, not the default key. Or we add a separate `[default].repo` key for "the absolute default category"; lmk preference.)

**2. `--repo <cat>` (no `=name`):**
- Look up `[default].repo-<cat>` → `<name>`.
- Then resolve `[repo.<cat>.<name>]`.
- `[default].repo-<cat>` unset → error: `no default for category '<cat>'; set [default].repo-<cat> or use --repo <cat>=<name>`.
- `[repo.<cat>.<name>]` missing → same "section not found" error as above.

**3. `--repo <cat>=<name>` (explicit):**
- Resolve `[repo.<cat>.<name>]` directly.
- Section missing → error: `config section [repo.<cat>.<name>] not found`.

**4. Multiple `--repo` flags:**
- Error: `multiple --repo specified; init creates one repo at a time`. (Init's dispatch is one-shot — you're either making a github remote OR local bares, not both.)

- Any other category in -4 → error `unknown category '<cat>' (built-ins: remote, local)`.
