Concrete schema for home/work + `--debug`, with derivation comments:

```toml
# ~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml
#
# Three layers:
#   - [default.*]              absolute defaults (no flag at all)
#   - [account.<acct>.*]       per-account defaults
#   - [repo.<cat>.<name>]      actual config blocks (account-shared)

# ====================================================================
# Top-level defaults — used when the corresponding flag is absent
# ====================================================================

[default]
account = "home"   # --account absent → "home"
debug = "trace"    # --debug used without value → "trace"

# ====================================================================
# Account: home
# ====================================================================

# --repo absent entirely:
#   [account.home.default.repo].category = "remote"
#   → [account.home.category.repo].remote = "github-personal"
#   → [repo.remote.github-personal]
[account.home.default.repo]
category = "remote"

# --repo <cat> (no =name):
#   [account.home.category.repo].<cat> → name → [repo.<cat>.<name>]
[account.home.category.repo]
remote = "github-personal"   # --repo remote → [repo.remote.github-personal]
local  = "test-fixtures"     # --repo local  → [repo.local.test-fixtures]

# ====================================================================
# Account: work
# ====================================================================

[account.work.default.repo]
category = "remote"

[account.work.category.repo]
remote = "github-work"       # --repo remote (under --account work)
local  = "work-fixtures"     # --repo local  (under --account work)

# ====================================================================
# Named repo configs — account-shared, referenced by name from accounts
# ====================================================================

[repo.remote.github-personal]
provider = "github"
owner    = "winksaville"
service  = "github.com"      # optional, defaults to "github.com"

[repo.remote.github-work]
provider = "github"
owner    = "anthropic"
service  = "github.com"

[repo.local.test-fixtures]
parent = "~/test-fixtures"

[repo.local.work-fixtures]
parent = "/work/test-fixtures"
```

**CLI invocations and what they resolve to:**

| Command | Account | Cat | Name | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vc-x1 init tf1` | home | remote | github-personal | `[repo.remote.github-personal]` |
| `vc-x1 init tf1 --account work` | work | remote | github-work | `[repo.remote.github-work]` |
| `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo remote` | home | remote | github-personal | same as no-flag (home default) |
| `vc-x1 init tf1 --account work --repo local` | work | local | work-fixtures | `[repo.local.work-fixtures]` |
| `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo remote=github-work` | home | remote | github-work | `[repo.remote.github-work]` (explicit name override) |
| `vc-x1 init tf1 --debug` | — | — | — | debug level = "trace" |
| `vc-x1 init tf1 --debug debug` | — | — | — | debug level = "debug" |

- `[default].account` config key — system default.

> AGENT

Honest answer: **under the names-as-pointers schema, those two CLI invocations don't work as you wrote them.**

- `--repo remote=github.com` → would look up `[repo.remote."github.com"]` (TOML needs the dots quoted). The section has to exist; "github.com" alone isn't enough info to make a URL — init still needs `provider`/`owner`/`service` from somewhere.
- `--repo local=~/test-fixtures` → would look up `[repo.local."~/test-fixtures"]`, which is essentially impossible as a section name (tilde, slash, etc.).

So you're not actually wanting names. You're wanting **literal values** at the CLI — the value after `=` IS the target (URL/path), not a name. Reading (ii).

Under literal-values, the schema collapses considerably and your examples work as-typed:

```toml
[default]
account = "home"

[account.home.repo]
default = "remote"

[account.home.repo.category]
remote = "git@github.com:winksaville"   # URL prefix; init appends /<NAME>.git
local  = "~/test-fixtures"              # fixture parent dir

[account.work.repo]
default = "remote"

[account.work.repo.category]
remote = "git@github.com:anthropic"
local  = "/work/fixtures"
```

CLI invocations:
- `vc-x1 init tf1` → home / remote → `git@github.com:winksaville/tf1.git`
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo local` → home / local → bares at `~/test-fixtures/remote-{code,claude}.git`
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo remote=git@gitlab.com:winksaville` → literal URL prefix wins
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --repo local=~/scratch` → literal path wins
- `vc-x1 init tf1 --account work --repo remote` → work / remote → `git@github.com:anthropic/tf1.git`

**Trade-off:** literal values are simpler and CLI-symmetric, but the named-`[repo.<cat>.<name>]` layer goes away. Multi-account still works (each account has its own category-keyed defaults). The values themselves carry the structure (URL prefix, path) instead of being looked up.

```toml
[default]
account = "home"
debug   = "trace"

[account.home]
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
repo.category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"

[account.work]
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:anthropic"
repo.category.local   = "/work/fixtures"
```

Each account name appears **once** (in its section header). Down from 4 mentions to 2.

Resolution is unchanged — toml_simple flattens dotted keys, so `account.home.repo.category.remote` is the same lookup key as before; we just spelled it more compactly.

Lock in the compact form?

> DEVELOPER

What about using Array Tables would that reduce duplication, https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0#array-of-tables combined with dotted names to nest them?

> AGENT

Honest answer: array of tables wouldn't reduce duplication for our case, and it makes things harder.

**With `[[account]]`:**
```toml
[[account]]
name = "home"
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
repo.category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"

[[account]]
name = "work"
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:anthropic"
repo.category.local   = "/work/fixtures"
```

vs. **named-section + dotted keys (current):**
```toml
[account.home]
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
repo.category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"
```

Per-account line count is essentially identical. The array form just trades the section header `[account.home]` for `[[account]]` + a `name = "home"` line — same character count, different shape.

**Two trade-offs that go the wrong way:**

1. **Lookup cost.** `[account.home]` keys directly into `account.home.*`. With `[[account]]`, lookup by name requires scanning the array (`find where name == "home"`). For a config with 2-5 accounts it doesn't matter performance-wise, but the code path is more complex.
2. **Parser cost.** Our `toml_simple` parser doesn't handle `[[...]]` (array of tables) syntax — it strips one layer of brackets, so `[[account]]` would parse as section literal `[account]`. Adding array-of-tables support is a meaningful extension (~30 LOC + tests).

Array of tables shines when entries are **homogeneous list items** (e.g., `[[server]]` for a list of unnamed servers in deployment config). For our case (named accounts looked up by key), `[account.<name>]` is the natural fit.

Recommendation: stick with the dotted-keys form we have. Add `[[...]]` support when we actually have a list-of-unnamed-things use case.

261	### User config (0.41.1-3)
262	
263	Bare-NAME init (`vc-x1 init tf1`) needs a place to look up
264	the implicit owner. Adopt a user-global config at
265	`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml` (XDG-compliant; honors
266	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). No magic fallbacks: missing file or
267	missing key → predictable error pointing at the config.
268	
269	Schema:
270	
271	```toml
272	[default]
273	repo-remote-provider = "github"
274	repo-local-fixtures = "~/test-fixtures"   # optional
275	
276	[github]
277	owner = "winksaville"
278	service = "github.com"   # optional, defaults to "github.com"
279	```
280	
281	`[default].repo-remote-provider` selects the per-provider
282	section (`[github]`, future `[gitlab]`, ...) consulted when
283	expanding bare NAME for the standard remote-backed init
284	path. Forward-compatible with the multi-service direction
285	without restructuring.
286	
287	`[default].repo-local-fixtures` is the default parent dir
288	for `vc-x1 init --fixture` when no `[PATH]` is given.
289	Independent of the provider chain.
290	
291	Resolution rules (no magic):
292	
293	- Bare alphanumeric NAME + no
294	  `[default].repo-remote-provider` set → error: "set
295	  `[default].repo-remote-provider` in
296	  `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml` or use `owner/name`
297	  shorthand".
298	- `repo-remote-provider = "github"` + no `[github].owner`
299	  → error: "set `[github].owner` in
300	  `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`".
301	- `[github].service` unset → defaults to `"github.com"`
302	  (canonical host, not magic).
303	- All present → `tf1` resolves to
304	  `git@<service>:<owner>/<NAME>.git`.
305	
306	`--fixture` resolution chain (independent of provider):
307	
308	- `--fixture <PATH>` → use `<PATH>`.
309	- `--fixture` (no path) → use
310	  `[default].repo-local-fixtures`.
311	- Neither → error: "set `[default].repo-local-fixtures`
312	  or pass `--fixture <PATH>`".
313	- `--fixture` is incompatible with URL or `owner/name`
314	  TARGETs (those dictate a remote); fine with Path or
315	  bare NAME.
316	
317	Per-workspace `.vc-config.toml` override (ancestor walk)
318	is deferred — chicken-and-egg at init time, and the
319	global file covers the dominant use case.
320	
321	`-3` lands the config module standalone (`src/config.rs`,
322	`UserConfig` struct, `load()` / `load_from(path)`); `-4`
323	wires it into init's bare-NAME path and adds
324	`--fixture [PATH]`.
325	
326	#### Refactoring opportunities (post-0.41.1)

  "old_string": "### User config (0.41.1-3)\n\nBare-NAME init (`vc-x1 init tf1`) needs a place to look up\nthe implicit owner. Adopt a user-global config at\n`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml` (XDG-compliant; honors\n`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). No magic fallbacks: missing file or\nmissing key → predictable error pointing at the config.\n\nSchema:\n\n```toml\n[default]\nrepo-remote-provider = \"github\"\nrepo-local-fixtures = \"~/test-fixtures\"   # optional\n\n[github]\nowner = \"winksaville\"\nservice = \"github.com\"   # optional, defaults to \"github.com\"\n```\n\n`[default].repo-remote-provider` selects the per-provider\nsection (`[github]`, future `[gitlab]`, ...) consulted when\nexpanding bare NAME for the standard remote-backed init\npath. Forward-compatible with the multi-service direction\nwithout restructuring.\n\n`[default].repo-local-fixtures` is the default parent dir\nfor `vc-x1 init --fixture` when no `[PATH]` is given.\nIndependent of the provider chain.\n\nResolution rules (no magic):\n\n- Bare alphanumeric NAME + no\n  `[default].repo-remote-provider` set → error: \"set\n  `[default].repo-remote-provider` in\n  `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml` or use `owner/name`\n  shorthand\".\n- `repo-remote-provider = \"github\"` + no `[github].owner`\n  → error: \"set `[github].owner` in\n  `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`\".\n- `[github].service` unset → defaults to `\"github.com\"`\n  (canonical host, not magic).\n- All present → `tf1` resolves to\n  `git@<service>:<owner>/<NAME>.git`.\n\n`--fixture` resolution chain (independent of provider):\n\n- `--fixture <PATH>` → use `<PATH>`.\n- `--fixture` (no path) → use\n  `[default].repo-local-fixtures`.\n- Neither → error: \"set `[default].repo-local-fixtures`\n  or pass `--fixture <PATH>`\".\n- `--fixture` is incompatible with URL or `owner/name`\n  TARGETs (those dictate a remote); fine with Path or\n  bare NAME.\n\nPer-workspace `.vc-config.toml` override (ancestor walk)\nis deferred — chicken-and-egg at init time, and the\nglobal file covers the dominant use case.\n\n`-3` lands the config module standalone (`src/config.rs`,\n`UserConfig` struct, `load()` / `load_from(path)`); `-4`\nwires it into init's bare-NAME path and adds\n`--fixture [PATH]`.",
  "new_string": "### User config (0.41.1-3, redesigned in 0.41.1-4)\n\nUser-global config at `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`\n(XDG-compliant; honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Backs init's\naccount- and repo-target resolution. No magic fallbacks:\nmissing file or missing key → predictable error pointing\nat the exact key to set.\n\n`-3` shipped a flat first-cut schema (`[default]\nrepo-remote-provider`, `[github] owner`); `-4` replaces it\nwith the account/category structure below before init\nbecomes the first consumer in `-5`. Since `-3` had no\nconsumers, the rewrite is non-breaking.\n\nSchema:\n\n```toml\n[default]\naccount = \"home\"      # default --account when absent\ndebug   = \"trace\"     # default --debug value when used without arg\n\n[account.home]\nrepo.default          = \"remote\"                       # default --repo cat when absent\nrepo.category.remote  = \"git@github.com:winksaville\"   # value for --repo remote (no =val)\nrepo.category.local   = \"~/test-fixtures\"              # value for --repo local (no =val)\n\n[account.work]\nrepo.default          = \"remote\"\nrepo.category.remote  = \"git@github.com:anthropic\"\nrepo.category.local   = \"/work/fixtures\"\n```\n\nThree layers — each level has its own default-finding key:\n\n| CLI                       | Step 1: account                | Step 2: category                  | Step 3: value                                    |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| (no `--repo`/`--account`) | `[default].account`            | `[account.<a>.repo].default`      | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |\n| `--account <a>`           | `<a>` (CLI)                    | `[account.<a>.repo].default`      | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |\n| `--repo <cat>`            | `[default].account` (or CLI)   | `<cat>` (CLI)                     | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |\n| `--repo <cat>=<val>`      | `[default].account` (or CLI)   | `<cat>` (CLI)                     | `<val>` (CLI, literal)                           |\n\nValues are **literal targets**, not section-name\npointers. For `category = \"remote\"`, the value is a URL\nprefix (init appends `/<NAME>.git`); for `category =\n\"local\"`, it's the parent dir for fixture bares. Built-in\ncategories `remote` and `local` are recognized; any other\ncategory name errors in `-5` (forward-compat: future\ncycles can add a `kind` field for user-defined categories).\n\nResolution errors (each step has its own message):\n\n- Step 1 missing → `no account specified; set [default].account or use --account <name>`.\n- Step 2 missing → `no default category for account '<a>'; set [account.<a>.repo].default or use --repo <cat>`.\n- Step 3 missing → `no value for --repo <cat> in account '<a>'; set [account.<a>.repo.category].<cat> or use --repo <cat>=<val>`.\n\nPer-workspace `.vc-config.toml` override (ancestor walk)\nis deferred — chicken-and-egg at init time, and the\nglobal file covers the dominant use case.\n\nModule shape:\n\n- `pub struct UserConfig { default_account, default_debug, accounts: HashMap<String, AccountConfig> }`.\n- `pub struct AccountConfig { repo_default, repo_category: HashMap<String, String> }`.\n- `load()` / `load_from(path)` as in `-3`.\n- `resolve_repo(account_override, repo_cli) -> (cat, value)` helper for consumers.\n\n`-4` lands the rewritten module standalone; `-5` (init\nreshape) is the first consumer."
}

> DEVELOPER

Is this a valid simplest ~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml ?

> AGENT

Depends on what you want defaulted.

**Empty file is valid** — config is fully optional. With no config, every CLI invocation must specify `--repo <cat>=<val>` explicitly.

**Simplest useful config — fully default-driven `vc-x1 init tf1`:**
```toml
[default]
account = "home"

[account.home]
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
```
5 lines. Lets `vc-x1 init tf1` resolve to `git@github.com:winksaville/tf1.git` with no flags.

**Variations:**
- Drop `repo.default` (4 lines) if you always pass `--repo remote` on the CLI.
- Drop `[default].account` (4 lines) if you always pass `--account home`.
- Add `repo.category.local = "..."` for fixture-mode default.
- Add a second `[account.work]` block for a second account.

So the truly minimal "useful" one is 4-5 lines. Tests cover empty file (valid → no defaults), partial config (some defaults set), and full schema (everything wired).

Want me to ship this and start -5?

> DEVELOPER

hmm, but if there is only one set of values we shouldn't need [account] at all?

> AGENT

Good point — the account layer is pure overhead when you only have one. Two ways to skip it:

**Option 1 — top-level `[repo]` as single-account shorthand:**
```toml
[repo]
default          = "remote"
category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"
```
3-4 lines for a complete single-account config. Multi-account still uses `[account.<name>]`.

Loader rule: if `[repo.*]` keys exist at top level, they form an implicit "default" account. If `[account.*]` sections exist, they take precedence (multi-account mode); having both would error to keep things unambiguous.

**Option 2 — keep one schema, just default the account name:**
```toml
[account.default]
repo.default          = "remote"
repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
```
Same line count as Option 1 but with the `[account.default]` boilerplate. Less elegant but uniform.

**Option 1 is what your message implies.** It's a small loader extension — add a `top_level_repo: Option<AccountConfig>` field and check it in `resolve_repo` after `--account` and `[default].account` fail to find anything.

Resolution chain becomes:
1. Account: `--account` CLI → `[default].account` → top-level `[repo]` (no account) → error.
2. Category: `--repo <cat>` → account's `repo.default` → error.
3. Value: `--repo <cat>=<val>` → account's `repo.category.<cat>` → error.

Add Option 1 to the rewrite, or keep -4 strict-multi-account and add the top-level shorthand in a follow-on?

Consumers apply their own\n/// errors at use time.\n///\n/// **Two write modes** for repo defaults:\n/// - **Top-level `[repo]`** — single-account shorthand. Sits in\n///   `top_level_repo`. Used when neither `--account` nor\n///   `[default].account` resolves to a known account.\n/// - **`[account.<name>]`** — multi-account. Sits in `accounts`.\n///   Selected by `--account` CLI or `[default].account`.\n///\n/// Mixing both is rejected at load time (ambiguous which one\n/// init should consult).\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct UserConfig {\n    /// `[default].account` — default account when `--account`\n    /// is absent.\n    pub default_account: Option<String>,\n\n    /// `[default].debug` — default value when `--debug` is used\n    /// without an argument. (Reserved; not currently consumed.)\n    pub default_debug: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Top-level `[repo]` — single-account shorthand. `Some`\n    /// only when the file has top-level `repo.*` keys and no\n    /// `[account.*]` sections.\n    pub top_level_repo: Option<AccountConfig>,\n\n    /// Per-account configuration, keyed by account name.\n    pub accounts: HashMap<String, AccountConfig>,\n}"
}

{

  "file_path": "/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/src/config.rs",
  "old_string": "pub fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if !path.exists() {\n        return Ok(UserConfig::default());\n    }\n    let map = toml_simple::toml_load(path)?;\n\n    let mut cfg = UserConfig {\n        default_account: map.get(\"default.account\").cloned(),\n        default_debug: map.get(\"default.debug\").cloned(),\n        accounts: HashMap::new(),\n    };\n\n    // Walk all keys looking for `account.<name>.…` patterns and\n    // group into per-account `AccountConfig` entries.\n    for (full_key, value) in &map {\n        let Some(rest) = full_key.strip_prefix(\"account.\") else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        // rest is `<name>.<...>`; split at the first dot.\n        let Some((name, suffix)) = rest.split_once('.') else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let account = cfg\n            .accounts\n            .entry(name.to_string())\n            .or_insert_with(AccountConfig::default);\n        match suffix {\n            \"repo.default\" => {\n                account.repo_default = Some(value.clone());\n            }\n            s if let Some(cat) = s.strip_prefix(\"repo.category.\") => {\n                account.repo_category.insert(cat.to_string(), value.clone());\n            }\n            _ => {} // unknown sub-key; ignore\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(cfg)\n}",
  "new_string": "pub fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if !path.exists() {\n        return Ok(UserConfig::default());\n    }\n    let map = toml_simple::toml_load(path)?;\n\n    let mut cfg = UserConfig {\n        default_account: map.get(\"default.account\").cloned(),\n        default_debug: map.get(\"default.debug\").cloned(),\n        top_level_repo: None,\n        accounts: HashMap::new(),\n    };\n\n    let mut top_level = AccountConfig::default();\n    let mut top_level_seen = false;\n\n    // Walk all keys; route `repo.*` to top-level, `account.<n>.…`\n    // to per-account.\n    for (full_key, value) in &map {\n        if let Some(suffix) = full_key.strip_prefix(\"repo.\") {\n            top_level_seen = true;\n            apply_repo_subkey(&mut top_level, suffix, value);\n            continue;\n        }\n        let Some(rest) = full_key.strip_prefix(\"account.\") else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let Some((name, suffix)) = rest.split_once('.') else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let Some(repo_suffix) = suffix.strip_prefix(\"repo.\") else {\n            continue; // unknown sub-section under [account.<n>]\n        };\n        let account = cfg\n            .accounts\n            .entry(name.to_string())\n            .or_insert_with(AccountConfig::default);\n        apply_repo_subkey(account, repo_suffix, value);\n    }\n\n    if top_level_seen && !cfg.accounts.is_empty() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"{}: mixing top-level [repo] with [account.*] is ambiguous — \\\n             remove top-level [repo] or move it under [account.<name>]\",\n            path.display()\n        )\n        .into());\n    }\n    if top_level_seen {\n        cfg.top_level_repo = Some(top_level);\n    }\n\n    Ok(cfg)\n}\n\n/// Apply one `repo.*` sub-key (e.g. `default`, `category.remote`)\n/// onto an `AccountConfig`. Used for both the top-level `[repo]`\n/// path and the `[account.<n>.repo]` path.\nfn apply_repo_subkey(account: &mut AccountConfig, suffix: &str, value: &str) {\n    match suffix {\n        \"default\" => {\n            account.repo_default = Some(value.to_string());\n        }\n        s if let Some(cat) = s.strip_prefix(\"category.\") => {\n            account.repo_category.insert(cat.to_string(), value.to_string());\n        }\n        _ => {} // unknown sub-key; ignore (forward-compat)\n    }\n}"
}

  "old_string": "pub fn resolve_repo(\n    cfg: &UserConfig,\n    account_override: Option<&str>,\n    repo_cli: Option<&RepoSelector>,\n) -> Result<(String, String), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    // Step 1: account.\n    let account_name = match account_override {\n        Some(a) => a.to_string(),\n        None => cfg.default_account.clone().ok_or(\n            \"no account specified; set [default].account or use --account <name>\",\n        )?,\n    };\n    let account = cfg.accounts.get(&account_name).ok_or_else(|| {\n        format!(\"account '{account_name}' not found in config (no [account.{account_name}] section)\")\n    })?;\n\n    // Step 2: category.\n    let category = match repo_cli {\n        Some(sel) => sel.category.clone(),\n        None => account.repo_default.clone().ok_or_else(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"no default category for account '{account_name}'; set \\\n                 [account.{account_name}.repo].default or use --repo <cat>\"\n            )\n        })?,\n    };\n\n    // Step 3: value.\n    let value = match repo_cli.and_then(|s| s.value.clone()) {\n        Some(v) => v,\n        None => account.repo_category.get(&category).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"no value for --repo {category} in account '{account_name}'; set \\\n                 [account.{account_name}.repo.category].{category} or use \\\n                 --repo {category}=<val>\"\n            )\n        })?,\n    };\n\n    Ok((category, value))\n}",
  "new_string": "pub fn resolve_repo(\n    cfg: &UserConfig,\n    account_override: Option<&str>,\n    repo_cli: Option<&RepoSelector>,\n) -> Result<(String, String), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    // Step 1: pick the AccountConfig to use.\n    //\n    // - `--account` CLI → must hit `cfg.accounts[name]`.\n    // - `[default].account` → must hit `cfg.accounts[that]`.\n    // - Otherwise fall back to top-level `[repo]` (no account).\n    // - Otherwise error.\n    //\n    // `account_label` is for error messages — section-name \"<name>\"\n    // when an account was selected, \"<top-level>\" for the no-account\n    // shorthand path.\n    let (account, account_label) = match (account_override, &cfg.default_account) {\n        (Some(name), _) => {\n            let acct = cfg.accounts.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"account '{name}' not found in config (no [account.{name}] section)\"\n                )\n            })?;\n            (acct, name.to_string())\n        }\n        (None, Some(name)) => {\n            let acct = cfg.accounts.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"account '{name}' (from [default].account) not found in config \\\n                     (no [account.{name}] section)\"\n                )\n            })?;\n            (acct, name.clone())\n        }\n        (None, None) => match cfg.top_level_repo.as_ref() {\n            Some(r) => (r, String::from(\"<top-level>\")),\n            None => {\n                return Err(\n                    \"no account specified; set [default].account, use \\\n                     --account <name>, or write a top-level [repo] section\"\n                        .into(),\n                );\n            }\n        },\n    };\n\n    // Step 2: category.\n    let category = match repo_cli {\n        Some(sel) => sel.category.clone(),\n        None => account.repo_default.clone().ok_or_else(|| {\n            section_error(&account_label, \"no default category\", \"repo.default\", \"use --repo <cat>\")\n        })?,\n    };\n\n    // Step 3: value.\n    let value = match repo_cli.and_then(|s| s.value.clone()) {\n        Some(v) => v,\n        None => account.repo_category.get(&category).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {\n            section_error(\n                &account_label,\n                &format!(\"no value for --repo {category}\"),\n                &format!(\"repo.category.{category}\"),\n                &format!(\"--repo {category}=<val>\"),\n            )\n        })?,\n    };\n\n    Ok((category, value))\n}\n\n/// Compose an error message for a missing-key case in `resolve_repo`.\n///\n/// Uses `[account.<label>.<key>]` for named accounts and just\n/// `[<key>]` for the top-level `[repo]` shorthand.\nfn section_error(account_label: &str, msg: &str, key: &str, cli_alt: &str) -> String {\n    let section = if account_label == \"<top-level>\" {\n        format!(\"[{key}]\")\n    } else {\n        format!(\"[account.{account_label}.{key}]\")\n    };\n    format!(\"{msg}; set {section} or use {cli_alt}\")\n}"
}

283	### User config (0.41.1-3, redesigned in 0.41.1-4)
284	
285	User-global config at `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`
286	(XDG-compliant; honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Backs init's
287	account- and repo-target resolution. No magic fallbacks:
288	missing file or missing key → predictable error pointing
289	at the exact key to set.
290	
291	`-3` shipped a flat first-cut schema (`[default]
292	repo-remote-provider`, `[github] owner`); `-4` replaces it
293	with the account/category structure below before init
294	becomes the first consumer in `-5`. Since `-3` had no
295	consumers, the rewrite is non-breaking.
296	
297	Schema:
298	
299	```toml
300	[default]
301	account = "home"      # default --account when absent
302	debug   = "trace"     # default --debug value when used without arg
303	
304	[account.home]
305	repo.default          = "remote"                       # default --repo cat when absent
306	repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"   # value for --repo remote (no =val)
307	repo.category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"              # value for --repo local (no =val)
308	
309	[account.work]
310	repo.default          = "remote"

315	```
316	
317	Three layers — each level has its own default-finding key:
318	
319	| CLI                       | Step 1: account                | Step 2: category                  | Step 3: value                                    |
320	|---|---|---|---|
321	| (no `--repo`/`--account`) | `[default].account`            | `[account.<a>.repo].default`      | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |
322	| `--account <a>`           | `<a>` (CLI)                    | `[account.<a>.repo].default`      | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |
323	| `--repo <cat>`            | `[default].account` (or CLI)   | `<cat>` (CLI)                     | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |
324	| `--repo <cat>=<val>`      | `[default].account` (or CLI)   | `<cat>` (CLI)                     | `<val>` (CLI, literal)                           |
325	
326	Values are **literal targets**, not section-name
327	pointers. For `category = "remote"`, the value is a URL
328	prefix (init appends `/<NAME>.git`); for `category =
329	"local"`, it's the parent dir for fixture bares. Built-in
330	categories `remote` and `local` are recognized; any other
331	category name errors in `-5` (forward-compat: future
332	cycles can add a `kind` field for user-defined categories).
333	
334	Resolution errors (each step has its own message):
335	
336	- Step 1 missing → `no account specified; set [default].account or use --account <name>`.
337	- Step 2 missing → `no default category for account '<a>'; set [account.<a>.repo].default or use --repo <cat>`.
338	- Step 3 missing → `no value for --repo <cat> in account '<a>'; set [account.<a>.repo.category].<cat> or use --repo <cat>=<val>`.
339	
340	Per-workspace `.vc-config.toml` override (ancestor walk)
341	is deferred — chicken-and-egg at init time, and the
342	global file covers the dominant use case.
343	
344	Module shape:
345	
346	- `pub struct UserConfig { default_account, default_debug, accounts: HashMap<String, AccountConfig> }`.
347	- `pub struct AccountConfig { repo_default, repo_category: HashMap<String, String> }`.
348	- `load()` / `load_from(path)` as in `-3`.
349	- `resolve_repo(account_override, repo_cli) -> (cat, value)` helper for consumers.
350	
351	`-4` lands the rewritten module standalone; `-5` (init
352	reshape) is the first consumer.
353	
354	#### Refactoring opportunities (post-0.41.1)
355	
356	Two cleanups surfaced while sizing the module that we
357	deliberately deferred to keep `-3` scoped:
358	
359	- **Unify `.vc-config.toml` accessors onto Pattern B.**
360	  The tree has two patterns for reading TOML config:
361	  - Pattern A (`desc_helpers.rs`, `fix_desc.rs`,
362	    `validate_desc.rs`): call site does
363	    `toml_simple::toml_load(path)` and passes the
364	    resulting `HashMap<String, String>` to map-typed
365	    accessor fns (`other_repo_from_config(&map)`,
366	    `ochid_prefix_from_config(&map)`).
367	  - Pattern B (`push::resolve_state_layout`, new
368	    `config::load_from`): function takes a path,
369	    returns a typed struct with the fields it cares
370	    about; conversion baked in.
371	  Pattern B is more discoverable and testable. A
372	  `WorkspaceConfig` struct with `load_from(path)` could
373	  replace the Pattern-A helpers across desc_helpers /
374	  fix_desc / validate_desc. ~50 LOC, mechanical.
375	- **Layered config precedence** — once `WorkspaceConfig`
376	  is typed, layering user → workspace → CLI becomes
377	  natural (workspace can override `[github].owner` for a
378	  specific project). Init can't use this layer because
379	  it runs *before* a workspace exists, but post-init
380	  commands could.
381	
382	Both candidates for the 0.41.2 cycle. See `notes/todo.md`.
383	
384	### Decisions made during design
385	
386	- **Version + cycle line.** This work + the sync `--check`
387	  fix land on the 0.41.x line. Init+clone = 0.41.1. Sync
388	  fix = a separate cycle (likely 0.41.2). Then rebase the
389	  in-flight 0.42.0 work on top of both.

The loader accepts a top-level `[repo]`\nsection as a single-account shorthand:\n\n```toml\n[repo]\ndefault          = \"remote\"\ncategory.remote  = \"git@github.com:winksaville\"\ncategory.local   = \"~/test-fixtures\"\n```\n\n3-4 lines for a complete config — no `[default].account`,\nno `[account.<name>]`. 233	Before proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:

192	
193	For multi-step:
194	
195	1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-0` with the plan and commit as a chore
196	   marker.
197	2. Implement in one or more `X.Y.Z-N` commits (increment N as
198	   needed).
199	3. Final commit bumps to `X.Y.Z` (no suffix), updates
200	   `notes/todo.md` and `notes/chores-*.md` — this is the "done"
201	   marker.
202	
203	Multi-step cycles surface the ladder at the top of
204	`notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` as a bullet list with `(done)` /
205	`(current)` markers — see the file's intro paragraph for the
206	format. Update the markers as each step ships so the In Progress
207	view stays current at a glance.
208	
209	**Why numeric suffixes (`-0`, `-1`, …) rather than `-devN`:**
210	semver pre-release identifiers may consist of a single numeric
211	component, and they compare numerically per spec. So
212	`X.Y.Z-1 < X.Y.Z-2 < … < X.Y.Z` correctly orders the dev ladder
213	below the done marker. Cargo accepts this form. The `-dev` prefix
214	adds no information the git log doesn't already convey and
215	doubles typing per commit.
216

16	/// - `OwnerName(owner, name)` — `owner/name` shorthand;
17	///   resolves to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
18	/// - `Path` — local path with explicit prefix
19	///   (`./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, or bare `~`). Path text is preserved
20	///   literally; tilde expansion is the consumer's responsibility.

22	#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: staged for 0.41.1-2 (clone) / 0.41.1-3 (init) consumers
23	pub enum Target {
24	    Url(String),
25	    OwnerName(String, String),
26	    Path(PathBuf),
27	}
28	
29	/// Parse a positional `<TARGET>` argument into one of the three
30	/// shapes.
31	///
32	/// Detection order (path forms first, then URL, then shorthand):
33	///
34	/// - Path forms: bare `.`, `..`, or `~`; or starts with `./`,
35	///   `../`, `/`, or `~/`. `.` and `..` are POSIX cwd/parent and
36	///   are unambiguous; the consumer resolves them to a real
37	///   workspace name via `canonicalize` + `file_name`.
38	/// - URL: contains `://`, or SSH-style `user@host:path` (an `@`
39	///   followed somewhere by `:`).
40	/// - `owner/name` shorthand: exactly one `/`, both sides non-empty,
41	///   no path or URL indicators.
42	///
43	/// Errors on bare alphanumeric names (genuinely ambiguous —
44	/// "missing `./`?" / "missing `/name` suffix?") and empty input.
45	#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: staged for 0.41.1-2 (clone) / 0.41.1-3 (init) consumers
46	pub fn parse_target(s: &str) -> Result<Target, String> {
47	    if s.is_empty() {
48	        return Err("empty target".into());
49	    }
50	
51	    if s == "."
52	        || s == ".."
53	        || s == "~"
54	        || s.starts_with("./")
55	        || s.starts_with("../")
56	        || s.starts_with('/')
57	        || s.starts_with("~/")
58	    {
59	        return Ok(Target::Path(PathBuf::from(s)));
60	    }
61	
62	    if s.contains("://") {
63	        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));
64	    }
65	    if let Some(at) = s.find('@')
66	        && s[at + 1..].contains(':')
67	    {
68	        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));
69	    }
70	
71	    if s.matches('/').count() == 1
72	        && let Some((owner, name)) = s.split_once('/')
73	        && !owner.is_empty()
74	        && !name.is_empty()
75	    {
76	        return Ok(Target::OwnerName(owner.to_string(), name.to_string()));
77	    }
78	
79	    Err(format!(
80	        "'{s}' is not a recognized target — expected URL, owner/name shorthand, or path prefix (./X, ../X, /X, ~/X, ~)"
81	    ))
82	}
83	
84	/// Derive the project name from a repo URL or `owner/name` shorthand.
85	///
86	/// - Strips trailing `.git`.
87	/// - Returns the last segment after the rightmost `/` or `:`.
88	/// - Errors when the resulting name would be empty.
89	pub fn derive_name(repo: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
90	    let stem = repo.strip_suffix(".git").unwrap_or(repo); // OK: .git suffix is optional
91	    let last = stem.rsplit(['/', ':']).next().unwrap_or(""); // OK: rsplit always yields at least one element
92	    if last.is_empty() {
93	        return Err(format!("cannot derive project name from '{repo}'").into());
94	    }
95	    Ok(last.to_string())
96	}
97	
98	/// Resolve a repo argument to a git clone URL.
99	///
100	/// - `owner/name` (single `/`, no `:` or scheme) →
101	///   `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
102	/// - Anything else is passed through as-is (already a URL).
103	pub fn resolve_url(repo: &str) -> String {
104	    if repo.contains("://") || repo.contains('@') {
105	        return repo.to_string();
106	    }
107	    if repo.matches('/').count() == 1 && !repo.contains(':') {
108	        return format!("git@github.com:{repo}.git");
109	    }

**Two paths for the -5 ladder step:**

- **(A) Single -5 commit:** surface change + dispatch rewrite + body refactor + tests. Big diff (~700 LOC), one shipment.
- **(B) Split -5/-6:** -5 = surface + dispatch (drops old flags, new `<TARGET>` + `--account`/`--repo`, plan_init uses parse_target + config::resolve_repo, tests rewritten). `init_with_symlink` body stays as-is, just consumes the new InitPlan. -6 = `init_one`/`init_dual` extraction. POR detection slides to -7, Fixture migration to -8.

The `init_with_symlink` body works against `InitPlan` (which stays the same shape after my dispatch rewrite), so splitting is clean — no broken intermediate state.

109	/// Run a command with retries, sleeping between attempts.
110	fn run_retry(
111	    cmd: &str,
112	    args: &[&str],
113	    cwd: &Path,
114	    retries: u32,
115	    delay_secs: u64,
116	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
117	    let mut last_err = String::new();
118	    for attempt in 1..=retries {
119	        match run(cmd, args, cwd) {
120	            Ok(out) => {
121	                if attempt > 1 {
122	                    debug!("succeeded after {attempt} attempts");
123	                }
124	                return Ok(out);
125	            }
126	            Err(e) => {
127	                last_err = e.to_string();
128	                if attempt < retries {
129	                    debug!("attempt {attempt}/{retries} failed: {last_err}");
130	                    debug!("retrying in {delay_secs}s...");
131	                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(delay_secs));
132	                }
133	            }
134	        }
135	    }
136	    Err(format!("failed after {retries} attempts: {last_err}").into())
137	}

152	    let bot_raw = parts.next();
153	    let code_trim = code_raw.trim();
154	    if code_trim.is_empty() {
155	        return Err("--use-template: code template path is empty".into());
156	    }
157	    let code = PathBuf::from(code_trim);
158	    let bot = match bot_raw.map(str::trim) {
159	        Some(b) if !b.is_empty() => PathBuf::from(b),
160	        _ => {
161	            let file_name = code.file_name().ok_or_else(|| {
162	                format!(
163	                    "--use-template: cannot derive default bot path from '{}' (no file name component)",
164	                    code.display()
165	                )
166	            })?;
167	            let new_name = format!("{}.claude", file_name.to_string_lossy());
168	            code.with_file_name(new_name)
169	        }
170	    };
171	    Ok((code, bot))
172	}

174	/// Top-level non-hidden files init writes. Kept here so that if init is
175	/// ever extended to write non-hidden top-level files, the pre-flight
176	/// conflict scan flags any template that would clash. Currently empty
177	/// because init only writes hidden files (`.vc-config.toml`, `.gitignore`),
178	/// and the template copy skips hidden entries.
179	const RESERVED_TEMPLATE_ENTRIES: &[&str] = &[];
180	
181	/// Validate one template directory: exists, is a directory, and has no
182	/// top-level non-hidden entry that would collide with init's own writes.
183	///
184	/// - `label` prefixes every error message (`code` / `bot`).
185	pub(crate) fn validate_template_one(
186	    label: &str,
187	    p: &Path,
188	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
189	    if !p.exists() {
190	        return Err(format!(
191	            "--use-template: {label} template '{}' does not exist",
192	            p.display()
193	        )
194	        .into());
195	    }
196	    if !p.is_dir() {
197	        return Err(format!(
198	            "--use-template: {label} template '{}' is not a directory",
199	            p.display()
200	        )
201	        .into());
202	    }
203	    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(p)? {
204	        let entry = entry?;
205	        let name = entry.file_name();
206	        let name_str = name.to_string_lossy();
207	        if name_str.starts_with('.') {
208	            continue;
209	        }
210	        if RESERVED_TEMPLATE_ENTRIES.contains(&name_str.as_ref()) {
211	            return Err(format!(
212	                "--use-template: {label} template '{}' contains reserved entry '{}'",
213	                p.display(),
214	                name_str
215	            )
216	            .into());
217	        }
218	    }
219	    Ok(())
220	}

222	/// Validate both template paths (dual-repo mode). Thin wrapper over
223	/// `validate_template_one` kept for single-call ergonomics.
224	pub(crate) fn validate_templates(
225	    code: &Path,
226	    bot: &Path,
227	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
228	    validate_template_one("code", code)?;
229	    validate_template_one("bot", bot)?;
230	    Ok(())
231	}

233	/// Recursively copy non-hidden entries from `src` to `dst`. Any entry whose
234	/// file name starts with `.` is skipped. Symlinks are skipped with a debug
235	/// log — templates don't need them, and following them risks escaping the
236	/// template tree.
237	pub(crate) fn copy_template_recursive(
238	    src: &Path,
239	    dst: &Path,
240	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
241	    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(src)? {
242	        let entry = entry?;
243	        let name = entry.file_name();
244	        let name_str = name.to_string_lossy();
245	        if name_str.starts_with('.') {
246	            continue;
247	        }
248	        let src_path = entry.path();
249	        let dst_path = dst.join(&name);
250	        let ft = entry.file_type()?;
251	        if ft.is_symlink() {
252	            debug!("skip symlink {}", src_path.display());
253	            continue;
254	        }
255	        if ft.is_dir() {
256	            mkdir_p(&dst_path)?;
257	            copy_template_recursive(&src_path, &dst_path)?;
258	        } else if ft.is_file() {
259	            debug!("copy {} -> {}", src_path.display(), dst_path.display());
260	            std::fs::copy(&src_path, &dst_path)?;
261	        }
262	    }
263	    Ok(())
264	}

266	/// Replace the first line of `<dir>/README.md` with `# <name>`. If
267	/// `README.md` is absent, this is a no-op. Trailing content after the
268	/// first newline is preserved verbatim; a file with no newline becomes
269	/// just `# <name>`.
270	pub(crate) fn rewrite_readme_first_line(
271	    dir: &Path,
272	    name: &str,
273	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
274	    let readme = dir.join("README.md");
275	    if !readme.exists() {
276	        return Ok(());
277	    }
278	    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&readme)?;
279	    let rest = match content.find('\n') {
280	        Some(pos) => &content[pos..],
281	        None => "",
282	    };
283	    let new_content = format!("# {name}{rest}");
284	    std::fs::write(&readme, new_content)?;
285	    debug!("rewrote first line of {}", readme.display());
286	    Ok(())
287	}

439	/// True when `s` looks like a git remote URL rather than a path.
440	///
441	/// - Scheme-qualified (`scheme://…`).
442	/// - scp-like SSH form (`user@host:path`).
443	/// - Everything else is treated as a path.
444	pub(crate) fn is_remote_url(s: &str) -> bool {
445	    if s.contains("://") {
446	        return true;
447	    }
448	    if let Some(at) = s.find('@')
449	        && let Some(colon) = s.find(':')
450	        && at < colon
451	        && !s[..at].contains('/')
452	    {
453	        return true;
454	    }
455	    false
456	}

458	/// True when `s` is a GitHub URL (host-based detection).
459	///
460	/// - SSH scp-like (`git@github.com:…`).
461	/// - `ssh://git@github.com/…`.
462	/// - `https://github.com/…` and `http://github.com/…`.
463	/// - GitHub URLs route to the `gh repo create` provisioner.
464	pub(crate) fn is_github_url(s: &str) -> bool {
465	    s.starts_with("git@github.com:")
466	        || s.starts_with("ssh://git@github.com/")
467	        || s.starts_with("https://github.com/")
468	        || s.starts_with("http://github.com/")
469	}

471	/// Normalize a `--repo-remote` value. Expand variables, then for
472	/// paths make absolute; URLs pass through after expansion.
473	pub(crate) fn normalize_remote(s: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
474	    let s = s.trim();
475	    if s.is_empty() {
476	        return Err("--repo-remote: value is empty".into());
477	    }
478	    let expanded = expand_vars(s)?;
479	    if is_remote_url(&expanded) {
480	        return Ok(expanded);
481	    }
482	    let p = PathBuf::from(&expanded);
483	    if p.is_absolute() {
484	        Ok(expanded)
485	    } else {
486	        let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
487	        Ok(cwd.join(p).to_string_lossy().to_string())
488	    }
489	}

491	/// Normalize a `--repo-local` value: expand variables, make
492	/// absolute. Parent doesn't need to exist yet — init creates it.
493	pub(crate) fn normalize_local_parent(s: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
494	    let s = s.trim();
495	    if s.is_empty() {
496	        return Err("--repo-local: value is empty".into());
497	    }
498	    let expanded = expand_vars(s)?;
499	    let p = PathBuf::from(&expanded);
500	    if p.is_absolute() {
501	        Ok(p)
502	    } else {
503	        let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
504	        Ok(cwd.join(p))
505	    }
506	}

520	/// How init should provision the remote repositories it pushes to.
521	/// See `notes/chores-06.md > Generalize --scope across commands
522	/// (0.40.0) > 0.40.0-1` for the dispatch rules.
523	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
524	pub(crate) enum Provisioner {
525	    /// `git init --bare` on local paths under `--repo-local`.
526	    LocalBareInit,
527	    /// `gh repo create` for GitHub URLs (default mode or
528	    /// `--repo-remote <github-url>`).
529	    GhCreate,
530	    /// Skip any create step; the caller pre-created the remote
531	    /// (non-GitHub URLs under `--repo-remote`).
532	    ExternalPreExisting,
533	}

535	/// Fully-resolved inputs to the init execution phase.
536	///
537	/// - Dispatch and ambiguity rules live in `plan_init`.
538	/// - Downstream code operates on an `InitPlan` — execution stays
539	///   linear.
540	#[derive(Debug)]
541	pub(crate) struct InitPlan {
542	    /// Which side(s) this plan creates. `scope.is_code_only()` means
543	    /// single-repo; `scope.is_both()` means dual.
544	    pub scope: Scope,
545	    pub project_dir: PathBuf,
546	    pub name: String,
547	    pub code_url: String,
548	    pub provisioner: Provisioner,
549	    /// Set only when `provisioner == LocalBareInit`.
550	    pub code_bare_path: Option<PathBuf>,
551	    /// GitHub `owner/name` for the code side; only populated for
552	    /// the `GhCreate` path (`gh repo create` needs it).
553	    pub gh_code_slug: Option<String>,
554	    /// Session-side dir. None when `scope.is_code_only()`.
555	    pub session_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
556	    /// Session-side project name (e.g. `<name>.claude`). None when
557	    /// `scope.is_code_only()`.
558	    pub session_name: Option<String>,
559	    /// Session-side origin URL. None when `scope.is_code_only()`.
560	    pub session_url: Option<String>,
561	    /// Session-side bare-repo path. `Some` only under `LocalBareInit`
562	    /// with `scope.is_both()`.
563	    pub session_bare_path: Option<PathBuf>,
564	    /// Session-side GitHub slug. `Some` only under `GhCreate` with
565	    /// `scope.is_both()`.
566	    pub gh_session_slug: Option<String>,
567	}
568	
569	/// Build an `InitPlan` from CLI args.
570	///
571	/// - Validate flag mutual-exclusion.
572	/// - Resolve URLs and paths; derive NAME from URL if not given.
573	/// - Pick the provisioner.
574	/// - Errors on any ambiguous or incomplete flag combination.
575	pub(crate) fn plan_init(args: &InitArgs) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
576	    // --- Resolve scope first: default (None) → dual; empty Vec is
577	    // invalid; `bot` alone is meaningless at init time. ---
578	    let scope = match &args.scope {
579	        None => Scope(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot]),
580	        Some(sides) => {
581	            let s = Scope(sides.clone());
582	            if s.is_empty() {
583	                return Err("--scope: value is empty".into());
584	            }
585	            if s.is_bot_only() {
586	                return Err(
587	                    "--scope=bot is meaningless at init time — use --scope=code for single-repo or --scope=code,bot (default) for dual-repo"
588	                        .into(),
589	                );
590	            }
591	            s
592	        }
593	    };
594	
595	    // --- Mutual-exclusion gates (flag-pair ambiguity) ---
596	    if args.repo_local.is_some() && args.repo_remote.is_some() {
597	        return Err("--repo-local and --repo-remote are mutually exclusive".into());
598	    }
599	    if args.repo_local.is_some() && args.dir.is_some() {
600	        return Err(
601	            "--repo-local and --dir are mutually exclusive (--repo-local is the parent)".into(),
602	        );
603	    }
604	    if args.repo_local.is_some() && args.owner.is_some() {
605	        return Err(
606	            "--repo-local and --owner are mutually exclusive (fixture mode has no GitHub)".into(),
607	        );
608	    }
609	    if args.repo_local.is_some() && args.private {
610	        return Err(
611	            "--repo-local and --private are mutually exclusive (fixture mode has no GitHub)".into(),
612	        );
613	    }
614	    if args.repo_remote.is_some() && args.owner.is_some() {
615	        return Err(
616	            "--repo-remote and --owner are mutually exclusive (URL already encodes owner)".into(),
617	        );
618	    }
619	    if args.repo_remote.is_some() && args.private {
620	        return Err(
621	            "--repo-remote and --private are mutually exclusive (visibility is set at repo creation, not here)"
622	                .into(),
623	        );
624	    }
625	
626	    // --- Scope-dependent ambiguity. ---
627	    if scope.is_code_only()
628	        && let Some(t) = &args.use_template
629	        && t.contains(',')
630	    {
631	        return Err(format!(
632	            "--scope=code takes a single template path; got '{t}' (drop the `,BOT` half)"
633	        )
634	        .into());
635	    }
636	
637	    match (&args.repo_local, &args.repo_remote) {
638	        (Some(parent_spec), None) => plan_local_fixture(args, parent_spec, scope),
639	        (None, Some(url_spec)) => plan_external_remote(args, url_spec, scope),
640	        (None, None) => plan_default_github(args, scope),
641	        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
642	        (Some(_), Some(_)) => {
643	            // OK: mutual-exclusion gate above already errored on this case
644	            unreachable!("mutual-exclusion gate earlier in plan_init")
645	        }
646	    }
647	}
648	
649	/// Plan for `--repo-local PARENT` — fixture mode.
650	///
651	/// - Code-only: single bare at `<PARENT>/remote.git`, no session.
652	/// - Dual: `remote-code.git` + `remote-claude.git` plus a nested
653	///   `.claude/` session.
654	fn plan_local_fixture(
655	    args: &InitArgs,
656	    parent_spec: &str,
657	    scope: Scope,
658	) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
659	    let name = args
660	        .name
661	        .clone()
662	        .ok_or("NAME is required with --repo-local")?;
663	    let parent = normalize_local_parent(parent_spec)?;
664	    let project_dir = parent.join(&name);
665	
666	    if scope.is_code_only() {
667	        let code_bare = parent.join("remote.git");
668	        return Ok(InitPlan {
669	            scope,
670	            code_url: code_bare.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
671	            code_bare_path: Some(code_bare),
672	            project_dir,
673	            name,
674	            provisioner: Provisioner::LocalBareInit,
675	            gh_code_slug: None,
676	            session_dir: None,
677	            session_name: None,
678	            session_url: None,
679	            session_bare_path: None,
680	            gh_session_slug: None,
681	        });
682	    }
683	
684	    // Dual: code + bot sides, nested session.
685	    let session_dir = project_dir.join(".claude");
686	    let code_bare = parent.join("remote-code.git");
687	    let session_bare = parent.join("remote-claude.git");
688	    let session_name = format!("{name}.claude");
689	    Ok(InitPlan {
690	        scope,
691	        code_url: code_bare.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
692	        code_bare_path: Some(code_bare),
693	        project_dir,
694	        name,
695	        provisioner: Provisioner::LocalBareInit,
696	        gh_code_slug: None,
697	        session_url: Some(session_bare.to_string_lossy().to_string()),
698	        session_bare_path: Some(session_bare),
699	        session_dir: Some(session_dir),
700	        session_name: Some(session_name),
701	        gh_session_slug: None,
702	    })
703	}
704	
705	/// Plan for `--repo-remote URL` — explicit URL override.
706	///
707	/// - Session URL derived (dual only).
708	/// - NAME derived from URL when not given (must agree if both).
709	/// - GitHub URLs → `GhCreate`; other URLs → `ExternalPreExisting`.
710	fn plan_external_remote(
711	    args: &InitArgs,
712	    url_spec: &str,
713	    scope: Scope,
714	) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
715	    let normalized = normalize_remote(url_spec)?;
716	    let code_url = ensure_git_suffix(&normalized);
717	    let url_name = derive_name(&code_url)?;
718	
719	    let name = match &args.name {
720	        Some(n) if *n == url_name => n.clone(),
721	        Some(n) => {
722	            return Err(format!(
723	                "NAME '{n}' disagrees with --repo-remote URL '{url_spec}' (derived '{url_name}')"
724	            )
725	            .into());
726	        }
727	        None => url_name.clone(),
728	    };
729	
730	    let parent_dir = match &args.dir {
731	        Some(d) => d.clone(),
732	        None => std::env::current_dir()?,
733	    };
734	    let project_dir = parent_dir.join(&name);
735	
736	    let provisioner = if is_github_url(&code_url) {
737	        Provisioner::GhCreate
738	    } else {
739	        Provisioner::ExternalPreExisting
740	    };

857	/// Extract the `owner/name` slug from a GitHub URL (any of the
858	/// supported forms: SSH scp-like, `ssh://`, `https://`).
859	fn github_slug_from_url(url: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
860	    let stem = url.strip_suffix(".git").unwrap_or(url);
861	    // The slug is the last two path components, `owner/name`.
862	    if let Some(path) = stem
863	        .strip_prefix("git@github.com:")
864	        .or_else(|| stem.strip_prefix("ssh://git@github.com/"))
865	        .or_else(|| stem.strip_prefix("https://github.com/"))
866	        .or_else(|| stem.strip_prefix("http://github.com/"))
867	    {
868	        let parts: Vec<&str> = path.split('/').collect();
869	        if parts.len() >= 2 {
870	            return Ok(format!(
871	                "{}/{}",
872	                parts[parts.len() - 2],
873	                parts[parts.len() - 1]
874	            ));
875	        }
876	    }
877	    Err(format!("cannot extract owner/name slug from GitHub URL '{url}'").into())
878	}

882	pub fn init(args: &InitArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
883	    init_with_symlink(args, true)
884	}

1291	    debug!("re-colocate jj atop the now-remote-linked code repo");
1292	    run(

1295	        &plan.project_dir,
1296	    )?;
1297	    debug!("restore code-side main bookmark after re-init");
1298	    run(
1299	        "jj",
1300	        &["bookmark", "set", "main", "-r", "@-"],
1301	        &plan.project_dir,
1302	    )?;
1303	    debug!("enable jj tracking of code-side main against origin");
1304	    run(
1305	        "jj",
1306	        &["bookmark", "track", "main", "--remote=origin"],
1307	        &plan.project_dir,
1308	    )?;
1309	    crate::common::verify_tracking(&plan.project_dir, "main")?;
1310	    let code_chid_final = jj_chid("@-", &plan.project_dir)?;

1341	    info!("");

1365	///
1366	/// - Provision the remote per the plan's provisioner.
1367	/// - Add `origin` and push `main` with retry.
1368	/// - Centralizing keeps both sides' step bodies identical.
1369	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
1370	fn run_remote_step(
1371	    step_label: &str,
1372	    side_label: &str,

1375	    gh_slug: Option<&str>,

1381	    match &plan.provisioner {

1383	            // Safe: GhCreate always supplies gh_slug.
1384	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
1385	            let slug = gh_slug.unwrap(); // OK: GhCreate path always sets gh_slug
1386	            info!("{step_label}: Creating GitHub repo {slug} ({side_label})...");
1387	            debug!("create {side_label}-side remote on GitHub");
1388	            run(
1389	                "gh",
1390	                &["repo", "create", slug, visibility],
1391	                &plan.project_dir,
1392	            )?;
1393	        }
1394	        Provisioner::LocalBareInit => {
1395	            // Safe: LocalBareInit always supplies bare_path.
1396	            #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
1397	            let bare = bare_path.unwrap(); // OK: LocalBareInit path always sets bare_path
1398	            info!(
1399	                "{step_label}: Initializing local bare repo at {} ({side_label})...",

1426	/// Split an `owner/name` slug. Errors if the shape is wrong (no `/`
1427	/// or more than one `/`).
1428	fn split_slug(slug: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
1429	    let parts: Vec<&str> = slug.split('/').collect();
1430	    if parts.len() != 2 || parts[0].is_empty() || parts[1].is_empty() {
1431	        return Err(format!("unexpected GitHub slug '{slug}' (want 'owner/name')").into());
1432	    }
1433	    Ok((parts[0], parts[1]))
1434	}

1	//! User-level config loaded from `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`.
2	//!
3	//! Backs init's account/repo-target resolution. No magic
4	//! fallbacks — a missing file or missing key produces a
5	//! predictable error pointing at the exact key to set.
6	//!
7	//! Schema (multi-account, dotted keys for compactness):
8	//!
9	//! ```toml
10	//! [default]
11	//! account = "home"      # default --account when absent
12	//! debug   = "trace"     # default --debug value when used without arg
13	//!
14	//! [account.home]
15	//! repo.default          = "remote"                       # default --repo cat when absent
16	//! repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"   # value for --repo remote (no =val)
17	//! repo.category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"              # value for --repo local (no =val)
18	//!
19	//! [account.work]
20	//! repo.default          = "remote"
21	//! repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:anthropic"
22	//! repo.category.local   = "/work/fixtures"
23	//! ```
24	//!
25	//! Three-layer resolution — see
26	//! `notes/chores-08.md > User config (0.41.1-3, redesigned in 0.41.1-4)`:
27	//!
28	//! 1. account: CLI `--account` → `[default].account` → error.
29	//! 2. category: CLI `--repo <cat>` → `[account.<a>.repo].default`
30	//!    → error.
31	//! 3. value: CLI `--repo <cat>=<val>` →
32	//!    `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>` → error.
33	//!
34	//! Values are **literal targets**, not section-name pointers.
35	//! For built-in `category = "remote"` the value is a URL prefix
36	//! (init appends `/<NAME>.git`); for `category = "local"` it's
37	//! the parent dir for fixture bare repos.
38	//!
39	//! `-3` shipped a flat first-cut (`[default] repo-remote-provider`,
40	//! `[github] owner`); `-4` is the redesign before any consumer
41	//! is wired in. `-5` (init reshape) is the first consumer.
42	
43	use std::collections::HashMap;
44	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
45	
46	use crate::toml_simple;
47	
48	/// Per-account configuration.
49	///
50	/// - `repo_default` — `[account.<name>.repo].default` — the
51	///   category to use when `--repo` is absent.
52	/// - `repo_category` — `[account.<name>.repo.category]` — map
53	///   from category name (e.g. `"remote"`, `"local"`) to its
54	///   literal value (URL prefix, fixture parent dir, etc.).
55	#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
56	pub struct AccountConfig {
57	    pub repo_default: Option<String>,
58	    pub repo_category: HashMap<String, String>,
59	}
60	
61	/// Resolved user config.
62	///
63	/// All fields are optional or default-empty — absent file or
64	/// absent keys yield empty values. Consumers apply their own
65	/// errors at use time.
66	///
67	/// **Two write modes** for repo defaults:
68	/// - **Top-level `[repo]`** — single-account shorthand. Sits in
69	///   `top_level_repo`. Used when neither `--account` nor
70	///   `[default].account` resolves to a known account.
71	/// - **`[account.<name>]`** — multi-account. Sits in `accounts`.
72	///   Selected by `--account` CLI or `[default].account`.
73	///
74	/// Mixing both is rejected at load time (ambiguous which one
75	/// init should consult).
76	#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
77	pub struct UserConfig {
78	    /// `[default].account` — default account when `--account`
79	    /// is absent.
80	    pub default_account: Option<String>,
81	
82	    /// `[default].debug` — default value when `--debug` is used
83	    /// without an argument. (Reserved; not currently consumed.)
84	    pub default_debug: Option<String>,
85	
86	    /// Top-level `[repo]` — single-account shorthand. `Some`
87	    /// only when the file has top-level `repo.*` keys and no
88	    /// `[account.*]` sections.
89	    pub top_level_repo: Option<AccountConfig>,
90	
91	    /// Per-account configuration, keyed by account name.
92	    pub accounts: HashMap<String, AccountConfig>,
93	}
94	
95	/// CLI selector for `--repo <cat>[=<val>]`.
96	///
97	/// - `--repo` absent → `None`.
98	/// - `--repo <cat>` → `Some({ category: cat, value: None })`.
99	/// - `--repo <cat>=<val>` → `Some({ category: cat, value: Some(val) })`.
100	#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: 0.41.1-5 is the first consumer; staged ahead in -4.
101	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
102	pub struct RepoSelector {
103	    pub category: String,
104	    pub value: Option<String>,
105	}
106	
107	/// Path to the user config file.
108	///
109	/// - Honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` if set (XDG Base Directory spec).
110	/// - Falls back to `$HOME/.config`.
111	/// - Errors if neither variable is set.
112	pub fn config_path() -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
113	    let base = if let Some(xdg) = std::env::var_os("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") {
114	        PathBuf::from(xdg)
115	    } else if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME") {
116	        PathBuf::from(home).join(".config")
117	    } else {
118	        return Err("neither $XDG_CONFIG_HOME nor $HOME is set".into());
119	    };
120	    Ok(base.join("vc-x1").join("config.toml"))
121	}
122	
123	/// Load the user config from the default location.
124	///
125	/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.
126	/// - Malformed file → fatal error.
127	#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: 0.41.1-5 is the first consumer; staged ahead in -4.
128	pub fn load() -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
129	    load_from(&config_path()?)
130	}
131	
132	/// Load the user config from an explicit path.
133	///
134	/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.
135	/// - Malformed file → fatal error (propagated from `toml_simple`).
136	/// - Unknown sections / keys are silently ignored
137	///   (forward-compatible with future schema additions).
138	pub fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
139	    if !path.exists() {
140	        return Ok(UserConfig::default());
141	    }
142	    let map = toml_simple::toml_load(path)?;
143	
144	    let mut cfg = UserConfig {
145	        default_account: map.get("default.account").cloned(),
146	        default_debug: map.get("default.debug").cloned(),
147	        top_level_repo: None,
148	        accounts: HashMap::new(),
149	    };
150	
151	    let mut top_level = AccountConfig::default();
152	    let mut top_level_seen = false;
153	
154	    // Walk all keys; route `repo.*` to top-level, `account.<n>.…`
155	    // to per-account.
156	    for (full_key, value) in &map {
157	        if let Some(suffix) = full_key.strip_prefix("repo.") {
158	            top_level_seen = true;
159	            apply_repo_subkey(&mut top_level, suffix, value);
160	            continue;
161	        }
162	        let Some(rest) = full_key.strip_prefix("account.") else {
163	            continue;
164	        };
165	        let Some((name, suffix)) = rest.split_once('.') else {
166	            continue;
167	        };
168	        let Some(repo_suffix) = suffix.strip_prefix("repo.") else {
169	            continue; // unknown sub-section under [account.<n>]
170	        };
171	        let account = cfg.accounts.entry(name.to_string()).or_default();
172	        apply_repo_subkey(account, repo_suffix, value);
173	    }
174	
175	    if top_level_seen && !cfg.accounts.is_empty() {
176	        return Err(format!(
177	            "{}: mixing top-level [repo] with [account.*] is ambiguous — \
178	             remove top-level [repo] or move it under [account.<name>]",
179	            path.display()
180	        )
181	        .into());
182	    }
183	    if top_level_seen {
184	        cfg.top_level_repo = Some(top_level);
185	    }
186	
187	    Ok(cfg)
188	}
189	
190	/// Apply one `repo.*` sub-key (e.g. `default`, `category.remote`)
191	/// onto an `AccountConfig`. Used for both the top-level `[repo]`
192	/// path and the `[account.<n>.repo]` path.
193	fn apply_repo_subkey(account: &mut AccountConfig, suffix: &str, value: &str) {
194	    match suffix {
195	        "default" => {
196	            account.repo_default = Some(value.to_string());
197	        }
198	        s if let Some(cat) = s.strip_prefix("category.") => {
199	            account
200	                .repo_category
201	                .insert(cat.to_string(), value.to_string());
202	        }
203	        _ => {} // unknown sub-key; ignore (forward-compat)
204	    }
205	}
206	
207	/// Resolve `(category, value)` for an init invocation.
208	///
209	/// Three-step chain — each step has its own error message
210	/// pointing at the exact config key to set or CLI arg to pass.
211	///
212	/// - `account_override` — `Some(a)` from `--account a` CLI;
213	///   `None` falls back to `[default].account`.
214	/// - `repo_cli` — the parsed `--repo` selector (or `None` if
215	///   the flag was absent).
216	#[allow(dead_code)] // OK: 0.41.1-5 is the first consumer; staged ahead in -4.
217	pub fn resolve_repo(
218	    cfg: &UserConfig,
219	    account_override: Option<&str>,
220	    repo_cli: Option<&RepoSelector>,
221	) -> Result<(String, String), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
222	    // Step 1: pick the AccountConfig to use.
223	    //
224	    // - `--account` CLI → must hit `cfg.accounts[name]`.
225	    // - `[default].account` → must hit `cfg.accounts[that]`.
226	    // - Otherwise fall back to top-level `[repo]` (no account).
227	    // - Otherwise error.
228	    //
229	    // `account_label` is for error messages — section-name "<name>"
230	    // when an account was selected, "<top-level>" for the no-account
231	    // shorthand path.
232	    let (account, account_label) = match (account_override, &cfg.default_account) {
233	        (Some(name), _) => {
234	            let acct = cfg.accounts.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {
235	                format!("account '{name}' not found in config (no [account.{name}] section)")
236	            })?;
237	            (acct, name.to_string())
238	        }
239	        (None, Some(name)) => {
240	            let acct = cfg.accounts.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {
241	                format!(
242	                    "account '{name}' (from [default].account) not found in config \
243	                     (no [account.{name}] section)"
244	                )
245	            })?;
246	            (acct, name.clone())
247	        }
248	        (None, None) => match cfg.top_level_repo.as_ref() {
249	            Some(r) => (r, String::from("<top-level>")),
250	            None => {
251	                return Err("no account specified; set [default].account, use \
252	                     --account <name>, or write a top-level [repo] section"
253	                    .into());
254	            }
255	        },
256	    };
257	
258	    // Step 2: category.
259	    let category = match repo_cli {
260	        Some(sel) => sel.category.clone(),
261	        None => account.repo_default.clone().ok_or_else(|| {
262	            section_error(
263	                &account_label,
264	                "no default category",
265	                "repo",
266	                "default",
267	                "use --repo <cat>",
268	            )
269	        })?,
270	    };
271	
272	    // Step 3: value.
273	    let value = match repo_cli.and_then(|s| s.value.clone()) {
274	        Some(v) => v,
275	        None => account
276	            .repo_category
277	            .get(&category)
278	            .cloned()
279	            .ok_or_else(|| {
280	                section_error(
281	                    &account_label,
282	                    &format!("no value for --repo {category}"),
283	                    "repo.category",
284	                    &category,
285	                    &format!("--repo {category}=<val>"),
286	                )
287	            })?,
288	    };
289	
290	    Ok((category, value))
291	}
292	
293	/// Compose an error message for a missing-key case in `resolve_repo`.
294	///
295	/// Renders as `[account.<label>.<section_subpath>].<leaf>` for
296	/// named accounts and `[<section_subpath>].<leaf>` for the
297	/// top-level `[repo]` shorthand.
298	fn section_error(
299	    account_label: &str,
300	    msg: &str,
301	    section_subpath: &str,
302	    leaf: &str,
303	    cli_alt: &str,
304	) -> String {
305	    let section = if account_label == "<top-level>" {
306	        format!("[{section_subpath}]")
307	    } else {
308	        format!("[account.{account_label}.{section_subpath}]")
309	    };
310	    format!("{msg}; set {section}.{leaf} or use {cli_alt}")
311	}

1	//! Shared test helpers for dual-repo integration tests.
2	//!
3	//! Provides a `Fixture` that wraps `crate::init::init_with_symlink`
4	//! plus a per-process unique-tempdir helper so parallel tests don't
5	//! collide. Lifted out of the `sync` test module (originally inline at
6	//! `sync.rs:521–560`) so `push`'s tests (0.37.0) and any future
7	//! subcommand's tests can sit on the same harness without
8	//! copy-paste drift.
9	//!
10	//! Test-only — the whole module is gated at its declaration site via
11	//! `#[cfg(test)] mod test_helpers;`.
12	
13	use std::fs;
14	use std::path::PathBuf;
15	use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
16	use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
17	
18	use crate::common::write_file;
19	use crate::init::{InitArgs, init_with_symlink};
20	
21	/// Per-process counter so same-nanosecond tempdir collisions yield
22	/// distinct paths when tests run in parallel.
23	static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
24	
25	/// Build a unique tempdir path for a test fixture.
26	///
27	/// Combines a nanosecond timestamp with a per-process atomic counter
28	/// so parallel tests and same-nanosecond collisions both yield
29	/// distinct paths. Prefix is `vc-x1-test-<tag>-<ts>-<n>` so callers
30	/// from different subcommand tests stay discoverable in `$TMPDIR`.
31	pub fn unique_base(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
32	    let ts = SystemTime::now()
33	        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
34	        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
35	        .unwrap_or(0); // OK: clock error → 0 is harmless for unique tempdir naming
36	    let n = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
37	    std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("vc-x1-test-{tag}-{ts}-{n}"))
38	}
39	
40	/// Owned dual-repo fixture with RAII cleanup.
41	///
42	/// Builds a fresh throwaway workspace under a unique tempdir by
43	/// driving `init::init_with_symlink` in `--repo-local` mode with
44	/// `create_symlink=false`, exposing the two repo paths (`work` and
45	/// `work/.claude`). The tempdir tree is removed when the value is
46	/// dropped, so a panicking test still cleans up after itself.
47	pub struct Fixture {
48	    /// Root tempdir that owns both repos and their bare-git remotes.
49	    pub base: PathBuf,
50	    /// Code repo path (`<base>/work`).
51	    pub work: PathBuf,
52	    /// Bot session repo path (`<base>/work/.claude`).
53	    pub claude: PathBuf,
54	}
55	
56	impl Fixture {
57	    /// Build a fresh fixture in a unique tempdir.
58	    pub fn new(tag: &str) -> Self {
59	        Self::new_opts(tag, false, None)
60	    }
61	
62	    /// Build a fresh fixture with optional pending changes and a
63	    /// template seed.
64	    ///
65	    /// - `with_pending` — after init, write a small file into each
66	    ///   repo so `@` carries uncommitted changes (useful for
67	    ///   finalize / push tests).
68	    /// - `use_template` — `CODE[,BOT]` forwarded to init.
69	    pub fn new_opts(tag: &str, with_pending: bool, use_template: Option<String>) -> Self {
70	        let base = unique_base(tag);
71	        // init refuses to reuse an existing project_dir, so `base`
72	        // must not exist yet. `unique_base` already guarantees that.
73	        let args = InitArgs {
74	            name: Some("work".to_string()),
75	            owner: None,
76	            dir: None,
77	            private: false,
78	            dry_run: false,
79	            push_retries: 5,
80	            push_retry_delay: 3,
81	            use_template,
82	            repo_local: Some(base.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
83	            repo_remote: None,
84	            scope: None, // default → code,bot
85	        };
86	        init_with_symlink(&args, false).expect("build test fixture via init");
87	
88	        let work = base.join("work");
89	        let claude = work.join(".claude");
90	
91	        if with_pending {
92	            write_file(&work.join("TODO.md"), "# TODO\n- first feature\n")
93	                .expect("write pending TODO.md");
94	            write_file(
95	                &claude.join("session-notes.md"),
96	                "# Session notes\n- simulated pending work\n",
97	            )
98	            .expect("write pending session-notes.md");
99	        }
100	
101	        Fixture { base, work, claude }
102	    }
103	
104	    /// Convenience: return both repo paths as a `Vec<PathBuf>`
105	    /// suitable for `sync_repos` (or any other `&[PathBuf]` API).
106	    pub fn repos(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
107	        vec![self.work.clone(), self.claude.clone()]
108	    }
109	}
110	
111	impl Drop for Fixture {
112	    /// Remove the fixture tree on drop. Best-effort; a failure here
113	    /// doesn't fail the test.
114	    fn drop(&mut self) {
115	        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.base);
116	    }
117	}

1	//! Which side(s) of a workspace a command should operate on.
2	//!
3	//! - `Side` is the clap `ValueEnum` — one of `code`, `bot`.
4	//! - `Scope` wraps the parsed list; a missing flag (None at the arg
5	//!   layer) means "caller decides", typically via workspace-state
6	//!   default resolution.
7	//! - See `notes/chores-06.md > Generalize --scope across commands
8	//!   (0.40.0)` for the full rationale and the vocabulary history.
9	
10	use clap::ValueEnum;
11	
12	/// One side of the workspace.
13	///
14	/// - `Code` — the primary (app) repo.
15	/// - `Bot` — the Claude Code session repo (typically at `.claude/`).
16	#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]
17	pub enum Side {
18	    Code,
19	    Bot,
20	}
21	
22	/// Parsed `--scope` value: the set of sides the command applies to.
23	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
24	pub struct Scope(pub Vec<Side>);
25	
26	impl Scope {
27	    /// True when the scope includes the code side.
28	    pub fn has_code(&self) -> bool {
29	        self.0.contains(&Side::Code)
30	    }
31	
32	    /// True when the scope includes the bot side.
33	    pub fn has_bot(&self) -> bool {
34	        self.0.contains(&Side::Bot)
35	    }
36	
37	    /// Exactly the code side — single-repo operation.
38	    pub fn is_code_only(&self) -> bool {
39	        self.has_code() && !self.has_bot()
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Exactly the bot side — single-repo operation on the bot.
43	    pub fn is_bot_only(&self) -> bool {
44	        !self.has_code() && self.has_bot()
45	    }
46	
47	    /// Both sides — dual-repo operation.
48	    pub fn is_both(&self) -> bool {
49	        self.has_code() && self.has_bot()
50	    }
51	
52	    /// Neither side — empty scope, always an invalid input.
53	    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
54	        self.0.is_empty()
55	    }
56	}
57	
58	#[cfg(test)]
59	mod tests {
60	    use super::*;
61	
62	    #[test]
63	    fn code_only() {
64	        let s = Scope(vec![Side::Code]);
65	        assert!(s.is_code_only());
66	        assert!(!s.is_bot_only());
67	        assert!(!s.is_both());
68	    }
69	
70	    #[test]
71	    fn bot_only() {
72	        let s = Scope(vec![Side::Bot]);
73	        assert!(!s.is_code_only());
74	        assert!(s.is_bot_only());
75	        assert!(!s.is_both());
76	    }
77	
78	    #[test]
79	    fn both_code_then_bot() {
80	        let s = Scope(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot]);
81	        assert!(!s.is_code_only());
82	        assert!(!s.is_bot_only());
83	        assert!(s.is_both());
84	    }
85	
86	    #[test]
87	    fn both_bot_then_code() {
88	        // Order doesn't matter — contains-based checks.
89	        let s = Scope(vec![Side::Bot, Side::Code]);
90	        assert!(s.is_both());
91	    }
92	
93	    #[test]
94	    fn empty() {
95	        let s = Scope(vec![]);
96	        assert!(s.is_empty());
97	        assert!(!s.is_code_only());
98	        assert!(!s.is_bot_only());
99	        assert!(!s.is_both());
100	    }
101	}
