30	/// Banner string emitted as the first line of normal command runs
31	/// and shown at the top of subcommand `--help` output. Built from
32	/// `Cargo.toml`'s name + version at compile time so it stays in
33	/// sync with the bumped version.
34	const BANNER: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"), " ", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
35	
36	/// Top-level about line — name, version, and the project tagline
37	/// on a single line. Used as the top-level `about` so `vc-x1 -h`
38	/// reads as one banner-plus-tagline header instead of two stacked
39	/// lines.
40	const TOP_ABOUT: &str = concat!(
41	    env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"),
42	    " ",
43	    env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
44	    " - jj workspace tooling"
45	);
46	
47	/// Build the clap command tree with `BANNER` set as `before_help`
48	/// on every subcommand (transitively). Top-level skips `before_help`
49	/// because its own `about` already carries the name+version+tagline.
50	/// Walks via `mut_subcommand` so individual subcommand
51	/// `#[command(long_about = ...)]` blocks don't have to repeat the
52	/// banner text.
53	fn cli_with_banner() -> clap::Command {
54	    fn add_to_subs(mut cmd: clap::Command) -> clap::Command {
55	        let names: Vec<String> = cmd
56	            .get_subcommands()
57	            .map(|c| c.get_name().to_string())
58	            .collect();
59	        for name in names {
60	            cmd = cmd.mut_subcommand(name, add_with_banner);
61	        }
62	        cmd
63	    }
64	    fn add_with_banner(mut cmd: clap::Command) -> clap::Command {
65	        cmd = cmd.before_help(BANNER);
66	        let names: Vec<String> = cmd
67	            .get_subcommands()
68	            .map(|c| c.get_name().to_string())
69	            .collect();
70	        for name in names {
71	            cmd = cmd.mut_subcommand(name, add_with_banner);
72	        }
73	        cmd
74	    }
75	    add_to_subs(Cli::command())
76	}
77

146	    /// Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes
147	    #[command(long_about = "Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.\n\n\
148	        Repo set is resolved (in order):\n  \
149	          - `-R` / `--repo`     exact list (back-compat / arbitrary multi-repo)\n  \
150	          - `--scope=code|bot|code,bot` dual-repo roles via `.vc-config.toml`\n  \
151	          - neither             default: `code,bot` when dual, else `code`\n\n\
152	        Default is --check (verify only) — fatal if any repo needs\n\
153	        action. Re-run with --no-check to apply (rebase / fast-forward).\n\
154	        Per repo:\n  \
155	          - up-to-date        nothing to do\n  \
156	          - behind            fast-forward bookmark to remote\n  \
157	          - ahead             nothing to sync (local has unpushed work)\n  \
158	          - diverged          rebase local onto remote; fail on conflicts\n  \
159	          - no remote         bookmark has no @<remote> counterpart; skip\n\n\
160	        Scripts and automation should pass --check or --no-check\n\
161	        explicitly — defaults can shift, explicit flags lock in the\n\
162	        contract. Interactive use can rely on the default.\n\n\
163	        After the bookmark action, `@` is rebased onto the (possibly\n\
164	        advanced) bookmark if it isn't already a descendant, so trailing\n\
165	        working-copy writes (e.g. `.claude`'s `/exit` tail) don't end up\n\
166	        orphaned on a stale branch.\n\n\
167	        On any failure, every repo is reverted to its starting state via\n\
168	        `jj op restore`. Working-copy files are preserved across the\n\
169	        revert — the operation log rewinds but disk content stays.\n\n\
170	        Output shape:\n  \
171	          - all-up-to-date: one-line summary (`sync: N repos, all bookmarks up-to-date`)\n  \
172	          - action needed (--check):  per-repo fetch + state + fatal error\n  \
173	          - action needed (--no-check): per-repo fetch + state + actions\n  \
174	          - --quiet:        no output; exit code signals success")]

185	    /// Dual-repo commit+push+finalize in one resumable command

187	        long_about = "Dual-repo commit+push+finalize in one resumable command.\n\n\
188	        Collapses today's manual Commit-Push-Finalize Flow into a\n\
189	        single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a\n\
190	        state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can\n\
191	        resume without re-doing completed stages.\n\n\
192	        Stages: preflight (fmt/clippy/test) → review (approve diff)\n\
193	        → message ($EDITOR / --title+--body, approve text) →\n\
194	        commit-app → commit-claude (skipped if clean) → bookmark-both\n\
195	        → push-app → finalize-claude. Failures in commit-app /\n\
196	        commit-claude / bookmark-both roll both repos back via\n\
197	        `jj op restore` to the snapshot recorded before commit-app.\n\
198	        After push-app succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and\n\
199	        recovery is forward-only.\n\n\
200	        Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes\n\
201	        to skip the review gate. Saved state carries title/body\n\
202	        across resumes so only the first invocation needs them."

207	fn run_command(result: Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>) -> ExitCode {
208	    match result {
209	        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
210	        Err(e) => {
211	            error!("{e}");
212	            ExitCode::FAILURE
213	        }
214	    }
215	}
216	
217	/// Permanent sanity check for the `main`-bookmark tracking state
218	/// in both repos of the dual-repo workspace. Prints one line on
219	/// entry and one on exit of every command. If entry and exit
220	/// differ, the executing command is the culprit; if entry differs
221	/// from the previous command's exit, something *between*
222	/// invocations broke it. Originally added in 0.37.2 as a temporary
223	/// diagnostic; promoted to permanent in 0.37.4 after the user
224	/// reported "happens more than once" — the signal is worth keeping
225	/// in place until confidence in its correctness is well-established
226	/// across varied use, at which point a "silent when clean"
227	/// refinement would remove the steady-state noise without losing
228	/// detection value (see `notes/todo.md`).
229	///
230	/// Walks up from cwd to locate the workspace root (the directory
231	/// whose `.vc-config.toml` has `path = "/"`), then probes `<root>`
232	/// and `<root>/.claude`. Same labeling whether the user runs from
233	/// the app root, from `.claude`, or from any subdir.
234	fn bm_track(phase: &str, command_name: &str) {
235	    let header = format!("bm-track {phase} vc-x1 {command_name}");
236	    let root = match common::find_workspace_root() {
237	        Some(r) => r,
238	        None => {
239	            log::info!("{header}: no-workspace");
240	            return;
241	        }
242	    };
243	    let repos: [(std::path::PathBuf, &str); 2] =
244	        [(root.clone(), "app"), (root.join(".claude"), ".claude")];
245	    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
246	    for (repo, label) in repos {
247	        if !repo.join(".jj").exists() {
248	            parts.push(format!("{label}(main)=no-jj"));
249	            continue;
250	        }
251	        match bm_track_one(&repo, "main", "origin") {
252	            Ok(true) => parts.push(format!("{label}(main)=tracked")),
253	            Ok(false) => parts.push(format!("{label}(main)=NOT_TRACKED")),
254	            Err(e) => parts.push(format!(
255	                "{label}(main)=err({})",
256	                e.lines().next().unwrap_or("")
257	            )),
258	        }
259	    }
260	    log::info!("{header}: {}", parts.join(", "));
261	}
262	
263	/// Query jj for whether `bookmark` in `repo` is tracking `remote`.
264	/// Returns `Ok(true)` if the tracked-list entry for `bookmark` shows
265	/// an `@<remote>` line (in any form — `@origin:` when synced, or
266	/// `@origin (ahead by N commits):` / similar when divergent — both
267	/// still count as tracking). `Ok(false)` when no such line exists
268	/// (bookmark isn't tracking this remote or doesn't exist). `Err` on
269	/// subprocess failure.
270	fn bm_track_one(repo: &Path, bookmark: &str, remote: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
271	    let repo_str = repo.to_string_lossy();
272	    let output = std::process::Command::new("jj")
273	        .args(["bookmark", "list", "--tracked", bookmark, "-R", &repo_str])
274	        .output()
275	        .map_err(|e| format!("spawn: {e}"))?;
276	    if !output.status.success() {
277	        return Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string());
278	    }
279	    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
280	    // Accept both the synced form (`@origin:`) and the decorated
281	    // divergent form (`@origin (ahead by N commits):`), which still
282	    // represents a tracking relationship.
283	    let colon = format!("@{remote}:");
284	    let paren = format!("@{remote} ");
285	    Ok(stdout.lines().any(|l| {
286	        let t = l.trim_start();
287	        t.starts_with(&colon) || t.starts_with(&paren)
288	    }))
289	}
290	
291	fn main() -> ExitCode {
292	    CompleteEnv::with_factory(cli_with_banner).complete();
293	    let matches = cli_with_banner().get_matches();
294	    let cli = match Cli::from_arg_matches(&matches) {
295	        Ok(cli) => cli,
296	        Err(e) => {
297	            e.exit();
298	        }
299	    };
300	
301	    let log_path = cli.log.as_ref().map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().to_string());
302	    logging::CliLogger::init(cli.verbose, log_path.as_deref());
303	
304	    // The detached `finalize --exec` re-entry is the bot's
305	    // session-end child; it shouldn't print the banner (extra
306	    // chatter in its log) or surface user-facing failure markers
307	    // (those are meant for the user's next interactive run).
308	    let is_detached_exec = matches!(
309	        cli.command,
310	        Commands::Finalize(ref f) if f.exec
311	    );
312	
313	    // `-L` / `--no-label` on the read-only multi-repo subcommands
314	    // (chid, desc, list, show) makes their output script-parseable
315	    // — adding a leading `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` line would break that. Skip
316	    // the banner whenever the active subcommand has the flag set.
317	    let suppress_banner = match &cli.command {
318	        Commands::Chid(a) => a.common.no_label,
319	        Commands::Desc(a) => a.common.no_label,
320	        Commands::List(a) => a.common.no_label,
321	        Commands::Show(a) => a.common.no_label,
322	        _ => false,
323	    };
324	
325	    if !is_detached_exec {
326	        if !suppress_banner {
327	            // Banner on every normal run, mirroring what `--help`
328	            // shows at the top.
329	            log::info!("{BANNER}");
330	        }
331	        finalize::surface_previous_failures();
332	    }
333	
334	    // Command name for bm-track output (first positional arg after
335	    // the binary; clap has already validated it by the time we get here).
336	    let command_name = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".to_string()); // OK: default when somehow invoked without a subcommand
337	
338	    if !is_detached_exec {
339	        bm_track("enter", &command_name);
340	    }
341	
342	    let exit_code = match cli.command {
343	        Commands::Chid(chid_args) => run_command(chid::chid(&chid_args)),
344	        Commands::Desc(desc_args) => run_command(desc::desc(&desc_args)),
345	        Commands::List(list_args) => run_command(list::list(&list_args)),
346	        Commands::Show(show_args) => run_command(show::show(&show_args)),
347	        Commands::ValidateDesc(validate_desc_args) => {
348	            run_command(validate_desc::validate_desc(&validate_desc_args))
349	        }
350	        Commands::FixDesc(fix_desc_args) => run_command(fix_desc::fix_desc(&fix_desc_args)),
351	        Commands::Clone(clone_args) => run_command(clone::clone_repo(&clone_args)),
352	        Commands::Init(init_args) => run_command(init::init(&init_args)),
353	        Commands::Symlink(symlink_args) => run_command(symlink::symlink(&symlink_args)),
354	        Commands::Sync(sync_args) => run_command(sync::sync(&sync_args)),
355	        Commands::Finalize(finalize_args) => {
356	            let opts = match finalize_args.into_opts(cli.log) {
357	                Ok(opts) => opts,
358	                Err(e) => {
359	                    error!("{e}");
360	                    return ExitCode::FAILURE;
361	                }
362	            };
363	            run_command(finalize::finalize(&opts))
364	        }
365	        Commands::Push(push_args) => run_command(push::push(&push_args)),
366	    };
367	
368	    if !is_detached_exec {
369	        bm_track("exit ", &command_name);
370	    }
371	
372	    exit_code
373	}

285	### User config (0.41.1-3, redesigned in 0.41.1-4)
286	
287	User-global config at `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`
288	(XDG-compliant; honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Backs init's
289	account- and repo-target resolution. No magic fallbacks:
290	missing file or missing key → predictable error pointing
291	at the exact key to set.
292	
293	`-3` shipped a flat first-cut schema (`[default]
294	repo-remote-provider`, `[github] owner`); `-4` replaces it
295	with the account/category structure below before init
296	becomes the first consumer in `-5`. Since `-3` had no
297	consumers, the rewrite is non-breaking.
298	
299	Schema:
300	
301	```toml
302	[default]
303	account = "home"      # default --account when absent
304	debug   = "trace"     # default --debug value when used without arg
305	
306	[account.home]
307	repo.default          = "remote"                       # default --repo cat when absent
308	repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"   # value for --repo remote (no =val)
309	repo.category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"              # value for --repo local (no =val)
310	
311	[account.work]
312	repo.default          = "remote"
313	repo.category.remote  = "git@github.com:anthropic"
314	repo.category.local   = "/work/fixtures"
315	```
316	
317	Three layers — each level has its own default-finding key:
318	
319	| CLI                       | Step 1: account                | Step 2: category                  | Step 3: value                                    |
320	|---|---|---|---|
321	| (no `--repo`/`--account`) | `[default].account`            | `[account.<a>.repo].default`      | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |
322	| `--account <a>`           | `<a>` (CLI)                    | `[account.<a>.repo].default`      | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |
323	| `--repo <cat>`            | `[default].account` (or CLI)   | `<cat>` (CLI)                     | `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`              |
324	| `--repo <cat>=<val>`      | `[default].account` (or CLI)   | `<cat>` (CLI)                     | `<val>` (CLI, literal)                           |
325	
326	Values are **literal targets**, not section-name
327	pointers. For `category = "remote"`, the value is a URL
328	prefix (init appends `/<NAME>.git`); for `category =
329	"local"`, it's the parent dir for fixture bares. Built-in
330	categories `remote` and `local` are recognized; any other
331	category name errors in `-5` (forward-compat: future
332	cycles can add a `kind` field for user-defined categories).
333	
334	Resolution errors (each step has its own message):
335	
336	- Step 1 missing → `no account specified; set [default].account, use --account <name>, or write a top-level [repo] section`.
337	- Step 2 missing → `no default category for account '<a>'; set [account.<a>.repo].default or use --repo <cat>`.
338	- Step 3 missing → `no value for --repo <cat> in account '<a>'; set [account.<a>.repo.category].<cat> or use --repo <cat>=<val>`.
339	
340	#### Single-account shorthand: top-level `[repo]`
341	
342	`[account.<name>]` boilerplate is overhead when there's
343	only one account. The loader accepts a top-level `[repo]`
344	section as a single-account shorthand:
345	
346	```toml
347	[repo]
348	default          = "remote"
349	category.remote  = "git@github.com:winksaville"
350	category.local   = "~/test-fixtures"
351	```
352	
353	3-4 lines for a complete config — no `[default].account`,
354	no `[account.<name>]`. Resolution: when no `--account` is
355	given and no `[default].account` is set, the loader uses
356	the top-level `[repo]` block as the implicit account.
357	
358	Mixing top-level `[repo]` **and** `[account.*]` sections
359	is rejected at load time (ambiguous which one init should
360	consult — error: `mixing top-level [repo] with [account.*]
361	is ambiguous`).
362	
363	Top-level error format uses `[repo.category].<cat>` rather
364	than `[account.<a>.repo.category].<cat>`.
365	
366	Per-workspace `.vc-config.toml` override (ancestor walk)
367	is deferred — chicken-and-egg at init time, and the
368	global file covers the dominant use case.
369	
370	Module shape:
371	
372	- `pub struct UserConfig { default_account, default_debug, top_level_repo: Option<AccountConfig>, accounts: HashMap<String, AccountConfig> }`.
373	- `pub struct AccountConfig { repo_default, repo_category: HashMap<String, String> }`.
374	- `pub struct RepoSelector { category, value: Option<String> }` — parsed `--repo` form.
375	- `load()` / `load_from(path)` — load + group dotted keys.
376	- `resolve_repo(cfg, account_override, repo_cli) -> (cat, value)` — three-step chain.
377	
378	`-4` lands the rewritten module standalone; `-5` (init
379	reshape) is the first consumer.
380	
381	#### Refactoring opportunities (post-0.41.1)
382	
383	Two cleanups surfaced while sizing the module that we
384	deliberately deferred to keep `-3` scoped:
385	
386	- **Unify `.vc-config.toml` accessors onto Pattern B.**
387	  The tree has two patterns for reading TOML config:
388	  - Pattern A (`desc_helpers.rs`, `fix_desc.rs`,
389	    `validate_desc.rs`): call site does
390	    `toml_simple::toml_load(path)` and passes the
391	    resulting `HashMap<String, String>` to map-typed
392	    accessor fns (`other_repo_from_config(&map)`,
393	    `ochid_prefix_from_config(&map)`).
394	  - Pattern B (`push::resolve_state_layout`, new
395	    `config::load_from`): function takes a path,
396	    returns a typed struct with the fields it cares
397	    about; conversion baked in.
398	  Pattern B is more discoverable and testable. A
399	  `WorkspaceConfig` struct with `load_from(path)` could
400	  replace the Pattern-A helpers across desc_helpers /
401	  fix_desc / validate_desc. ~50 LOC, mechanical.
402	- **Layered config precedence** — once `WorkspaceConfig`
403	  is typed, layering user → workspace → CLI becomes
404	  natural (workspace can override `[github].owner` for a
405	  specific project). Init can't use this layer because
406	  it runs *before* a workspace exists, but post-init
407	  commands could.
408	
409	Both candidates for the 0.41.2 cycle. See `notes/todo.md`.
410	
411	### Decisions made during design
412

16	## init + clone redesign (0.41.1)
17	
18	Empirical validation 2026-04-27 against `vc-x1 0.42.0-3` (see
19	[`vc-x1-init.md`](vc-x1-init.md)) surfaced cosmetic anomalies
20	and a substantive design gap. Init's flag surface
21	(`--repo-local`, `--repo-remote`, `--owner`, `--dir`,
22	`[NAME]`) carries 6+ mutually-exclusive preflight checks just
23	to prevent impossible combinations from being typed. Clone
24	already implements a unified-positional alternative (URL /
25	`owner/name` shorthand); this cycle extends that pattern to
26	init, adds POR support to both, and unifies their CLI
27	surfaces.
28	
29	Branched off `6747a27` (0.41.0 close-out). On close-out, the
30	in-flight 0.42.0 work on `main` rebases on top.
31	
32	### Command structure
33	
34	```
35	vc-x1 init  <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por] [--account <a>] [--repo <cat>[=<val>]] [--private] [--dry-run]
36	vc-x1 clone <TARGET> [NAME] [--scope code,bot|por]                                                    [--dry-run]
37	```
38	
39	Init carries `--account`, `--repo`, and `--private`;
40	clone has none of them. Clone's TARGET is the source
41	(URL/path); init's TARGET is the workspace name/path
42	combined with config-resolved remote.
43	
44	`<TARGET>` accepts:
45	
46	- **URL** — `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`,
47	  `https://...(.git)?` (detected by `://` or SSH
48	  `<host>:<path>` shape with `@`).
49	- **`owner/name` shorthand** — single `/`, no path prefix;
50	  resolved to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
51	- **Path-prefixed** — `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`,
52	  bare `.`, or bare `..`. Path IS the target; last component
53	  is the workspace name (consumer canonicalizes `.` / `..`
54	  to a real basename via `canonicalize` + `file_name`).
55	- **Bare alphanumeric NAME** — for **init** only, becomes
56	  the workspace name; the remote URL is resolved via the
57	  user config's `--repo` chain
58	  ([`User config`](#user-config-0411-3-redesigned-in-0411-4)).
59	  Missing required config keys produce the
60	  step-specific errors documented there. For **clone**,
61	  bare NAME is an error (genuinely ambiguous — "missing
62	  `./`?" / "missing `/name` suffix?"); clone has no
63	  config-driven defaults.
64	
65	`[NAME]`:
66	
67	- **init**: URL / `owner/name` forms → overrides the derived
68	  workspace name (workspace at `cwd/<NAME>`). Path forms →
69	  error if combined (path already specifies the destination).
70	- **clone**: all forms (URL, `owner/name`, Path-as-source) →
71	  destination dir name in cwd. Without `[NAME]`, derived
72	  from the source via `derive_name`. For clone, TARGET is
73	  the *source* (URL or local repo path) and `[NAME]` is
74	  the *destination* — symmetric with `git clone <src>
75	  [<dest>]`.
76	
77	`--scope`:
78	
79	- `code,bot` (default): both repos, dual-repo layout.
80	- `por`: single repo, no `.vc-config.toml` written.
81	- `code` / `bot` standalone: error. Reason — these are
82	  config-lookup keywords; init has no config to look up
83	  against, and clone's simplification omits them too. The
84	  manual decomposition (clone code as POR, clone bot as
85	  POR, place at `.claude/`, run `vc-x1 symlink`) covers the
86	  rare cases where a user wants the dual layout composed
87	  by hand.
88	
89	`--private`: only meaningful for init when creating a new
90	GitHub repo. Sets visibility at `gh repo create`. Silently
91	warn-and-ignore if the remote already exists. Errors on
92	clone (clone never creates a remote).
93	
94	`--account <name>` (init only): override
95	`[default].account`. Determines which `[account.<name>]`
96	section is consulted for `--repo` resolution.
97	
98	`--repo <cat>[=<val>]` (init only): pick the repo target
99	for this run.
100	- `--repo` absent → use account's `repo.default` →
101	  category's value.
102	- `--repo <cat>` → use `<cat>`'s configured value.
103	- `--repo <cat>=<val>` → use literal `<val>`.
104	
105	Built-in categories: `remote` (value is a URL prefix —
106	init appends `/<NAME>.git`) and `local` (value is the
107	parent dir for fixture bare repos at
108	`<parent>/remote-{code,claude}.git`). Replaces the old
109	`--owner` / `--repo-local` / `--repo-remote` /
110	`--fixture` flag set with one unified mechanism.
111	
112	`--dry-run`: validate the operation as far as possible
113	without side effects. Print what would be done.
114	
115	### Operations
116	
117	**Init** is *smart* — it detects the target dir's state and
118	chooses the right operation.
119	
120	| Target state | `--scope=code,bot` | `--scope=por` |
121	|---|---|---|
122	| empty / nonexistent | create dual-repo from scratch | create POR |
123	| POR (jj+git, no config) | upgrade to dual | error (already POR) |
124	| POR (git only, no `.jj/`) | bootstrap `jj git init`, then upgrade | error (already POR-shape) |
125	| code POR + `.claude/` peer POR (configs missing) | write configs only | error |
126	| dual-repo (configs present) | error (already there) | error (downgrade) |
127	| single-repo (illegal shape) | error | error |
128	| anything else (random files, etc.) | error with diagnostic | error with diagnostic |
129	
130	**Clone** is *dumb* — it just clones sources (URLs or local
131	repo paths) into target dirs.
132	
133	| `--scope=por` | clone the source into `<target_dir>` |
134	| `--scope=code,bot` | clone code source into `<target_dir>`; derive bot source (`<source>.claude`); clone into `<target_dir>/.claude/`; create symlink via `vc-x1 symlink` |
135	
136	For both clone modes: `<target_dir>` must NOT exist
137	(`vc-x1 clone` errors if anything is there). Use
138	`vc-x1 sync` to update an existing checkout.
139	
140	Path-form for clone is symmetric with `git clone /local/bare.git`
141	— useful for local fixtures, CI scratch dirs, integration
142	tests against bare repos. Init/clone differ on what TARGET
143	*means* (init: destination; clone: source) but share the
144	same `parse_target` acceptance set.
145	
146	`.vc-config.toml` files for the dual-repo case are *tracked
147	content in the remotes*, not files clone writes. They ride
148	along with the clone. If a remote doesn't have them
149	committed, `vc-x1 init <path> --scope=code,bot` from inside
150	the cloned dir handles the config-only upgrade case (see
151	init's state table above).
152	
153	`--scope=code,bot` is implemented as in-process composition
154	of the `--scope=por` primitive (called twice: once for code
155	URL, once for derived bot URL) plus a `symlink::create`
156	call. No subprocess overhead.
157	
158	If init or clone fails partway through, manual cleanup is
159	required (no rollback).
160

1	# CLAUDE.md - Bot Instructions
2	
3	## Project Structure
4	
5	This project uses **two separate jj-git repos**:
6	
7	1. **App repo** (`/` — project root): Contains the application source code.
8	2. **Bot session repo** (`/.claude/`): Contains Claude Code session data.
9	
10	Both repos are managed with `jj` (Jujutsu), which coexists with git.
11	
12	## Repo Paths (relative from project root)
13	
14	- App repo: `.` (project root)
15	- Bot session repo: `.claude`
16	  (symlink from `~/.claude/projects/<path-to-project-root>/.claude`)
17	
18	## Working Directory
19	
20	Prefer staying in the project root. Use `-R` flags or absolute paths
21	to target other directories rather than `cd`. If `cd` seems necessary,
22	discuss with the user first — losing track of cwd causes subtle
23	command failures downstream.
24	
25	When invoking shell commands, prefer the shortest unambiguous path —
26	usually relative to cwd (`ls notes/`, not
27	`ls /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/notes/`). Long absolute paths
28	clutter the transcript without adding information. Out-of-workspace
29	paths (`/tmp/...`, `~/.config/...`) stay absolute. Read/Edit/Write
30	tool args also stay absolute — that's a tool-boundary constraint,
31	not a stylistic choice.
32	
33	## Memory
34	
35	Do not use the bot's per-project memory directory
36	(`~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/`). In a dual-repo setup with
37	CLAUDE.md it provides no capability CLAUDE.md doesn't already cover,
38	and it loses on discoverability:
39	
40	- **CLAUDE.md** — at the repo root, a well-known location for bot
41	  instructions, committed, reviewable, visible to every collaborator
42	  (human or bot).
43	- **Memory directory** — hidden under the user's home, tied to one
44	  machine, invisible to anyone but the bot, never diffed or reviewed.
45	
46	Easy for everyone to find beats convenient for the bot alone. Put
47	durable context in CLAUDE.md (or committed `notes/`) instead.
48	
49	## Speculation marker
50	
51	Durable text the bot writes — CLAUDE.md, `notes/`, commit bodies,
52	chores sections — should stick to observations and direct descriptions
53	of the code or data. If a mechanism, hypothesis, or causal claim
54	enters the text, prefix it with "The bot thinks ..." so a reader can
55	tell the measured from the inferred.
56	
57	**Why:** unmarked speculation reads like evidence, and a future reader
58	(or the bot on a later session) can pick it up as a known fact when
59	it's not. Measured / inferred is a distinction worth keeping visible
60	in the written record.
61	
62	**How to apply:** observations and factual descriptions need no
63	marker. Prefix with "The bot thinks ..." (or a close variant like
64	"The bot's guess is ...") when the claim is a mechanism ("X wins
65	because Y caches better"), a cause ("the drift was due to thermal
66	state"), a prediction ("this should scale linearly"), or any
67	reasoning not directly supported by the data on hand.
68	
69	## Committing
70	
71	Use `-R` (`--repository`) at the end to target the correct repo. Use
72	relative paths to reduce noise. Putting `-R` last keeps the verb/action
73	visible at the start of the command.
74	
75	### App repo
76	```
77	jj commit -m \
78	"title" \
79	-m "body
80	
81	ochid: /.claude/<changeID>" \
82	-R .
83	```
84	
85	### Bot session repo
86	```
87	jj commit -m \
88	"title" \
89	-m "body
90	
91	ochid: /<changeID>" \
92	-R .claude
93	```
94	
95	## jj Basics
96	
97	- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R .claude` — show working copy status
98	- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R .claude` — show commit log
99	- `jj commit -m "title" -m "body" -R <repo>` — finalize working copy into a commit
100	- `jj describe -m "title" -m "body" -R <repo>` — set description without committing
```

200	   `notes/todo.md` and `notes/chores-*.md` — this is the "done"
201	   marker.
202	
203	Multi-step cycles surface the ladder at the top of
204	`notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` as a bullet list with `(done)` /
205	`(current)` markers — see the file's intro paragraph for the
206	format. When starting a new step, the *first* edit is to mark
207	that step `(current)` in `notes/todo.md` — before any code/doc
208	work — so the In Progress view reflects what's actually
209	happening. The flip back to `(done)` is part of the pre-commit
210	checklist (item 6).
211	
212	**Why numeric suffixes (`-0`, `-1`, …) rather than `-devN`:**
213	semver pre-release identifiers may consist of a single numeric
214	component, and they compare numerically per spec. So
215	`X.Y.Z-1 < X.Y.Z-2 < … < X.Y.Z` correctly orders the dev ladder
216	below the done marker. Cargo accepts this form. The `-dev` prefix
217	adds no information the git log doesn't already convey and
218	doubles typing per commit.
219	
220	The final release commit (no suffix) signals completion rather than
221	amending prior commits. This keeps history readable and makes it easy
222	to see which commits were exploratory vs final.
223	
224	### Chores section headers
225	
226	Chores section headers use trailing version format:
227	
228	```
229	## Description (X.Y.Z)
230	```
231	
232	Example: `` ## Add `fn claude-symlink` (0.27.0) ``
233	
234	### Pre-commit checklist
235	
236	Before proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:
237	
238	1. `cargo fmt`
239	2. `cargo clippy`
240	3. `cargo test`
241	4. `cargo install --path . --locked` (if applicable) — `--locked`
242	   is required: without it, `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock`
243	   and re-resolves from scratch, which can pick incompatible
244	   versions even when `cargo build` / `cargo test` succeed.
245	5. Retest after install
246	6. Update `notes/todo.md` — for multi-step cycles, flip the
247	   just-completed step's marker from `(current)` to `(done)`
248	   **before** running `vc-x1 push`. The commit being pushed
249	   should reflect the new state. (The next step's `(current)`
250	   marker is set later, at the *start* of that step — see the
251	   Versioning multi-step section.)
252	7. Update `notes/todo.md` — at cycle close-out (final commit),
253	   move the entry from `## In Progress` to `## Done`.
254	8. Update `notes/chores-*.md` — add a subsection describing the change
255	9. Update `notes/README.md` — if functionality changed (new flags,
256	   new subcommands, changed behavior)
257	
258	## Code Conventions
259	
260	### Doc comments on every file, function, and method
261	
262	Every `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every
263	function and method must have a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief —
264	one sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline is that the
265	comment exists, not that it be long.
266	
267	This is a deliberate override of the generic "write no comments"
268	default that applies to inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the
269	module / item surface are expected; inline explanatory comments
270	inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a
271	non-obvious WHY.
272	
273	**Shape:** short intro (1–3 sentences, shorter is better), then
274	a `-` bullet list for any structured details. Avoid long prose
275	paragraphs — they read as a wall of text and hide the structure
276	that bullets make scannable. Same shape applies to:
277	
278	- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files.
279	- Chore descriptions in `notes/chores-NN.md`.
280	- Todo entries in `notes/todo.md` (when an item needs more than
281	  one line of detail; pure one-liners are still fine).
282	
283	**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive
284	`--help` output. Clap reflows by default and collapses bullets
285	into running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on
286	any field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- …` lands on
287	its own line in the rendered help.
288	
289	### `// OK: …` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)
290	
291	Non-test code that calls `.unwrap()`, `.unwrap_or(…)`,
292	`.unwrap_or_default()`, or `.unwrap_or_else(…)` must have a trailing
293	`// OK: …` comment that justifies why the call is acceptable.
294	
295	- `// OK: <specific reason>` — document the real precondition,
296	  invariant, or domain reason. Preferred whenever the reason isn't
297	  self-evident.
298	- `// OK: obvious` — the default is self-evident from context (e.g.
299	  `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("")` — empty desc → empty title).
```

  "new_string": "/// Resolve `(category, value)` for an init invocation.\n///\n/// Three-step chain — each step has its own error message\n/// pointing at the exact config key to set or CLI arg to pass.\n///\n/// - `account_override` — `Some(a)` from `--account a` CLI;\n///   `None` falls back to `[default].account`.\n/// - `repo_cli` — the parsed `--repo` selector (or `None` if\n///   the flag was absent).\n///\n/// Fast path: when `repo_cli` provides both `category` and\n/// `value` (`--repo <cat>=<val>`), the result is fully\n/// determined by the CLI; no account or category lookup is\n/// needed and account-related errors are skipped. This makes\n/// config-less invocations (and test fixtures) work without a\n/// `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`.\npub fn resolve_repo(\n    cfg: &UserConfig,\n    account_override: Option<&str>,\n    repo_cli: Option<&RepoSelector>,\n) -> Result<(String, String), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    // Fast path: `--repo <cat>=<val>` is fully self-contained.\n    if let Some(sel) = repo_cli\n        && let Some(val) = sel.value.as_ref()\n    {\n        return Ok((sel.category.clone(), val.clone()));\n    }\n\n    // Step 1: pick the AccountConfig to use."
}

Default bot path is `<CODE>.claude`\n    /// (file-name concat, not path join — templates are siblings).\n    ///\n    /// - With `--scope=code`: only `CODE` is used; passing `,BOT`\n    ///   is fatal (no session side to seed).\n    /// - Non-hidden contents copied recursively; relative paths against cwd.\n    /// - Exclusive with `--repo-remote`, `--dir`, `--owner`, `--private`.\n    #[arg(long, value_name = \"PARENT\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub repo_local: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Override the `origin` URL stem (single value).\n    ///\n    /// - Session URL derived: insert `.claude` before `.git` suffix,\n    ///   or append if no `.git`.\n    /// - GitHub URLs → `gh repo create` (same as default).\n    /// - Other URLs → caller pre-creates the remote; init only pushes.\n    /// - Supports `~/…`, `$VAR`, `${VAR}` in path-shaped values.\n    /// - Exclusive with `--repo-local`, `--owner`, `--private`.\n    #[arg(long, value_name = \"URL\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub repo_remote: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Which repo(s) of the workspace to create.\n    ///\n    /// `SCOPE=code|bot|code,bot`:\n    ///\n    /// - `code` — single-repo workspace, no `.claude/` session.\n    /// - `bot` — fatal at init time (meaningless without code).\n    /// - `code,bot` (default) — dual-repo workspace.\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        value_name = \"SCOPE\",\n        value_delimiter = ',',\n        verbatim_doc_comment\n    )]\n    pub scope: Option<Vec<Side>>,\n}",

Use `por` for single-repo or `code,bot` for dual.\npub fn parse_init_scope(s: &str) -> Result<InitScope, String> {\n    match s {\n        \"code,bot\" | \"bot,code\" => Ok(InitScope::CodeBot),\n        \"por\" => Ok(InitScope::Por),\n        \"code\" | \"bot\" => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not valid for init — use 'code,bot' (dual) or 'por' (single)\"\n        )),\n        _ => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not recognized — expected 'code,bot' or 'por'\"\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse the `--repo` value into a `RepoSelector`.\n///\n/// - `<cat>` → `RepoSelector { category, value: None }`.\n/// - `<cat>=<val>` → `RepoSelector { category, value: Some(val) }`.\n/// - Empty category or empty value (after `=`) errors.\npub fn parse_repo_arg(s: &str) -> Result<RepoSelector, String> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(\"--repo: value is empty\".into());\n    }\n    match s.split_once('=') {\n        Some((cat, val)) => {\n            let cat = cat.trim();\n            let val = val.trim();\n            if cat.is_empty() {\n                return Err(format!(\"--repo: missing category in '{s}'\"));\n            }\n            if val.is_empty() {\n                return Err(format!(\"--repo: empty value in '{s}'\"));\n            }\n            Ok(RepoSelector {\n                category: cat.to_string(),\n                value: Some(val.to_string()),\n            })\n        }\n        None => Ok(RepoSelector {\n            category: s.to_string(),\n            value: None,\n        }),\n    }\n}\n\n/// CLI args for `vc-x1 init`.\n#[derive(Args, Debug)]\npub struct InitArgs {\n    /// Target — URL, owner/name shorthand, path, or bare NAME.\n    ///\n    /// - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`\n    ///   — used as-is; config not consulted.\n    /// - owner/name shorthand: resolves to\n    ///   `git@github.com:owner/name.git`; config not consulted.\n    /// - Path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..` — IS the\n    ///   workspace dest; remote resolved via `--repo` chain.\n    /// - Bare NAME: workspace at `cwd/<NAME>`; remote resolved via\n    ///   `--repo` chain.\n    #[arg(value_name = \"TARGET\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub target: String,\n\n    /// Workspace dir name override (URL / owner/name forms only).\n    ///\n    /// - URL / owner/name forms: workspace lands at `cwd/<NAME>`\n    ///   instead of the URL-derived name.\n    /// - Path / bare-NAME forms: error if given (TARGET already\n    ///   names the workspace).\n    #[arg(value_name = \"NAME\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub name: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Account name — picks `[account.<a>]` from user config.\n    ///\n    /// - Without this flag, `[default].account` (or top-level\n    ///   `[repo]` shorthand) is used.\n    /// - Meaningful only with Path or bare-NAME targets — URL /\n    ///   owner/name targets supply the remote directly.\n    #[arg(long, value_name = \"NAME\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub account: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Repo target — `<cat>` or `<cat>=<val>`.\n    ///\n    /// - Built-in categories: `remote` (URL prefix; init appends\n    ///   `/<NAME>.git`) and `local` (parent dir for fixture bare\n    ///   repos at `<parent>/remote-{code,claude}.git`).\n    /// - `--repo <cat>` looks up the value via the account chain.\n    /// - `--repo <cat>=<val>` uses the literal value, no config\n    ///   lookup needed.\n    /// - Meaningful only with Path or bare-NAME targets.\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        value_name = \"CAT[=VAL]\",\n        value_parser = parse_repo_arg,\n        verbatim_doc_comment\n    )]\n    pub repo: Option<RepoSelector>,\n\n    /// Topology — `code,bot` (dual, default) or `por` (single).\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        short,\n        value_name = \"SCOPE\",\n        value_parser = parse_init_scope,\n        default_value = \"code,bot\",\n        verbatim_doc_comment\n    )]\n    pub scope: InitScope,\n\n    /// Create private GitHub repos (default: public).\n    ///\n    /// - Only meaningful when the resolved provisioner is\n    ///   `gh repo create` (GitHub URL or `--repo remote` whose\n    ///   value points at GitHub).\n    #[arg(long, verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub private: bool,\n\n    /// Dry run — show what would be done without executing\n    #[arg(long)]\n    pub dry_run: bool,\n\n    /// Max push retries after repo creation [default: 5]\n    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 5)]\n    pub push_retries: u32,\n\n    /// Seconds between push retries [default: 3]\n    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 3)]\n    pub push_retry_delay: u64,\n\n    /// Seed repos from template directories.\n    ///\n    /// Value is `CODE[,BOT]`. Default bot path is `<CODE>.claude`\n    /// (file-name concat, not path join — templates are siblings).\n    ///\n    /// - With `--scope=por`: only `CODE` is used; passing `,BOT`\n    ///   is fatal (no session side to seed).\n    /// - Non-hidden contents copied recursively; hidden entries\n    ///   (names starting with `.`) are skipped — init writes its\n    ///   own hidden files.\n    /// - If a copied tree has a `README.md`, its first line is\n    ///   rewritten to `# <repo-name>`.\n    #[arg(long, value_name = \"CODE[,BOT]\", verbatim_doc_comment)]\n    pub use_template: Option<String>,\n}"
}

errors.\npub fn parse_repo_arg(s: &str) -> Result<RepoSelector, String> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(\"--repo: value is empty\".into());\n    }\n    match s.split_once('=') {\n        Some((cat, val)) => {\n            let cat = cat.trim();\n            let val = val.trim();\n            if cat.is_empty() {\n                return Err(format!(\"--repo: value: None,\n        }),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ---------- parse_topology ----------\n\n    #[test]\n    fn topology_code_bot() {\n repo_arg_category_only() {\n        let sel = parse_repo_arg(\"remote\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(sel.category, \"remote\");\n        assert_eq!(sel.value, None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn repo_arg_category_and_value() {\n        let sel = parse_repo_arg(\"local=/tmp/fixtures\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(sel.category, \"local\");\n        assert_eq!(sel.value.as_deref(), Some(\"/tmp/fixtures\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn repo_arg_trims_whitespace() {\n        let sel = parse_repo_arg(\"  remote = git@github.com:foo  \").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(sel.category, Use `por` for single-repo or `code,bot` for dual.\npub fn parse_init_scope(s: &str) -> Result<InitScope, String> {\n    match s {\n        \"code,bot\" | \"bot,code\" => Ok(InitScope::CodeBot),\n        \"por\" => Ok(InitScope::Por),\n        \"code\" | \"bot\" => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not valid for init — use 'code,bot' (dual) or 'por' (single)\"\n        )),\n        _ => Err(format!(\n            \"'--scope={s}' is not recognized — expected 'code,bot' or 'por'\"\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse the `--repo` value into a `RepoSelector`.\n///\n/// - `<cat>` → `RepoSelector { category, value: None }`.\n/// - `<cat>=<val>` → `RepoSelector { category, value: Some(val) }`.\n/// - Empty category or empty value (after `=`) errors.\npub fn parse_repo_arg(s: &str) -> Result<RepoSelector, String> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(\"--repo: value is empty\".into());\n    }\n    match s.split_once('=') {\n        Some((cat, val)) => {\n            let cat = cat.trim();\n            let val = val.trim();\n            if cat.is_empty() {\n                return Err(format!(\"--repo: missing category in '{s}'\"));\n            }\n            if val.is_empty() {\n                return Err(format!(\"--repo: empty value in '{s}'\"));\n            }\n            Ok(RepoSelector {\n                category: cat.to_string(),\n                value: Some(val.to_string()),\n            })\n        }\n        None => Ok(RepoSelector {\n            category: s.to_string(),\n            value: None,\n        }),\n    }\n}\n\n/// CLI args for `vc-x1 init`.",

Both fair.

**"workspace":** agreed, I let it creep in. Looking at what I wrote, the natural replacements are:
- "workspace topology" → "scope kind"
- "workspace dir / dest" → "destination" or "destination dir"
- "workspace at `cwd/<NAME>`" → just "at `cwd/<NAME>`" (context already implies what's being created)
- "TARGET already names the workspace" → "TARGET already names the destination"

The vocabulary you've been using (repo / dual-repo / POR) names what's being created; "destination" / "dest" names where it goes. That covers everything I had "workspace" for. Sound right, or do you have a preferred replacement when the sentence really wants to name the whole set-of-repos thing as a unit?

**"topology":** you're right — the enum is the typed value of `--scope`, and the value happens to *describe* a topology rather than *be* one. The name should reflect what the type is, not what the value describes.

Three candidates:
- **`ScopeKind`** — most Rust-idiomatic (mirrors `io::ErrorKind`, `path::Component`, etc.). Reads as "the kind of value `--scope` accepts." My lean.
- **`ScopeValue`** — your suggestion, slightly more direct ("the value of --scope") but a bit generic.
- **`RepoShape`** — uses your word "shape", names the result. Good but redirects from "this is a `--scope` value" to "this is what you get."

`ScopeKind` and `ScopeValue` both keep the name tied to the option; `RepoShape` slides toward the result. Mild preference for `ScopeKind` on idiom alone, but I'd take any of the three over `Topology`.

There's also the existing `scope.rs` containing `Scope(Vec<Side>)` (the runtime value used in `InitPlan`) — that one's a separate concept (sides operated on, not topology choice). They could merge in the 0.42.0 sum-type cycle, but for now they're distinct, and that's fine.

1	//! Parsing and derivation helpers for repository URLs and targets.
2	//!
3	//! Single source of truth for the positional shapes that `init` and
4	//! `clone` accept (URL, owner/name shorthand, path) and for the
5	//! URL-derivation helpers shared between them.
6	//!
7	//! Lifted from `clone.rs` / `init.rs` in 0.41.1-1; consumers
8	//! migrate to `parse_target` in 0.41.1-2 (clone) and 0.41.1-3
9	//! (init).
10	
11	use std::path::PathBuf;
12	
13	/// A parsed positional `<TARGET>` argument to `init` or `clone`.
14	///
15	/// - `Url` — full git URL (`scheme://...` or SSH `user@host:path`).
16	/// - `OwnerName(owner, name)` — `owner/name` shorthand;
17	///   resolves to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
18	/// - `Path` — local path with explicit prefix
19	///   (`./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, or bare `~`). Path text is preserved
20	///   literally; tilde expansion is the consumer's responsibility.
21	/// - `BareName` — a bare alphanumeric (no `/`, `:`, or path
22	///   prefix). Init resolves it via the user-config remote chain;
23	///   clone errors on it (no config-driven default).
24	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Clone)]
25	pub enum Target {
26	    Url(String),
27	    OwnerName(String, String),
28	    Path(PathBuf),
29	    BareName(String),
30	}
31	
32	/// Parse a positional `<TARGET>` argument into one of the four
33	/// shapes.
34	///
35	/// Detection order (path forms first, then URL, then shorthand,
36	/// then bare NAME):
37	///
38	/// - Path forms: bare `.`, `..`, or `~`; or starts with `./`,
39	///   `../`, `/`, or `~/`. `.` and `..` are POSIX cwd/parent and
40	///   are unambiguous; the consumer resolves them to a real
41	///   workspace name via `canonicalize` + `file_name`.
42	/// - URL: contains `://`, or SSH-style `user@host:path` (an `@`
43	///   followed somewhere by `:`).
44	/// - `owner/name` shorthand: exactly one `/`, both sides non-empty,
45	///   no path or URL indicators.
46	/// - Bare NAME: no `/`, no `:`, no URL/path indicators. Init
47	///   resolves it via the user-config remote chain (workspace
48	///   lands at `cwd/<NAME>`); clone errors on it (no config).
49	///
50	/// Errors only on empty input or syntactic garbage that fits
51	/// none of the above (e.g. `owner/name/extra`).
52	pub fn parse_target(s: &str) -> Result<Target, String> {
53	    if s.is_empty() {
54	        return Err("empty target".into());
55	    }
56	
57	    if s == "."
58	        || s == ".."
59	        || s == "~"
60	        || s.starts_with("./")

474	pub(crate) fn normalize_remote(s: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
475	    let s = s.trim();
476	    if s.is_empty() {
477	        return Err("--repo-remote: value is empty".into());
478	    }
479	    let expanded = expand_vars(s)?;
480	    if is_remote_url(&expanded) {
481	        return Ok(expanded);
482	    }
483	    let p = PathBuf::from(&expanded);
484	    if p.is_absolute() {
485	        Ok(expanded)
486	    } else {
487	        let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
488	        Ok(cwd.join(p).to_string_lossy().to_string())
489	    }
490	}
491

remote resolved\n///   from config.\n///\n/// The `cfg` parameter is the loaded user config; `init` loads it\n/// once at entry and passes it through so tests can supply a\n/// synthetic config without touching disk.\npub(crate) fn plan_init(\n    args: &InitArgs,\n    cfg: &UserConfig,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let scope = match args.scope {\n        ScopeKind::CodeBot => Scope(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot]),\n        ScopeKind::Por => Scope(vec![Side::Code]),\n    };\n\n    if scope.is_code_only()\n        && let Some(t) = &args.use_template\n        && t.contains(',')\n    {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"--scope=por takes a single template path; got '{t}' (drop the `,BOT` half)\"\n        )\n        .into());\n    }\n\n    let parsed = parse_target(&args.target)?;\n    match parsed {\n        Target::Url(url) => plan_from_url(args, scope, url),\n        Target::OwnerName(o, n) => plan_from_url(args, scope, format!(\"git@github.com:{o}/{n}.git\")),\n        Target::Path(p) => plan_from_path(args, scope, p, cfg),\n        Target::BareName(n) => plan_from_bare_name(args, scope, n, cfg),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Plan when TARGET is a URL or `owner/name` shorthand.\n///\n/// - URL is explicit; config not consulted.\n/// - `--account` / `--repo` are rejected (would have no effect).\n/// - `[NAME]` overrides the URL-derived directory name.\nfn plan_from_url(\n    args: &InitArgs,\n    scope: Scope,\n    url: String,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if args.account.is_some() {\n        return Err(\n            \"--account is meaningless with a URL or owner/name TARGET (config not consulted)\".into(),\n        );\n    }\n    if args.repo.is_some() {\n        return Err(\n            \"--repo is meaningless with a URL or owner/name TARGET (config not consulted)\".into(),\n        );\n    }\n    let code_url = ensure_git_suffix(&url);\n    let derived_name = derive_name(&code_url)?;\n    let name = args.name.clone().unwrap_or(derived_name);\n    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;\n    let project_dir = cwd.join(&name);\n\n    let provisioner = if is_github_url(&code_url) {\n        Provisioner::GhCreate\n    } else {\n        Provisioner::ExternalPreExisting\n    };\n    let gh_code_slug = if provisioner == Provisioner::GhCreate {\n        Some(github_slug_from_url(&code_url)?)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    build_plan(scope, name, project_dir, code_url, provisioner, gh_code_slug)\n}\n\n/// Plan when TARGET is a path. Path IS the destination; basename\n/// names the repo. Remote resolved via the `--repo` chain.\nfn plan_from_path(\n    args: &InitArgs,\n    scope: Scope,\n    path: PathBuf,\n    cfg: &UserConfig,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if args.name.is_some() {\n        return Err(\n            \"[NAME] is meaningless with a path TARGET (path already names the destination)\".into(),\n        );\n    }\n    let project_dir = resolve_path_target(&path)?;\n    let name = project_dir\n        .file_name()\n        .ok_or_else(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"path TARGET '{}' has no last component; cannot derive a repo name\",\n                path.display()\n            )\n        })?\n        .to_str()\n        .ok_or(\"path TARGET is not valid UTF-8\")?\n        .to_string();\n    let (cat, val) = config::resolve_repo(cfg, args.account.as_deref(), args.repo.as_ref())?;\n    plan_from_resolved(scope, name, project_dir, &cat, &val)\n}\n\n/// Plan when TARGET is a bare alphanumeric NAME. Destination at\n/// `cwd/<NAME>`; remote resolved via the `--repo` chain.\nfn plan_from_bare_name(\n    args: &InitArgs,\n    scope: Scope,\n    name: String,\n    cfg: &UserConfig,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if args.name.is_some() {\n        return Err(\n            \"[NAME] is meaningless with a bare-NAME TARGET (TARGET already names the repo)\".into(),\n        );\n    }\n    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;\n    let project_dir = cwd.join(&name);\n    let (cat, val) = config::resolve_repo(cfg, args.account.as_deref(), args.repo.as_ref())?;\n    plan_from_resolved(scope, name, project_dir, &cat, &val)\n}\n\n/// Build an `InitPlan` for a Path or BareName target after the\n/// `--repo` chain has resolved to `(category, value)`. Dispatches\n/// to `plan_remote` (URL prefix) or `plan_local` (fixture parent).\nfn plan_from_resolved(\n    scope: Scope,\n    name: String,\n    project_dir: PathBuf,\n    category: &str,\n    value: &str,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    match category {\n        \"remote\" => plan_remote(scope, name, project_dir, value),\n        \"local\" => plan_local(scope, name, project_dir, value),\n        other => Err(format!(\n            \"--repo category '{other}' is not recognized — built-ins are 'remote' and 'local'\"\n        )\n        .into()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Plan for `category = \"remote\"`: URL prefix + `/<NAME>.git`.\nfn plan_remote(\n    scope: Scope,\n    name: String,\n    project_dir: PathBuf,\n    url_prefix: &str,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let prefix = url_prefix.trim_end_matches('/');\n    let code_url = format!(\"{prefix}/{name}.git\");\n    let provisioner = if is_github_url(&code_url) {\n        Provisioner::GhCreate\n    } else {\n        Provisioner::ExternalPreExisting\n    };\n    let gh_code_slug = if provisioner == Provisioner::GhCreate {\n        Some(github_slug_from_url(&code_url)?)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    build_plan(scope, name, project_dir, code_url, provisioner, gh_code_slug)\n}\n\n/// Plan for `category = \"local\"`: bare repos under a parent dir.\n///\n/// - Dual: `<parent>/remote-code.git` + `<parent>/remote-claude.git`.\n/// - POR: `<parent>/remote.git`.\nfn plan_local(\n    scope: Scope,\n    name: String,\n    project_dir: PathBuf,\n    parent_spec: &str,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let parent = normalize_local_parent(parent_spec)?;\n\n    if scope.is_code_only() {\n        let code_bare = parent.join(\"remote.git\");\n        return Ok(InitPlan {\n            scope,\n            code_url: code_bare.to_string_lossy().to_string(),\n            code_bare_path: Some(code_bare),\n            project_dir,\n            name,\n            provisioner: Provisioner::LocalBareInit,\n            gh_code_slug: None,\n            session_dir: None,\n            session_name: None,\n            session_url: None,\n            session_bare_path: None,\n            gh_session_slug: None,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let session_dir = project_dir.join(\".claude\");\n    let code_bare = parent.join(\"remote-code.git\");\n    let session_bare = parent.join(\"remote-claude.git\");\n    let session_name = format!(\"{name}.claude\");\n    Ok(InitPlan {\n        scope,\n        code_url: code_bare.to_string_lossy().to_string(),\n        code_bare_path: Some(code_bare),\n        project_dir,\n        name,\n        provisioner: Provisioner::LocalBareInit,\n        gh_code_slug: None,\n        session_url: Some(session_bare.to_string_lossy().to_string()),\n        session_bare_path: Some(session_bare),\n        session_dir: Some(session_dir),\n        session_name: Some(session_name),\n        gh_session_slug: None,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Compose an `InitPlan` for the URL-style provisioners (`GhCreate`\n/// and `ExternalPreExisting`) — both `plan_from_url` and\n/// `plan_remote` share this tail because the only difference between\n/// them is how they construct the URL.\nfn build_plan(\n    scope: Scope,\n    name: String,\n    project_dir: PathBuf,\n    code_url: String,\n    provisioner: Provisioner,\n    gh_code_slug: Option<String>,\n) -> Result<InitPlan, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    if scope.is_code_only() {\n        return Ok(InitPlan {\n            scope,\n            project_dir,\n            name,\n            code_url,\n            provisioner,\n            code_bare_path: None,\n            gh_code_slug,\n            session_dir: None,\n            session_name: None,\n            session_url: None,\n            session_bare_path: None,\n            gh_session_slug: None,\n        });\n    }\n    let session_url = derive_session_url(&code_url);\n    let session_name = format!(\"{name}.claude\");\n    let session_dir = project_dir.join(\".claude\");\n    let gh_session_slug = if provisioner == Provisioner::GhCreate {\n        Some(github_slug_from_url(&session_url)?)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    Ok(InitPlan {\n        scope,\n        project_dir,\n        name,\n        code_url,\n        provisioner,\n        code_bare_path: None,\n        gh_code_slug,\n        session_url: Some(session_url),\n        session_name: Some(session_name),\n        session_dir: Some(session_dir),\n        session_bare_path: None,\n        gh_session_slug,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Resolve a Path target to an absolute `PathBuf`. Handles `~`,\n/// `~/X`, `$VAR`, `${VAR}` expansion; makes relative paths\n/// absolute against cwd; lexically normalizes `.` / `..`. The\n/// resulting path is **not** required to exist (init creates it).\nfn resolve_path_target(p: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let s = p.to_str().ok_or(\"path TARGET is not valid UTF-8\")?;\n    let expanded = expand_vars(s)?;\n    let pb = PathBuf::from(&expanded);\n    let abs = if pb.is_absolute() {\n        pb\n    } else {\n        std::env::current_dir()?.join(pb)\n    };\n    Ok(normalize_path(&abs))\n}\n\n/// Lexically normalize a path: collapse `.` / `..` components\n/// without touching disk. `std::fs::canonicalize` requires the\n/// path to exist, but init's destination doesn't yet.\nfn normalize_path(p: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut out: Vec<std::path::Component> = Vec::new();\n    for comp in p.components() {\n        match comp {\n            std::path::Component::ParentDir => {\n                let pop = matches!(\n                    out.last(),\n                    Some(std::path::Component::Normal(_)) | Some(std::path::Component::CurDir)\n                );\n                if pop {\n                    out.pop();\n                } else {\n                    out.push(comp);\n                }\n            }\n            std::path::Component::CurDir => {}\n            other => out.push(other),\n        }\n    }\n    out.iter().collect()\n}"
}

**Dispatch rewrite — what landed:**

- `plan_init(args, cfg)` — now takes `&UserConfig`, dispatches on `parse_target(&args.target)`:
  - `Target::Url(u)` → `plan_from_url`
  - `Target::OwnerName(o, n)` → `plan_from_url(format!("git@github.com:{o}/{n}.git"))`
  - `Target::Path(p)` → `plan_from_path` (resolves remote via config chain, basename of path = repo name)
  - `Target::BareName(n)` → `plan_from_bare_name` (destination at `cwd/<n>`)

- `plan_from_url` — explicit URL; rejects `--account` and `--repo` as meaningless ("config not consulted"). `[NAME]` overrides URL-derived dir.

- `plan_from_path` / `plan_from_bare_name` — both call `config::resolve_repo(cfg, account, repo)` then dispatch via `plan_from_resolved` to `plan_remote` (URL prefix → `<prefix>/<name>.git`) or `plan_local` (bare repos under parent dir). `[NAME]` errors on both (TARGET already names the repo/destination).

- `build_plan` — shared tail for the URL-style provisioners (`GhCreate`/`ExternalPreExisting`); deduplicates `plan_from_url` and `plan_remote`.

- `resolve_path_target` + `normalize_path` — new helpers: `~`/`$VAR` expansion + lexical `.`/`..` collapse without touching disk (init's destination doesn't exist yet, so `canonicalize` won't work).

**Dropped:** `plan_local_fixture`, `plan_external_remote`, `plan_default_github`, `normalize_remote` (unused).

**`init_with_symlink`** loads config once at entry (`config::load()?`) and passes through.

One semver gotcha to flag before you pick:

**`0.41.1-5.0` actually sorts *higher* than `0.41.1-5`, not lower.** Semver rule: longer pre-release identifier set with a matching prefix has higher precedence. So `[5] < [5, 0]` → `0.41.1-5 < 0.41.1-5.0`. Same for `0.41.1-5.a`. That inverts the project's "dev ladder below done marker" invariant from CLAUDE.md.

(Quick check: `0.41.1-5` is `[5]`, `0.41.1-5.0` is `[5, 0]`. Per spec: "A larger set of pre-release fields has a higher precedence than a smaller set, if all of the preceding identifiers are equal." So `-5.0 > -5`.)

**Options that preserve the ordering invariant:**

1. **`0.41.1-4.0`, `0.41.1-4.1`, …** — sub-ladder *between* the -4 done marker and the -5 done marker. Sorts: `-4 < -4.0 < -4.1 < … < -5`. Reads as "post-4, pre-5". Mildly unusual but principled.

2. **Don't sweat it.** The WIP gets squashed into the eventual -5 commit; ordering only matters in the durable log of done markers, and the WIP isn't durable. Use `0.41.1-5.0` if it's clearer, accept that for the WIP's lifetime it sorts above -5.

3. **Stay at `0.41.1-4` for the WIP commit, install nothing.** The version-bump-for-binary-distinction need is real *only* if you need a built binary that says it isn't -4. If you just want a commit boundary for review, no version bump needed.

My lean: **option 1 (`0.41.1-4.0`)** if you want a built-and-installed binary that reports a distinct version while preserving sort order. **Option 3** if you don't actually need a new binary right now (the dispatch isn't testable end-to-end without test rewrite anyway).

Which?

It don't matter, identifing what you're actually running is what's important, IMO. Thoughts?

  "new_string": "    pub fn new_opts(tag: &str, with_pending: bool, use_template: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        let base = unique_base(tag);\n        // init refuses to reuse an existing project_dir, so `base`\n        // must not exist yet. `unique_base` already guarantees that.\n        //\n        // Path TARGET = `<base>/work` (workspace destination); the\n        // basename (\"work\") becomes the repo name. `--repo local=<base>`\n        // sets the bare-repo parent so the layout mirrors the old\n        // `--repo-local <base>` + NAME=`work` shape:\n        //   <base>/work/                  (code repo)\n        //   <base>/work/.claude/          (bot session repo)\n        //   <base>/remote-code.git        (code bare origin)\n        //   <base>/remote-claude.git      (bot bare origin)\n        let work_path = base.join(\"work\");\n        let args = InitArgs {\n            target: work_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),\n            name: None,\n            account: None,\n            repo: Some(RepoSelector {\n                category: \"local\".to_string(),\n                value: Some(base.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),\n            }),\n            scope: ScopeKind::CodeBot,\n            private: false,\n            dry_run: false,\n            push_retries: 5,\n            push_retry_delay: 3,\n            use_template,\n        };\n        init_with_symlink(&args, false).expect(\"build test fixture via init\");"
}

> AGENT

Two things — yes to debug, and a bug your output revealed:

## Bug in your dry-run

Line 8: `gh repo create github.com:winksaville/tf1.claude --public; push to git@github.com:github.com:winksaville/tf1.claude.git`

The doubled `github.com:github.com:` is wrong. Root cause: you typed `github.com:winksaville/tf1` (no `git@` prefix), and `parse_target` misclassifies it as `OwnerName("github.com:winksaville", "tf1")` because the owner/name shorthand check doesn't reject `:`. The dispatch then wraps it: `git@github.com:{owner}/{name}.git` → `git@github.com:github.com:winksaville/tf1.git`.

Fix: tighten the owner/name shorthand in `repo_url.rs::parse_target` to reject `:` in either half. Then `github.com:winksaville/tf1` falls through to the catch-all error, which can suggest "did you mean `git@github.com:winksaville/tf1`?" if we want to be helpful.

(You probably *meant* the `git@` SSH form. Bare `host:owner/name` could be auto-promoted to SSH URL but that's a separate dwim decision worth a separate discussion.)

## Debug logging — where I'd put it

```
init() entry:
  debug!("init args: target={target:?}, name={name:?}, account={account:?},
          repo={repo:?}, scope={scope:?}")

config::load_from() success:
  debug!("config loaded from {path:?}: default_account={..}, top_level_repo={..},
          accounts={accounts}")
  debug!("config: file not found at {path:?}; using empty config")  // miss path

config::resolve_repo:
  debug!("resolve_repo: short-circuit — explicit cat={} val={}", ...)  // fast path
  debug!("resolve_repo: account selected — {} (from {})", account_label, source)
       // source: "--account CLI", "[default].account", "<top-level [repo]>"
  debug!("resolve_repo: category — {} (from {})", category, source)
  debug!("resolve_repo: value — {} (from {})", value, source)

plan_init dispatch:
  debug!("parse_target: {target} → {variant:?}")

plan_from_url:
  debug!("plan_from_url: code_url={code_url}, derived_name={derived_name},
          name={name} ({from}), provisioner={provisioner:?}")
       // from: "[NAME] override" or "URL-derived"

plan_from_path / plan_from_bare_name / plan_remote / plan_local:
  debug!("plan_*: project_dir={..}, code_url={..}, provisioner={..},
          gh_code_slug={..}, code_bare_path={..}")
```

So at `-v` (debug) you'd see the full provenance trail: which CLI flag set what, which config key supplied what, which target variant was matched, and the final plan. The `(from {})` annotation on each resolved value is the key piece — that's exactly the "what parts it's getting from where" you asked for.

Scope question: do you want the bug fix bundled into -5 (it's the same surface), or split as -6 / a separate point fix? And does the debug-logging shape above match what you want, or refine first?

Good consistency intuition. But there's a wrinkle worth surfacing first: the form `github.com:winksaville` (no `git@`) doesn't actually work cleanly in config either, just less visibly.

**What happens today with `repo.category.remote = "github.com:winksaville"` in config:**

1. `resolve_repo` returns `("remote", "github.com:winksaville")`
2. `plan_remote` builds `code_url = "github.com:winksaville/tf1.git"`
3. `is_github_url` checks for `git@github.com:` / `https://github.com/` / etc. — `github.com:winksaville/tf1.git` matches **none** → routes to `ExternalPreExisting`
4. Init expects you to have pre-created the remote, then tries `git remote add origin github.com:winksaville/tf1.git` + push — git can't resolve that as an SSH URL (no `git@`)

So your equivalence intuition is right — the two paths *should* behave the same — but the way they "agree" today is by both being broken. The chores-08 schema example uses `git@github.com:winksaville` (with the prefix) for a reason.

**The actual design question:** strict or permissive?

**A. Strict.** Require `git@github.com:owner` everywhere (config + CLI). Fix:
- `parse_target` rejects `:` in owner/name shorthand → `github.com:winksaville/tf1` falls to catch-all
- Catch-all error grows a "did you mean `git@github.com:...`?" suggestion
- Config keeps the same docs (already documents `git@` prefix)

**B. Permissive.** Auto-promote `host:owner/path` to `git@host:owner/path` everywhere. Fix:
- `parse_target` accepts SSH scp-like form without `@` (treats `host:path` as URL)
- `is_github_url` (and friends) normalize the input — strip-or-add `git@` consistently
- Apply same normalization on the config-resolved URL prefix

**My lean: A (strict).** Reasons:
- Silent URL transformation bites later — user reads config six months on and can't tell if the prefix works
- Strict → permissive is a 1-cycle expansion if patterns emerge; permissive → strict is a deprecation
- The cost of `git@` is 4 chars; the cost of debugging a doubled-up URL is much higher (you just lived this)
- A helpful error suggests the fix concretely

**B has real appeal** if "config and CLI must be string-equivalent" is a hard rule for you — that's a defensible principle and not crazy to adopt now while the surface is small.

Which way?

(For the debug-logging proposal — assume green light unless you want to refine first; I can bundle that in with whichever direction you pick.)

130	/// Load the user config from an explicit path.
131	///
132	/// - Missing file → empty `UserConfig`.
133	/// - Malformed file → fatal error (propagated from `toml_simple`).
134	/// - Unknown sections / keys are silently ignored
135	///   (forward-compatible with future schema additions).
136	pub fn load_from(path: &Path) -> Result<UserConfig, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
137	    if !path.exists() {
138	        return Ok(UserConfig::default());
139	    }
140	    let map = toml_simple::toml_load(path)?;
141	
142	    let mut cfg = UserConfig {
143	        default_account: map.get("default.account").cloned(),
144	        default_debug: map.get("default.debug").cloned(),
145	        top_level_repo: None,
146	        accounts: HashMap::new(),
147	    };
148	
149	    let mut top_level = AccountConfig::default();
150	    let mut top_level_seen = false;
151	
152	    // Walk all keys; route `repo.*` to top-level, `account.<n>.…`
153	    // to per-account.
154	    for (full_key, value) in &map {
155	        if let Some(suffix) = full_key.strip_prefix("repo.") {
156	            top_level_seen = true;
157	            apply_repo_subkey(&mut top_level, suffix, value);
158	            continue;
159	        }
160	        let Some(rest) = full_key.strip_prefix("account.") else {
161	            continue;
162	        };
163	        let Some((name, suffix)) = rest.split_once('.') else {
164	            continue;
165	        };
166	        let Some(repo_suffix) = suffix.strip_prefix("repo.") else {
167	            continue; // unknown sub-section under [account.<n>]
168	        };
169	        let account = cfg.accounts.entry(name.to_string()).or_default();
170	        apply_repo_subkey(account, repo_suffix, value);
171	    }
172	
173	    if top_level_seen && !cfg.accounts.is_empty() {
174	        return Err(format!(
175	            "{}: mixing top-level [repo] with [account.*] is ambiguous — \
176	             remove top-level [repo] or move it under [account.<name>]",
177	            path.display()
178	        )
179	        .into());
180	    }
181	    if top_level_seen {
182	        cfg.top_level_repo = Some(top_level);
183	    }
184	
185	    Ok(cfg)
186	}
187	
188	/// Apply one `repo.*` sub-key (e.g. `default`, `category.remote`)
189	/// onto an `AccountConfig`. Used for both the top-level `[repo]`
190	/// path and the `[account.<n>.repo]` path.
191	fn apply_repo_subkey(account: &mut AccountConfig, suffix: &str, value: &str) {
192	    match suffix {
193	        "default" => {
194	            account.repo_default = Some(value.to_string());
195	        }
196	        s if let Some(cat) = s.strip_prefix("category.") => {
197	            account
198	                .repo_category
199	                .insert(cat.to_string(), value.to_string());
200	        }
201	        _ => {} // unknown sub-key; ignore (forward-compat)
202	    }
203	}
204	
205	/// Resolve `(category, value)` for an init invocation.
206	///
207	/// Three-step chain — each step has its own error message
208	/// pointing at the exact config key to set or CLI arg to pass.
209	///

Proposed new subsection to insert between line 161 and `### Notes references`:

```markdown
### Per-file review checkpoints

The "review before commit block" rule applies to in-progress work
too, at finer grain. After every file edit (or every cohesive
change unit when multiple Edits to one file form a single semantic
change), STOP, summarize what changed, and wait for explicit
go-ahead before touching the next file or running follow-on
commands (cargo test/install, dogfood invocations, vc-x1 …, etc.).

**Why:** the user reviews diffs as work lands. Chaining multiple
file edits without pausing forces them to untangle cumulative
state instead of inspecting each step in isolation. Surfaces bugs
later, when undoing is more expensive.

**How to apply:**
- "continue", "go", "do it", "lg" approves *the next unit only*,
  not all remaining units of a multi-file plan. A green light to
  proceed with a *direction* is not a green light to skip
  per-step checkpoints — the two are orthogonal.
- A "unit" is one file's worth of cohesive change. Multiple Edits
  to the same file that constitute one semantic change (e.g.
  adding a function plus its tests at the same time) can land
  together; edits spanning multiple files cannot.
- After landing a unit: brief summary (2–5 lines) and stop. No
  cargo build / test / install / dogfood runs unless the user
  explicitly asks, even when those would be useful for verifying.
- This is in addition to (not a replacement for) the
  Review-before-commit-block rule above.
```

> AGENT

**`repo_url.rs` — bug fix + helpful error + 2 tests**

**Change 1: Tighten owner/name shorthand to reject `:`** (lines 81-82, two new conditions):

```rust
if s.matches('/').count() == 1
    && let Some((owner, name)) = s.split_once('/')
    && !owner.is_empty()
    && !name.is_empty()
    && !owner.contains(':')   // NEW
    && !name.contains(':')    // NEW
{
    return Ok(Target::OwnerName(owner.to_string(), name.to_string()));
}
```

This makes `github.com:winksaville/tf1` fall through to the catch-all instead of mis-classifying as `OwnerName("github.com:winksaville", "tf1")`.

**Change 2: Helpful catch-all error** (lines 93-106, new block before the generic error):

```rust
// Catch-all. If it looks like an SSH scp-like form missing the
// `git@` prefix (host:owner/name), suggest the canonical form
// — easy mistake to make and the resulting "did you mean…?"
// is concrete enough to fix with one re-type.
if let Some(colon) = s.find(':')
    && colon > 0
    && !s[..colon].contains('/')
    && s[colon + 1..].contains('/')
    && !s.contains('@')
{
    return Err(format!(
        "'{s}' is not a recognized target — looks like an SSH URL missing the 'git@' prefix; did you mean 'git@{s}'?"
    ));
}
```

Detection shape: `<host>:<path>` form — colon at non-zero index, no `/` before the colon, at least one `/` after, no `@` anywhere. The generic "expected URL, owner/name…" error stays as the final fallback for inputs that don't fit the SSH-shape pattern.

**Change 3: 2 new tests** (in `mod tests`):

```rust
#[test]
fn parse_target_host_colon_path_without_at_suggests_ssh_form() {
    let err = parse_target("github.com:winksaville/tf1").unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.contains("missing the 'git@' prefix"), "got: {err}");
    assert!(err.contains("git@github.com:winksaville/tf1"), "got: {err}");
}

#[test]
fn parse_target_owner_with_colon_rejected() {
    let err = parse_target("a:b/c").unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.contains("missing the 'git@' prefix"), "got: {err}");
}
```

First test reproduces your dogfood input; second is a minimal repro of the same family.
